a2+(135pm), Sr2+(112pm), Ca2+(99pm) or Na+ (102pm), the first possibility is the more feasible.However, due to the asymmetry in the structure, most of the Dy3+ ions enter into the lattice NaSr4 (VO4) 3 instead of NaBa4 (VO4) 3 phosphors, and few of them are located at the surface.Substitution at the Ca2+ site in NaCa4 (VO4) 3 will lead to more distortion in the host in comparison to its substitution in NaSr4 (VO4) 3 phosphor.The charge compensating defect in the immediate vicinity is likely to influence the local site symmetry.This is reflected in the emission spectra, wherein the asymmetry factor is higher in the NaSr4 (VO4) 3 sample compared to the NaCa4 (VO4) 3 and NaBa4 (VO4) 3 phosphors.As Dy3+ ions progressively replace the Sr2+ ions, an increase in PL emission intensity is observed and the asymmetry factor is progressively reduced.The low‐symmetry location of Dy3+ results in predominant emission of 4F9/2→6H15/2 transition.Hence, NaSr4 (VO4) 3 phosphors shows strong PL emission intensity compared to NaCa4 (VO4) 3 and NaBa4 (VO4) 3 phosphors when Dy is doped, as shown in Fig.8.Usually, low doping gives weak luminescence, but excess doping perhaps causes quenching of the luminescence.The maximum intensity of Dy3+ is observed at 1 mol%, as shown in Fig.7.The second possibility is more feasible.Most of the Dy3+ ions are located at the surface of NaSr4 (VO4) 3 as compared to NaBa4 (VO4) 3 and NaCa4 (VO4) 3 phosphors, and few of them enter into the lattice.Substitution at Sr2+ site in NaSr4 (VO4) 3 will lead to less distortion and induce more oxygen vacancies in the host in comparison to substitution in the NaBa4 (VO4) 3 and NaCa4 (VO4) 3 phosphors.The charge compensating defects in the immediate vicinity are likely to influence the local site symmetry of the NaSr4 (VO4) 3 host.The NaM4 (VO4) 3: Dy3+( M=Ca,., Ba, Sr) phosphor shows the characteristics of the Dy3+ ion Figure 9 shows a schematic energy level diagram of the Dy3+ ion.

Conclusion In the present study, NaM4 (VO4) 3: Dy3+( M=Ca, Ba, Sr) phosphors have been synthesized by the conventional high‐temperature solid‐state diffusion method.The PL emission spectrum has two characteristics peaks, one at 484 nm (blue) and another at 576 nm (yellow) wavelength, at the excitation wavelength of 323 nm.The excitation is 323 nm, which is an Hg‐free wavelength, and this excitation is applicable for the development of eco‐friendly lamp phosphors for solid‐state lighting.The results indicate that NaM4 (VO4) 3: Dy3+( M=Ca, Ba, Sr) phosphors could be applicable in near‐UV excited solid‐state lighting.

Short communication Multiwavelength excited white-emitting Dy3+ doped Sr3Bi (PO4) 3 phosphor Zhiping Yanga, Yufeng Liua,n, Chong Liua, FuYanga,b, Quanmao Yuc, XuLia, Fachun Lua aCollege of Physics Science and Technology, Hebei University, Baoding 071002, China bCollege of Science, Hebei North University, Zhangjiakou 075000, China cInstitute of Functional Materials, Jiangxi University of Finance & Economics, Nanchang 330013, China Received 23October 2012; received in revised form 15February 2013; Available online 20February 2013 Abstract Multiwavelength excited white emitting phosphor Dy3+ doped Sr3Bi (PO4) 3 was synthesized by solid state reaction method.The phase of the as-prepared powders was measured by X-ray diffraction pattern (XRD) and the luminescent properties of Sr3Bi (PO4) 3: Dy3+ were systematically investigated by excitation spectra, emission spectra and concentration quenching.The excitation spectra included bands located at 348 nm, 362 nm, 385 nm and 451 nm were due to the f - f transitions of Dy3+ within its 4 f configuration.This excitation is useful for solid state lighting and light-emitting diodes.Under 348 nm excitation, the emissions of Dy3+ ions are observed at 481 nm (blue) due to the 4F9/26H15/2 transitions, 575 nm (yellow) due to 4F9/2-6H13/2 transitions and a weak 664 nm (red) due to 4F9/2-6H11/2 transitions.The optimal emission intensity of the Sr3Bi1-x (PO4) 3: x Dy3+ phosphors is found to be x=0.07.The chromaticity coordinates of the samples were in the near white region.All results demonstrated that Sr3Bi (PO4) 3: Dy3+ might be a potential phosphor for NUV-based white light-emitting diodes.& 2013Elsevier Ltd and Techna Group S.r.l.All rights reserved.Keywords: A.Powders: solid-state reaction; C.Optical properties; Luminescence; Phosphors 1.

erved.Keywords: A.Powders: solid-state reaction; C.Optical properties; Luminescence; Phosphors 1.Introduction Recently, trivalent dysprosium ions (Dy3+) doped phosphors have been extensively studied due to its intense blue (484 nm, 4F9/2-6H15/2 ) and yellow (575 nm, 4F9/2-6H13/2 ) emissions and the potential applications in white light emission [1].However, the ratio of the two dominant Dy3+ emission bands arising from the transitions 4F9/2-6H15/2 (blue) and 4F9/2-6H13/2 (yellow) changes in different hosts, because the yellow emission is strongly influenced by the chemical environment surrounding Dy3+ due to J=2 (4F9/2-6H13/2) while the blue emission (4F9/2-6H15/2) is relatively invariable.Therefore, the color tone of Dy3+.doped phosphors can be modified by changing the relative intensity of the yellow light through the crystal field.At present, there are many hosts that can be activated by Dy3+, such as borates [2–4], phosphates [5–8], aluminates [9,10], silicates [11–13], vanadates [14–16], molybdates [1], etc.Among these hosts, phosphates are good candidates due to their low synthetic temperatures, stabilities, and low costs.As a member of metal phosphate, Sr3Bi (PO4) 3 has an cubic structure with a space group of I-43d.However, to the best of our knowledge, the photoluminescence properties of Sr3Bi (PO4) 3: Dy3+ phosphors have not been reported yet.In this paper, we synthesized the phosphor Dy3+ doped Sr3Bi (PO4) 3., in which luminescence properties were studied in detail by means of excitation and emission spectra. 2.Experimental Sr3Bi (PO4) 3: Dy3+ powders were prepared by solid-state reaction.The starting materials included SrCO3 [analytical reagent (A.R.)], Bi2O3 ( A.R.) NH4H2PO4 ( A.R.), and Dy2O3 ( 99.99 % ).Stoichiometric amounts of the starting reagents were thoroughly mixed and ground by an agate mortar.An excess (2%) of NH4H2PO4 was used to compensate for the evaporation of NH4H2PO4 at a high temperature.The mixtures were conducted at 1250C for 3 h in an electric furnace.

NH4H2PO4 at a high temperature.The mixtures were conducted at 1250C for 3 h in an electric furnace.After cooling down to the room temperature, the samples were ground into powder for characterizations.The powder sample was characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) in a Bruker AXSD8 advanced automatic diffractometer (Bruker Co., German) with Ni-filtered CuKa radiation (=1.54178 ).A scan rate of 0.02 / s was applied to record the patterns in the 2y range 10–901.Photoluminescence excitation and emissions spectra were collected in a fluorescence spectrophotometer (Hitachi F-4600).The chromaticity data were taken by the PMS-80 spectra analysis system.All the measurements were conducted at room temperature. 3.Results and discussion 3.1.X-ray diffraction analysis The obtained phosphors are white powder.Fig.1 shows the X-ray powder diffraction patterns of typical phosphors Sr3Bi0.93 (PO4) 3: 0.07Dy3+ and the standard data of Sr3Bi (PO4) 3.In Fig.1, the diffraction patterns of the sample Sr3Bi0.93 (PO4) 3; 0.07Dy3+ phase was found to be in agreement with that of the host material Sr3Bi (PO4) 3 from the reported data JCPDS card no.33-1319.Sr3Bi (PO4) 3 has the structural type of eulytine, and Bi3+ occupies distorted octahedron of oxygen ions due to three short and three long Bi–O distances, according to Ref.[17].Therefore, it can be predicted that Bi3+ occupy noninversion centrosymmetric sites and some Bi3- are replaced by Dy3+ in Sr3Bi (PO4) 3; Dy3+ because they have the same valence and ionic radii [18].The lattice parameters values of Sr3Bi (PO4) 3 are a=b=c=10.1990A, Z=4 and V=1060.90A3.There exists no impact of Dy3+ on the host structure even at the optimized dopant concentration of 7 mol%.These results indicated that Dy3+ were undoubtedly doped into the Sr3Bi (PO4) 3 crystal lattice. [21], nonradiative energy transfer in the luminescence of oxidic phosphors is based on resonance transfer by electric multipole– multipole interaction or exchange interaction.The situation in Dy3+ compounds can be characterized as follows [22]: If the Dy3+- Dy3+ distance is larger than 5A, the exchange interaction becomes ineffective, and only a multipolar interaction is important; if the Dy3+- Dy3+ distance is shorter than 5: A., the exchange interaction becomes effective.As the Rc of Dy3+- Dy3+ for Sr3Bi (PO4) 3: Dy3+ phosphor is calculated to be 19.3A, the multipolar interaction is the major mechanism of concentration quenching of Dy3+ in the Sr3Bi (PO4) 3: Dy3+ phosphor.Considering the energy match rule [1], three possible cross-relaxation channels (CRC) among Dy3+ are shown in Fig.5, denoted as CRC1, CRC2 and CRC3.The Dy3+ at - 4F9/2 level can be de-excited to (6H9/2/6F11/2).(6F9/2/6H7/2) or 6F1/2 level via these three cross-relaxation processes, in the mean while, the ground state Dy3+ Fig.4.The emission spectra of Sr3Bi1-x (PO4) 3: x Dy3+( x=0.005, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.07, 0.10, 0.15) ( ex=348 nm).

Fig.6.The CIE chromaticity coordinate for the prepared typical Sr3Bi0.93 (PO4) 3: 0.07Dy3+ under the excitation wavelength of 348 nm.accepting the energies from the Dy3+ at 4F9/2 level will arrive at 6F3/2, 6F5/2 and (6H9/2/6F11/2) level.Finally, all the Dy3+ ions involved in CRC1, CRC2 and CRC3 processes will get in their ground states, thus the luminescence related to 4F9/2 level are quenched. 3.4.Color parameters of samples Color coordinates are one of the important factors for evaluating phosphors’ performance.It is a well known fact that the color coordinates are same if the spectra profiles are identical.In such case, the color coordinates for the sample doped with 7 mol% Dy3+ were calculated using the intensity-calibrated emission spectra data and the chromatic standard issued by the Commission Internationale de I’Eclairage in 1931 (CIE1931).The CIE chromaticity diagram of Sr3Bi0.93 (PO4) 30.07Dy3+ under 348 nm excitation is shown in Fig.6 with the cross symbols ( x=0.327, y=0.353 ).It indicates that the color coordinates of present phosphors are close to the ‘‘ideal white’’ ( x=0.333, y=0.333 ) in chromaticity diagram. 4.Conclusions The novel white emitting phosphors Sr3Bi1-x (PO4) 3 x Dy3+ with various Dy3 concentrations have been synthesized by the conventional solid-state reaction.The structure of the compound was confirmed by the XRD technique.

conventional solid-state reaction.The structure of the compound was confirmed by the XRD technique.The peaks of the emissions of Dy3+ ions are located at 481 nm (blue), 575 nm (yellow) and 664 nm (red) under the excitation of 348 nm, 362 nm, 385 nm and 451 nm.Concentration quenching occurs when the Dy3+ concentration is beyond 7 mol%.The CIE color coordi nates indicates that the phosphors are suitable for white light-emitting.The photoluminescence results show that the excitation peaks are useful for solid state lighting in lamp industry. TL response of nanocrystalline MgB4O7: Dy irradiated by 3MeV proton beam, 50MeV Li3+ and 120MeV Ag9+ ion beams Numan Salah a,n, Sami Habib a, Saeed S.Babkair b, S.P.Lochab c, Vibha Chopra ca Center of Nanotechnology, King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah 21589, Saudi Arabia b Center of Nanotechnology, Department of Physics, Faculty of Science, King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah 21589, Saudi Arabia c Inter-University Accelerator Centre, Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, New Delhi 110067, India HIGHLIGHTScTL response of nanocrystalline MgBO:Dy irradiated by ion beams is studied.c Proton beam as well as Li3+ and Ag9+ ion beams irradiated samples showed different TL responses.c This nanomaterial has highest the TL sensitivity to Li3+, then Ag9+ ions and finally protons.c TRIM code is used to calculate the absorbed doses, penetration depths and main energy loss. articleinfoabstract Article history: Received 24October 2012Accepted 24January 2013Available online 9February 2013Keywords: Nanoparticles MgBO:DyIon beams Thermoluminescence Magnesium borate (MgB407) is a highly sensitive phosphor commonly used in a thermoluminescence (TL) dosimeter.In this work we report on TL response of nanocrystalline MgB4O7: Dy irradiated by 3MeV proton beam as well as 50MeV Li3+ and 120MeV Ag9+ ion beams in the fluence range of 11011 – 11015 ions/cm 2.The induced TL glow curves were compared with that of gamma rays irradiation.A single glow peak is observed at around 430K in the samples irradiated by Li3+ and Ag9+ ions, while that exposed to proton beam has an extra one at 525K.This nanomaterial has maximum sensitivity to Li3+, then Ag9+ ions and finally protons.The TL response curves of the samples exposed to these radiations are linear/sublinear at the lower fluences, while at higher values they saturate.

content: o these radiations are linear/sublinear at the lower fluences, while at higher values they saturate.These variations in the glow curve structure and TL response could be attributed to the modifications created in the traps/luminescent centres.TRIM code was also used to calculate the absorbed doses, penetration depths and main energy loss.The results show that this nanomaterial might be useful for the dosimetry of heavy charged particles such as Li3+ and Ag9+ particularly at low fluences, while in case of proton beam the TL glow curve is greatly altered and shows poor sensitivity.& 2013Elsevier Ltd.All rights reserved. 1.Introduction Nanoscale materials are defined as the materials with grain size in the nanometer scale.The surface to volume ratio is so large that the electron behaviour differs from that of bulk materials.This characteristic leads to a beneficial modification of optical, electrical, magnetic, and other physical and chemical properties of the materials.These nanomaterials have attracted large number of researchers from different areas, especially from the field of luminescence.Recent reports on different luminescent nanomaterials showed that they have a potential application in dosimetry of ionizing radiations for the measurements of high doses using the thermoluminescence (TL) technique, where the conventional microcrystalline phosphors saturate (Salah et al., 2006a, 2006b, 2008b, 2009, 2011a, 2011b; Salah, 2008a; Sahare et al., 2007; Lochab et al., 2007a, 200b; Salah, 2011c).The use of nanoscale materials has solved this problem to a major extent.The reported results of the nanomaterials have presented excellent characteristics such as high sensitivity and saturation at very high doses.Recently, the use of TL technique in measuring the doses from the conventional radiation beams has been increased.Ion beams of charged particles become a powerful technique for cancer diagnosis and therapy (Barth et al., 2003; Strehl, 1999).

les become a powerful technique for cancer diagnosis and therapy (Barth et al., 2003; Strehl, 1999).There are a number of commercial TL dosimeters (TLD) which are readily available to the users and researchers but in spite of this, efforts are still being made by the research community to improve the TL characteristics of different materials (Madhusoodanan et al., 1999; Shinde et al., 2001; Lakshmanan et al., 2002; Kim et al., 2004) for specific applications.Magnesium borate (MgB4O7) is a highly sensitive phosphor commonly used for medical dosimetry using the TL technique.The preparation of polycrystalline MgB4O7 activated by dysprosium (Dy) was reported in 1974 (Kazankaya et al., 1974).It is a near tissue equivalent material with an effective atomic number for photoelectric absorption equal to 8.4 compared to 7.4 for water and soft biological tissue.The dosimetric characteristics of MgB4O7: Dy were systematically reported in 1982–1983 (Barbina et al., 1982; Driscol et al., 1983).Later on this material was doped with extra dopants like sodium (Na; Furetta et al., 2000) and reported to be a useful TLD material particularly in individual monitoring and in various medical dosimetry purposes.The nanostructure form of this material was studied for its TL response to gamma rays in 2007 (Lochab et al., 2007b).They found that the nanomaterial has a linear TL response for high doses, poor fading and excellent reusability features.These excellent TL characters have encouraged further investigations about this nanomaterial.Recently, the nanocrystalline form of MgB4O7: Dy, INa was exposed to gamma rays and 150MeV proton beam, and studied for its TL response (Bahl et al., 2013).The authors reported that the TL response curve of gamma rays is linear in a good range of exposure (0.1-1000Gy), but proton beam irradiated materials shows early saturation ( < 350Gy ) / However, this nanomaterial has not been tested for its TL response to other ionizing radiations like heavy ions.

ations.These modifications might be more in case of heavier ions such as Li3+ and Ag9- þ.This might be the cause of missing the TCs/LCs of the second TL glow peak of MgB4O7: Dy nanoparticles irradiated by Li3- þ and Ag9+ ion beams (Fig.3 curves b and c).The TCs/LCs responsible for the second peak at 525K probably become optically non-active.Sparsely ionizing radiations like protons or gamma rays show almost similar TL results.The used protons perhaps could not induce much modification in the TCs/LCs compare to those of the other used heavier ions ( i.e.Li3+ and Ag9+).Proton is a very tiny particle compared with these ions; therefore, the number of electrons excited/trapped in these TCs/LCs might be small in case of proton beam irradiated sample (Fig.3, curve a).This might lead to a poor TL intensity in comparison with those of the other ion beams.The TL intensity in case of Ag9+ irradiated sample is also not high (Fig.3, curve c) compare to that of Li3+ irradiated sample ( Fig.3, curve b).This might be due to the small penetration depth of Ag9+ in the MgB4O7: Dy pellet.TRIM code calculations (Ziegler et al., 1985) show that the penetration depth of 120MeV Ag9+ ions in the MgB4O7: Dy pellet is only 27.72 m, while that of Li3+ is 527.98 mm (Table1).This means that there is only a small layer of MgB4O7:Dy pellet contributing to the TL emission in case of Ag9+ ions irradiated sample.TRIM code calculations given in Table 1 show that more than 99.9% of energy lost by the used 3MeV proton beam as well as 50MeV Li3+ and 120MeV Ag9+ ion beams in 1 mm thick MgB4O7: Dy pellets is electronic in nature, which perhaps influences the initial energy band structure and the trapping and recombination mechanism.Similar effects were also observed in our earlier studies (Sahare et al., 2005; Salah, et al., 2006a) which could be attributed to the change in the population of LCs/TCs; during irradiation by highly energetic ions.

content: ction The Dy3+, mainly as doping ions in phosphors, has two dominant bands in the emission spectrum.The yellow band (575nm) corresponds to the 4F9/2-6H13/2 transition while the blue band (480nm) corresponds to the 4F9/2-6H15/2 transition [1,2].It is lucky that the intensity of the two hypersensitive transitions varies obviously with chemical environment in different host material systems, so the white-light emitting can be generated by accurately mixing and adjusting the intensity ratio of yellow-to-blue emission(Y/B) in a suitable matrix.Besides that, due to the special electron trapping and thermoluminescence properties of the materials doped with Dy3+, Dy3+ ion has been considered as an excellent activator for long-lasting phosphorescence (LLP) materials and has been widely used as a dopant in various matrixes [3–9].The phosphors Dy doped have been also studied on its long afterglow white-emitting behaviors, but the reports on white LED phosphors doped with Dy3+ were quite rare.While the characteristic emission peaks of Dy3+ ions locate at blue light and yellow light regions.Thus, it is entirely feasible to implement white light directly by utilizing single-doped Dy3+ ions in some inorganic compounds.Base on the disscusion, it is very important to develop a novel host material suitable for Dy3+ ions doping.Bi4Si3O12 (BSO) has been studied as an excellent scintillator, which has good mechanical, thermal, electrical and electro-optical properties, good physical and chemical properties, low price and low melting point (1300K) [10–14].Bi3+ in BSO shows a broad band-like absorption property.And Bi3+ ions are very good sensitizers of luminescence [15,16], which can efficiently absorb the near UV/ blue light and transfer the energy to the luminescence center.In this letter, BSO silicate host is chosen for Dy3+ doping to search novel efficient white-emitting phosphors which exhibits a direct white light when excited under UV light of 270 nm.

and then dried at 353K for 24 h.Then the precursor obtained was calcined at 773K and 1073K in an air atmosphere, respectively.After these procedures, the resultant BSO:xDy and BSO:xDy,yTb phosphors were produced.In the present work, the doping concentrations of Dy3+ ion were fixed at x0, 1, 4, 5 and 6 mol%, while the concentrations of Tb3+ were fixed at y=4, 6, 8, and 10 mol%.The crystalline structures of the phosphors were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) with CuKα radiation (=0.1541 nm).The excitation (PLE) and emission (PL) spectra of both BSO:Dy and BSO:Dy,Tb powders under UV light (270nm) were recorded on a Hitachi F-4600 spectrometer.The temperature dependence of PL intensity was also measured in a range from room temperature (RT) to 393K.All of the samples were the same mass and pressed into wafers with the same dimensions of approximately ∅20 mm 1 mm for measuring the photoluminescence spectrum.The slits for both excitation and emission light were all set as 2.5 nm, the scan speed was fixed at 240 nm/min, and the voltage was operated at the condition of V=700V.

Fig.1.XRD pattern of BSO:4 mol% Dy powders calcined at 773K and 1073K in an air atmosphere, respectively.Both the photoluminescence spectra of the 4 mol% Dy-doped BSO phosphor under an excitation at 270 nm and excitation spectra under lights monitored at 575 nm, 488 nm and 460 nm are shown in Fig.3.Usually, the Dy3+→02-charge transfer band is located at 166 nm that cannot be seen in visible range [17].So, a predominant broad excitation band at 268 nm is from the host excitation, coexisting with several small sharp peaks located at 350 nm–400 nm for 4f–4f transitions of Dy3+.The characteristic emission peaks of Dy3+ ions located at 488 nm, 575 nm and 665 nm can be attributed to the electron transitions of Dy3+ 4F9/26H13/2 for the 575 nm emission, 4F9/26H15/2 for the 488 nm emission and 4F9/26H11/2 for the 665 nm, respectively.But the peak, located at 665 nm, is rather weak and it scarcely has contribution to the white light.The broad band at 460 nm can be assigned to the host emission of BSO, resulting from that O pelectrons absorb energies and then transfer to Bip-electrons [18].Compared to the results illustrated in Figs.2 and 3, there are three points indicated that the energy transfer occurs between Bi3+ and Dy3+.Firstly, the PL and PLE spectra are overlapped at the region of 350–400 nm.In the overlapped region, the energies are transferred directly from Bi3+ to Dy3+.Secondly, the peaks, located at 575 nm and 488 nm, can be obtained under 270 nm excitation.In other words, the energies are absorbed by host and transferred to the Dy3+ partly, that means the energy transfer occurred indirectly between Bi3+ and Dy3+.

nsferred to the Dy3+ partly, that means the energy transfer occurred indirectly between Bi3+ and Dy3+.Besides that, the phenomenon, the intrinsic emission peak of BSO is weakened and the characteristic peaks of Dy are enhanced as the doping concentration increases, declares that the energy transfer also occurred between Bi3+ and Dy3+.In order to clearly explain the possible process of origin phosphorescence for the BSO:Dy phosphors and the energy transfer, we drew a schematic energy level diagram, as shown in Fig.4.The solid lines mean the excitation and emission.The dash lines mean the energy transfer.The luminescence process can be represented as followings: after irradiation by UV light, the electrons in valence band are excited to the conduction band and primary free electrons and holes are formed in the host sample.Then, relaxation of the primary electrons and holes produces numerous secondary electrons and holes, which result in a number of e–h pairs.After that, the energy transfers from the e–h pairs to the luminescence centers, Bi3+ ions and Dy3+ ions.Finally, the luminescence can be observed.According to the first-principle study on pure BSO [18], it is possible that the O atoms around Bi absorb the energy (p-electrons) and transfer to the Bip-electrons via route 1 in this process.Meantime, the energy is transferred to Dy3+ ions via route 2.Because the PLE spectra are overlapped at the region of 350–400 nm, route 3 is also occurred. The MgB4O7: Dy pellets produced by solid state present some advantages. articleinfo Article history: Received 24June 2013Accepted 28April 2014Available online 9May 2014Keywords: Magnesium tetraborate Thermoluminescent dosimetry High dose dosimetry abstract There are several routes employed for the production of synthetic magnesium tetraborate, for example, sol–gel method, combustion, wet reaction synthesis, solid-state route and precipitation (crystalgrowth).The most commonly used synthesis methods are the wet reaction (precipitation) and solid-state synthesis; both production routes are efficient, but is very difficult to find a direct comparison for them.The present work proposes a direct comparison of both production routes used for magnesium tetraborate synthesis for thermoluminescent (TL) dosimetry.In this work, MgB4O7: Dy was prepared by both methods, wet reaction or precipitation-route 1, and solid-state synthesis -route 2, with the same amount of dopant (0.1%).In the first part of work, the crystalline phases were confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and it was observed that MgB4O7: Dy can be obtained satisfactorily through both routes, although a very intense crystalline phase of H3BO3 for the powder produced through route 1 was observed.The dose response curve of MgBO pellets (producedforbothroutes) presents linear behavior when the materials are irradiated with 60Co in the dose range of 10-100Gy.
section: Thermoluminescent dosimetric comparison for two different MgB<sub>4</sub>O<sub>7</sub>: Dy production routes L.F.Souza <sup>n</sup>, R.M.Vidal, S.O.Souza, D.N.Souza Physics Department of Federal University of Sergipe, Campus Prof.José Aloísio de Campos, 49.100-000, São Cristóvão, SE, Brazil ## H I G H L I G H T S High doses dosimetry with r Mg B4O7 : Dy .Some differences about two different routes of Mg B4O7 : Dy Wet reaction and solid state synthesis routes for MgB O :Dy production. <sup>The</sup> Mg B4O7 : Dy pellets produced by solid state present some advantages.## a r t i c l e i n f o Article history: Received24June2013Accepted28April2014Available online9May2014Keywords: Magnesium tetraborate Thermoluminescent dosimetry High dose dosimetry ## a b s t r a c t There are several routes employed for the production of synthetic magnesium tetraborate, for example, sol–gel method, combustion, wet reaction synthesis, solid-state route and precipitation (crystal growth).The most commonly used synthesis methods are the wet reaction (precipitation) and solid-state synthesis; both production routes are efficient, but is very difficult to find a direct comparison for them.The present work proposes a direct comparison of both production routes used for magnesium tetraborate synthesis for thermoluminescent (TL) dosimetry.In this work, Mg B4O7 : Dy was prepared by both methods, wet reaction or precipitation-route1, and solid-state synthesis -route2, with the same amount of dopant (0.1%).In the first part of work, the crystalline phases were confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and it was observed that Mg B4O7 : Dy can be obtained satisfactorily through both routes, although a very intense crystalline phase of H3B O3 for the powder produced through route1 was observed.The dose response curve of MgB O pellets (produced for both routes) presents linear behavior when the materials are irradiated with60Co in the dose range of10 - 100Gy .

content: presents linear behavior when the materials are irradiated with 60Co in the dose range of 10-100Gy.The results showed that both methods produce MgB4O7: Dy efficiently; however, solid-state synthesis produces MgB4O7: Dy more sensitive to gamma radiation.& 2014Elsevier Ltd.All rights reserved. 1.Introduction Borate has been the focus of many studies, particularly for nonlinear optics and radiation dosimetry based on the thermoluminescence (TL) phenomenon (Chung, 2010).Magnesium borate has good characteristics to be applied as a TL dosimeter; it is about 10 times more sensitive than LiF and has an effective atomic number for photoelectric absorption equal to 8.4, compared with 7.4 for water and soft biological tissue that is crucial for personal dosimetry.Magnesium tetraborate (MgB4O7) is already described in the literature as a highly sensitive and low fading phosphor, with excellent performance for detection of beta, gamma and neutron radiations (Prokic, 2007).It is also used for high dose dosimetry, exhibiting linearity for a wide range of doses, in the order of μGy–Gy (Furetta et al., 2000).The first MgB4O7: Dy, sintered as pellets of 5.5 mm diameter and 1 mm thickness, were produced by the Boris Kidric Institute of Nuclear Sciences, Vinca, Yugoslavia (Szabo et al., 1984).In the early 1990s, Campos and Fernandes Filho (1990) produced this material by precipitation route and managed many desirable qualities for personnel and environmental dosimetry, such as great TL reproducibility and low energy dependence for gamma ray.A literature survey showed that no studies have investigated which is the best production route for magnesium tetraborate for thermoluminescent (TL) applications.The main methods for preparation of polycrystalline and nanocrystalline MgB4O7 are via the wet reaction (alsoknownasprecipitation), crystal growth (BridgmanmethodandCzochralskimethod) (Azorin, 2014), solidstate synthesis, sol–gel methods, and combustion methods (Bahl et al., 2013).

) (Azorin, 2014), solidstate synthesis, sol–gel methods, and combustion methods (Bahl et al., 2013).The combustion method produces MgB4O7 in nanoscale size, which is interesting for very high doses dosimetry (Bahl et al., 2013).However, the most commonly used methods for obtaining the MgB4O7 in microcrystalline powder are precipitation and solid-state synthesis; both methods produce phosphor with a particle size in the micron range order.TL phosphors with particle sizes in this range can be very sensitive and have a linear dose– response at low doses to high doses (mGy-Gy), with dose saturation at very high doses (kGy) (Wani et al., 2012).In this work, two batches of pellets of MgB4O7 were prepared with powder produced by solid-state and wet reaction synthesis.Their TL reproducibility and sensitivity were analyzed after gamma irradiation.The main purpose of this study was to analyze the effect of the synthesis methods on TL properties of doped magnesium tetraborate and to evaluate which of these methods of synthesis (precipitation or solid-state synthesis) have better efficacy for high dose detection. 2.Materials and methods MgB4O7: Dy produced by the wet reaction (precipitationmethod) was called route 1, and solid-state synthesis was called route 2.The reagents and dopants used to produce MgB4O.7:Dy for both routes were 2 g MgO (Merck, 99.9% purity), 15 g H3BO3 (Merck, 99.9% purity) and oxide dysprosium (Dy2O3), 0.1% mol (Sigma-Aldrich, 99.9% purity).Both synthesis routes follow the reaction described below: MgO+4H3BO3→MgB4O7+ 6H2O For route 1, all reagents and dopants ( MgO, H3BO3 and Dy2O3 ) were diluted in nitric acid (HNO3), which assists and accelerates the formation of MgB4O7, with the aid of a magnetic stirrer for 5 min.At the end of the reaction, a whitish and pasty fluid was achieved, which remained in an oven for 24 h at 1001C to dry.In order to remove possible residual acidity, consecutive washings of the final compound with distilled water were carried out.

residual acidity, consecutive washings of the final compound with distilled water were carried out.For route 2, the same reagents, dopants and respective proportions were used as for route 1, except for nitric acid.For the solidstate synthesis, raw materials were mixed and ground using a mortar and a pestle to obtain a homogenized mixture.In route 1, the mixture was sintered at 800C for 2 h inside a furnace in atmospheric air, followed by 500C for 1 h.For route 2, the sintering was performed at 900C for 4 h inside a furnace in atmospheric air, followed by 5001C for 1 h.To confirm their structures after the sinterization process, the powders obtained by routes 1 and 2 were investigated by X-ray diffraction (XRD).The XRD measurements were performed with a powder diffractometer (RigakumodelDMAX2000) using CuKα radiation, with the tube operating at 40 kV/20 mA in the step scan mode to steps of 2 ( )=0.02 in the interval of scan 2θ from 10 to 801, and 10 s per step.All measurements were performed at room temperature. Fig.1.Experimental XRD of polycrystalline MgBO produced by route 1 and the reference patterns o MgB4O7 and HBO.TL analyses were performed using samples in pellet format.To obtain mechanically-resistant pellets it is common to use a mixture of polycrystals and a polymer (D’amorim et al., 2012).In this work, all pellets were produced with the addition of Teflon, with mass proportion of 1 (phosphor):0.4 (Teflon).The pellets were produced by cold compaction in a hydraulic press, with 100 kgf / c m2.After pressing, the pellets were sintered at 300C for 30 min and 400C for 1.5 h.Each pellet had a final mass of 40.0 mg, and was approximately 6.0 mm in diameter and 2.0 mm in thickness.For pellet selection, three consecutive cycles of irradiation, TL reading, and thermal treatment were performed.For each batch 10 pellets were chosen that exhibited TL behavior with coefficient of variation (CV%) lower than 10%.

10 pellets were chosen that exhibited TL behavior with coefficient of variation (CV%) lower than 10%.This coefficient is defined as the percentage ratio of the standard deviation to the mean values of TL emissions.The standards established for pellet selection are in accordance with ISO12794:2000 (ISO, 2000), in which only dosimeters that presented a variation coefficient (CV%) below 10% are used.These analyses can help in identifying the different sources of variation in the reproducibility of the TL system (D’amorim et al., 2012).The pellets were exposed to gamma radiation, using the 60Co Gamma-Cell System (doserateof141Gy/h), at the Radiation Technology/IPENCenter, and to a gammacell 220 (doserate10kGy/h), at DEN-UFPE.All irradiations were performed with the pellets positioned between 3 mm thick Lucite plates, to ensure that electronic equilibrium conditions were produced (build-up).The TL response of pellets was acquired by a Harshaw TL reader system, model TLD-3500, obtained with a linear heating rate of 10C / s.In the sequence, the samples were thermally treated at 400 C / 1 h for their reuse.For both methods, the region of interest (ROI) for integration area was within 200–3001C. 3.Results and discussions Figs.1 and 2 show the diffraction pattern of powders obtained via routes 1 and 2.The XRD pattern indicates that the synthesized materials for routes 1 and 2 are in the orthorhombic phase, coincident with ICSDCard number 01-076-0666.The crystallographic parameters are a13.73 Å; b7.97 Å; c8.62 Å;=90=90, corresponding to magnesium tetraborate (MgB4O7) Experimental data (Figs.1 and 2) show that by both routes the majority phase obtained was MgBO, but some pronounced peaks corresponded to boric acid (No.00-0231034) were also present for material prepared through route 1 (precipitationmethod).One of the main raw materials for MgB4O7 synthesis is H3BO3, which was used for both production routes in the same amounts, but it is observed that H3BO3 did not react completely, as expected by route 1.

in the same amounts, but it is observed that H3BO3 did not react completely, as expected by route 1.In route 2, the peak relating to H3BO3 is much less pronounced (Fig.2), showing a better efficacy of the solid-state reaction, which shows that higher temperatures result in a unique phase of rl MgB407.This excess of H3BO3 promotes the reduction of TL sensitivity, due to a reduction in the mechanical strength of the pellet (Campos and Fernandes Filho, 1990). Fig.2.Experimental XRD of polycrystalline MgBO produced by route 2 and the reference patterns of MgB4O7 and HBO.a b Fig.3.Glow curves of MgBO:Dy (route1) obtained with a linear heating-rate of 101C/s and the TL-dose dependence.a b Fig.4.Glow curves of MgBO:Dy (route2) obtained with a linear heating-rate of 101C/s and the TL-dose dependence.Figs.3 and 4a show the glow curves for MgB4O7: Dy for routes 1 and 2, respectively.Two TL emission regions are observed for MgB4O7: Dy (route1), the first at approximately 2001C and a second less intense peak at around 250C.The TL emission observed for MgB4O7: Dy is expected and the peaks observed are due to 480 and 580 nm from Dy3+ emissions (Karali et al., 2002).The dose response curve for route 1 (shown in Fig.

and 580 nm from Dy3+ emissions (Karali et al., 2002).The dose response curve for route 1 (shown in Fig.3b) presents linear behavior for the dose range studied (10–100Gy).For the MgB4O7 produced through route 2, one well-defined TL emission peak can be observed at around 2501C (Fig.4a) and the dose response has linear behavior (Fig.4b).For TL dosimetry, it is important that material has few TL emission peaks for better data interpretation and correlation between TL responses and radiation absorbed dose, which is the main purpose of TL dosimetry (Boss, 2001).In Fig.5, it can be observed that the MgB4O7: Dy produced by the solid-state synthesis (route2) shows greater sensitivity in its TL response compared to the dose response obtained by pellets produced by route 1.Taking into account that the relative Fig.5.Sensitivity of MgBO:Dy for routes 1 and 2 (10–100Gy).TL sensitivity is dependent on the intrinsic efficiency of dosimeters, the size of the pellet and of the range response of the TLD reader (Boss, 2001), the sensitivity obtained for MgB4O7: Dy (route2) is higher than MgB4O7: Dy (route1).These differences observed in TL sensitivity can also be associated with different structural properties (size of particle, morphology) of the materials due the preparation routes used, as explained by other authors who studied the influence of the production routes in TL efficiency to other dosimeters (Azorin, 2014; Yukihara et al., 2013).Route 1 produces MgB4O7 effectively, but besides being a longer synthesis, the wash processes do not guarantee the complete removal of residual acidity of the material, as can be observed in Fig.1.In addition to being a faster method, that is, in 1 day the material can be produced efficiently, using high temperatures, the solid state synthesis ensures the formation of homogeneous phases in the phosphors. 4.

atures, the solid state synthesis ensures the formation of homogeneous phases in the phosphors. 4.Conclusions The initial comparative study performed here shows that the MgB4O7: Dy pellets produced by solid-state synthesis (route2) have some advantages over the material produced through wet reaction (route1).For both methods, an excess of boric acid was observed by XRD, because H3BO3 did not react completely, although for MgB4O7: Dy (route2) the TL peak referring to H3BO3 is sharply reduced, showing that the use of high temperatures in solid-state synthesis is more efficient for the MgB4O7 formation.The solid-state synthesis route is a simple method and does not require HNO3, only high sintering temperatures ( 900C, 4 h ) to ensure the production of a TL-sensitive material.The phosphor synthesized by route 2 has one TL emission peak around 250C that provides higher facility for TL analyses.The dose response curves for both materials are linear in the dose range studied, showing that both routes are useful for producing TL dosimeters for monitoring high doses, although, the MgB4O7: Dy (route2) has a higher TL sensitivity compared with MgB4O7: Dy (route1). Preparation and photoluminescence properties of Ḋ y Ḍ 3+-doped Ba3Lu (PO4) 3 phosphors YANGZaifa (杨在发), SUNYumei (孙宇梅), XUQiguang (徐齐光), SUNJiayue (孙家跃) (School of Science, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing 100048, China) Received 16April 2015; revised 31August 2015Abstract: Ba3Lu (PO4) 3Dy3+ phosphors were successfully synthesized by conventional solid state reaction and its photoluminescence properties were investigated by X-ray diffraction (XRD), photoluminescence spectra and diffuse reflectance spectra, respectively.Results showed that the phosphor could be excited by the ultraviolet visible light in the region from 320 to 460 nm, and it showed two dominant emission bands peaking at 484 nm (bluelight) and 575 nm (yellowlight) which originated from the transitions of 4F9/2→6H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 of Dy3+, respectively.According to Dexter’s theory, the concentration quenching mechanism occurred via the electric dipole-dipole interaction.The lifetime values of Dy3+ ions at different concentrations (x=0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08 and 0.10) were determined to be about 0.8556, 0.7595, 0.6864, 0.6059 and 0.5456 ms.Keywords: luminescence; white light-emitting diodes; Ba3Lu (PO4) 3: Dy3; phosphors; rare earths In recent years, great progress has been made on white light-emitting diodes (LEDs) for solid-state lighting, such as automotive headlamp, backlighting, flashlights, and so on [ 1, 2 ].Rare earth doped phosphors of w-LEDs have attracted increasing attention due to their excellent characteristics of long lifetime, high brightness, safe, and environmental friendliness[3–5].As a typical white light emission ion, trivalent dysprosium Dy3+ ion has drawn keen interests of research due to the potential applications in near white light emission.It is clearly noted that Dy3+ ion has two dominant emission bands peaking at 484 nm (bluelight) and 575 nm (yellowlight), respectively.
section: Preparation and photoluminescence properties of Ḋ y Ḍ 3+-doped Ba3Lu ( P O4 ) 3 phosphors YANG Zaifa (杨在发), SUN Yumei (孙宇梅), XU Qiguang (徐齐光), SUN Jiayue (孙家跃) (School of Science, Beijing Technology and Business University, Beijing100048, China) Received16April2015; revised31August2015Abstract: Ba3Lu ( P O4 ) 3Dy3+phosphors were successfully synthesized by conventional solid state reaction and its photoluminescence properties were investigated by X-ray diffraction (XRD), photoluminescence spectra and diffuse reflectance spectra, respectively.Results showed that the phosphor could be excited by the ultraviolet visible light in the region from320 to460 nm, and it showed two dominant emission bands peaking at484 nm (blue light) and575 nm (yellow light) which originated from the transitions of4F9/2 → 6H15/2 and4F9/26H13/2 o f Dy3+, respectively.According to Dexter’s theory, the concentration quenching mechanism occurred via the electric dipole-dipole interaction.The lifetime values of Dy3+ions at different concentrations (x=0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08 and0.10) were determined to be about0.8556, 0.7595, 0.6864, 0.6059 and0.5456 ms.Keywords: luminescence; white light-emitting diodes; Ba3Lu ( P O4 ) 3 : Dy3 ; phosphors; rare earths In recent years, great progress has been made on white light-emitting diodes (LEDs) for solid-state lighting, such as automotive headlamp, backlighting, flashlights, and so o n [ 1 , 2 ] .Rare earth doped phosphors of w-LEDs have attracted increasing attention due to their excellent characteristics of long lifetime, high brightness, safe, and environmental friendliness<sup>[3–5]</sup>.As a typical white light emission ion, trivalent dysprosium Dy3+ion has drawn keen interests of research due to the potential applications in near white light emission.It is clearly noted that Dy3+ion has two dominant emission bands peaking at484 nm (blue light) and575 nm (yellow light), respectively.

content: as two dominant emission bands peaking at 484 nm (bluelight) and 575 nm (yellowlight), respectively.The former is assigned to 4F9/2→6H15/2 transition, which is relatively invariable while the latter is attributed to the 4F9/26H13/2 transition and its intensity is strongly influenced by the chemical environment surrounding Dy3+ ion due to J=2 [ 6, 7 ].Therefore, white light emission can be formed with appropriate color temperature and chromaticity coordinates through suitable adjustment of the blue to yellow (B/Y) intensity ratio in Dy3+-doped luminescence materials[8].As a result, Dy3+-doped single-phased phosphors has been investigated a lot, such as ZnWO4: Dy3+[ 9 ] CaMoO4Dy3+[ 10 ], Sr3Gd(PO4)3:Dy3+ [11].Orthophosphates, with formula A3B (PO4) 3, where A represents divalent cation and B trivalent cation, acted as eminent matrices for solid-state lighting because the strongly disordered structure contributing to the luminescence have been extensively investigated, such as Ba3Y (PO4) 3 [ 12 ], Ca3Bi (PO4) 3 [ 13 ], Sr3Y (PO4) 3 [ 14 ], and so on.Recently, Guo et al.reported Eu2+- Mn2+ codoped orange-yellow-emitting Ba3Lu(PO4)3 phosphors[15].Zhang et al.reported an intense red-emitting phosphor Ba3Lu (PO4) 3: Eu3+ for near ultraviolet (NUV) light emitting diodes application[16].Jin et al.[17] reported the colortunable phosphors Ba3Lu(PO4)3:Ce3+,Tb3+ for the use in field emission displays.These results indicate that the Ba3Lu (PO4) 3 compound is a good host for rare earth ions doped phosphor.However, there are no reports about the detailed photoluminescence properties of Ba3.u (PO4) 3: Dy3+ phosphors so far.

ut the detailed photoluminescence properties of Ba3.u (PO4) 3: Dy3+ phosphors so far.In the present study, to find a white light phosphor for solid state light, we synthesized the eulytite-type material Ba3Lu (PO4) 3Dy3+ phosphors and investigated their luminescence properties and the concentration quenching mechanism. 1Experimental The conventional solid-state reaction method was used to synthesize the Ba3Lu1- (PO4) 3: x Dy3+( x=0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08 and 0.10) powder samples.The starting reagents, BaCO3 (AR (analyticalreagent)), Lu2O3 ( 99.99 % ).N H4H2PO4 (AR) and Dy2O3 ( 99.99 % ) were weighed according to the stoichiometric ratios.Then, they were ground evenly in an agate mortar and the mixture was preheated at 600C for 3 h in a muffle furnace, reground, and calcined at 1300 oC for 6 h in air atmosphere.Finally the as-synthesized samples were slowly cooled to room temperature in the furnace and ground again into powder for subsequent measurement.X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) patterns of the samples were examined on a X-ray powder diffractometer (Bruker D2, Karlsruhe, Germany) with CuKα radiation (=0.15406 nm ) operated at 30 kV, 10 mA.The continuous scanning rate (2θ ranging from 20o to 70o) used as phase formation determination was 12(o)/min.Roomtemperature photoluminescence excitation (PLE) and emission (PL) spectra were measured using a Hitachi F-7000 fluorescence spectrophotometer (Tokyo, Japan) equipped with a150W xenon lamp as an excitation source.The luminescence decay curves were recorded on a spectrofluorometer (HORIBA, JOBINYVONFL3-21), and 370 nm pulse laser radiation (Spectra-LED) was used as the excitation source.All the measurements of the phosphors were performed at room temperature. 2Results and discussion Fig.1 displays the XRD patterns of Ba3Lu1-x (PO4) 3.x Dy3+( x=0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08 and 0.10) powder samples compared with the standard data of Ba3Lu(PO4)3 (JCPDSNo.43-0212).

Fig.7CIE chromaticity diagram of Ba3Lu0.95 (PO4) 3: 0.05Dy3+ phosphors excited at 349 nm 3Conclusions In summary, synthesis and optical properties of Ba3Lu1-x (PO4) 3 x Dy3+ phosphors were investigated in this paper.The XRD study confirmed that the samples with different concentrations of Dy3+ were composed of mono-phase Ba3Lu (PO4) 3.The PL spectrum of the phosphor consisted of two main peaks at 484 and 576 nm under 349 nm excitation, which originated from the transitions of 4F9/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 of Dy3+, respectively.The PLE spectrum for 484 nm emission consisted of several characteristic peaks located at 294, 324, 349, 363, 387, 426 and 453 nm.The optimum dopant concentration of Dy3+ ions was confirmed to be 5 mol.% in Ba3Lu (PO4) 3: Dy3+ system and the energy transfer mechanism was dipole-dipole interaction.The lifetime values of Dy3+ ions at different concentrations (x=0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.08 and 0.10) were determined to be about 0.8556, 0.7595, 0.6864, 0.6059 and 0.5456 ms, respectively.

content: in combination with a yellow phosphor of cerium (III)-doped yttrium aluminum garnet (AGCe3+) [3].The drawback of this combination, however, is poor color rendition due to lack of a redemitting component, thermal quenching and narrow visible range.In order to meet the optimum requirements of w-LEDs, tricolor phosphors with high stability and intense absorption in UV or near UV spectral region are in great demand [4].At the same time, single-composition white-emitting phosphors for ultraviolet (UV) or near UV excitation have drawn much attention for solid state lighting.It is well-known that a Dy3+ ion with a4 f9 electronic configuration generally has two dominant emission bands in visible range: the blue band (470–500 nm) due to the 4F9/26H15/2 transition and the yellow band (570–600 nm) due to the 4F9/26H13/2 transition.White light can be obtained by not only mixing the appropriate ratio of the three primary red, green, and blue colors, but also by creating the appropriate mixture of blue and yellow emissions.Consequently, white light emission can be fabricated with appropriate color temperature and chromaticity coordinates through suitable adjustment of the blue to yellow intensity ratio in Dy3+-doped luminescence materials.Furthermore, the color rendering property of phosphors would be improved by adding Dy3+ to the host [5,6].As a result, Dy3+ ions have been reported multiple times [7,8].Dy3+ doped phosphors, such as SrMgSiO [7], NaLa(MoO) [9] etc.have been recognized as potential white-light-emitting phosphors for UV-pumped LEDs.Since 1970, orthophosphates with the general formula A3M (PO4) 3 (whereAisdivalentcationandMistrivalentcation) have composed a large family of eulytine depending on different A and M, such as Ca3Ln (PO4) 3 [10], Sr3La (PO4) 3 [11], Ba3Lu (PO4) 3 [12], and so on.

ent A and M, such as Ca3Ln (PO4) 3 [10], Sr3La (PO4) 3 [11], Ba3Lu (PO4) 3 [12], and so on.In these eulytine phosphates, a certain number of them have been synthesized as hosts for rare earth doped phosphors, such as Sr3Y (PO4) 3: Ce3+ and Sr3Y (PO4) 3: Sb3+, in which the Ce3+ ion showed efficient ultraviolet emission and the Sb3+ ion showed an efficient near-white emission [13].For well-studied compound Sr3Gd (PO4) 3, many publications have been on the study of crystal structure, synthesis technology, luminescence and other properties of this optical material.An efficient near-infrared quantum cutting Tb3+- Yb3+ co-doped phosphors Sr3Gd (PO4) 3 have been synthesized in [14].A novel tunable full-color-emitting SrGd (PO4) 3: Eu2+, Mn2+ phosphor system was successfully developed in [15].These results indicate that the developed phosphor may be promising as a single-component white-light-emitting phosphor for white LEDs.Owing to potential application for w-LEDs of Dy3+ and Sr3Gd (PO4) 3, there have been no reports on the photoluminescence of Sr3Gd (PO4) 3: Dy3+ 1 phosphor so far.In this work, Dy3+þ doped Sr3Gd (PO4) 3 phosphors were prepared by a solid-state reaction.Some investigations on the luminescent properties, concentration quenching and thermal quenching properties were discussed in detail. 2.Experimental 2.1.Sample preparation A series of Sr3Gd1-1 (PO4) 3: x Dy3+( x=0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.03, 0.05, 0 ) 5 and 0.08) were described in this work and compounds were synthesized by the high-temperature solid-state reaction method.The starting materials, SrCO3 (AR (AnalyticalReagent)), Gd2O3 (99.99%), NH4H2PO4 (AR) and Dy2O3 (99.99%), were weighed stoichimetrically and ground evenly in an agate mortar and subsequently put into an alumina crucible.First, the mixtures were heated up to 600C and kept at this temperature for 4 h.The resulting samples were again well grounded in an agate mortar and then heated up to 12501C for 5 h in ambient air.

White light emission from Ca9Bi(PO4)7:Dy3þ single-phase phosphors for light-emitting diodes Z.W.Zhang a, b, A.J.Song b, Y.Yue a, H.Zhong a, X.Y.Zhang a, M.Z.Ma a, *, R.P.Liu aa State Key Laboratory of Metastable Materials Science and Technology, Yanshan University, Qinhuangdao, 066600, China b Chemical Engineering College, Hebei Normal University of Science and Technology, Qinhuangdao, 066600, China articleinfo Article history: Received 8June 2015Received in revised form 1July 2015Accepted 2July 2015Available online 4August 2015Keywords: CaBi(PO):Dy3þ Single-phase full-color phosphor Luminescence abstract A novel single-phase full-color phosphor CagBi (PO4) 7: Dy3+þ was synthesized by a high-temperature solidstate reaction.X-ray powder diffraction analysis confirmed the phase formation of CagBi (PO4) 7: Dy3+ material.The photoluminescence (PL) excitation and emission spectra and the concentration dependence of the emission intensity of the phosphor were investigated.The results show that the phosphor could be efficiently excited by near-UV (NUV) light (340e440nm), exhibiting blue (487nm) and yellow (577nm) emissions corresponding to the 4F9/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 transitions, respectively.The luminescence intensity of CagBi1-x (PO4) 7: x Dy3+ phosphor first increased and then decreased with increasing Dy3+ concentration and reached the maximum value at rx=0.20.The effect of Mg2+ co-doping concentration on the PL intensity of the as-prepared samples was also investigated.The calculated color coordinates lie in the white region.Therefore, the obtained results suggest that the prepared phosphors have great potential for use as single-phase full-color phosphors for NUV white-light-emitting diodes. 1.

content: ull-color phosphors for NUV white-light-emitting diodes. 1.Introduction Nowadays, white-light-emitting diodes (WLEDs) have attracted much attention due to their advantages over the existing incandescent and fluorescent lamps, such as high efficiency, compactness, long operational lifetime, and environmental friendliness.Therefore, researchers have developed several technologies combining blue/UVLED and phosphors to generate white light [1,2].The first method uses blue LED chips and yellow YAG: Ce3+ phosphors, exhibiting both a high luminescence efficiency and lower color-rendering index [3,4].The second method uses the combination of near-UV (NUV) LED chips and the red/green/yellow/blue light emitted from the phosphors, exhibiting a high colorrendering index and low luminous efficiency due to the light reabsorption among different color phosphors [5].Thus, developing single-phase full-color phosphors has been a popular technique [6,7].It is well known that appropriate hosts doped with Dy3+ ions can emit white light because of their principal emissions in the blue and yellow regions, corresponding to the 4F9/2 6H15/2 and 4F9/2 6H13/2 transitions.This method has attracted much attention because of its capability of white-light emission in a single host [8e11].Although the single-phase full-color emitting phosphors for NUV-pumped WLED have been extensively developed, exploring an excellent host is still worthy to be considered.Phosphates are promising host materials for their easy synthesis, low cost, and chemical/thermal stabilities over a wide range of temperatures [4e6].As the dopants, trivalent rare-earth ions ( RE3+, such as Dy3+) are expected to substitute the Bi3+ sites in CagBi (PO4) 7 host lattice, because RE3+ and Bi3+þ have the same valence and almost identical ionic radii.Therefore, doping the Dy3+ activator into this structure should afford a novel efficient white-emitting phosphor.

section: Layered Crystal Structure, Color-Tunable Photoluminescence, and Excellent Thermal Stability of Mg In2P4014Phosphate-Based Phosphors Jing Zhang,<sup>†</sup> Ge-Mei Cai,*<sup>,†</sup> Lv-Wei Yang,<sup>†</sup> Zhi-Yuan Ma,<sup>†,‡</sup> and Zhan-Peng Jin<sup>†</sup> <sup>†</sup>School of Materials Science and Engineering, Education Ministry Key Laboratory of Non-ferrous Materials Science and Engineering, Central South University, Changsha410083, Hunan, China <sup>‡</sup>Department of Chemical System Engineering, The University of Tokyo, 7-3-1Hongo, Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo113-8656, Japan *S Supporting Information ABSTRACT: Single-component white phosphors stand a good chance to serve in the next-generation high-power white lightemitting diodes.Because of low thermal stability and containing lanthanide ions with reduced valence state, most of reported phosphors usually sufer unstable color of lighting for practical packaging and comparably complex synthetic processes.In this work, we present a type of novel color-tunable blue−white− yellow-emitting Mg In2P4O14 : Tm3+/ Dy3+phosphor with high thermal stability, which can be easily fabricated in air.Under UV excitation, the Mg In2P4O14 : Tm0 .02Dy0 .03 white phosphor exhibits negligible thermal-quenching behavior, with a99.5% intensity retention at150 \ C , C , relative to its initial value at room temperature.The phosphor host Mg In2P4O14 was synthesized and reported for the first time.Mg In2P4O14 crystallizes in the space group of C2/c (No.15) with a novel layered structure built of alternate anionic and cationic layers.Its disordering structure, with Mg and In atoms co-occupying the same site, is believed to facilitate the energy transfer between rare-earth ions and benefit by sustaining the luminescence with increasing temperature.The measured absolute quantum yields of Mg In2P4O14 : Dy0 .04 , Mg In2P4O14 : Tm0 .01Dy0 .04 , and Mg In2P4O14 - Tm0 .02 - Dy0 .

content: m yields of MgIn2P4O14: Dy0.04, MgIn2P4O14: Tm0.01Dy0.04, and MgIn2P4O14-Tm0.02-Dy0.03 phosphors under the excitation of 351 nm ultraviolet radiation are 70.50%, 53.24%, and 52.31%, respectively.Present work indicates that the novel layered MgIn2P4O14 is a promising candidate as a single-component white phosphor host with an excellent thermal stability for near-UV-excited whitelight-emitting diodes (wLEDs). 1.INTRODUCTION In virtue of the prominent characteristics, including high luminous eficiency, low energy consumption, high reliability, long service life and environmental friendliness, white-light emitting diodes (wLEDs) have been regarded as the next generation of solid-state lighting sources, superseding the traditional fluorescent lamps and incandescent lamps.1 There are three main methods of mixing colors to produce white light from an LED.2 The most common implementation of the commercial wLEDs is fabricated by integrating blue LED chips with the yellow phosphor YAG: Ce ( Y3Al5O12: Ce3+), but the lack of a red light component leads to a poor color rendering index (CRI).The second type of wLEDs is adopted by combining the UVLED chips with red, green, and blue (RGB) triphosphors.However, this type of wLEDs sufers from the deficient reabsorption of the emissions among the three phosphor components.

f wLEDs sufers from the deficient reabsorption of the emissions among the three phosphor components.In order to improve the quality of white light, a better wLED design that adopts single-component white phosphor and UVLED chips has been proposed, which has the advantages of high luminous eficiency, simple manufacture, comparably low cost, etc.Phosphor usually consists of a matrix or host and an activator, and sometimes a sensitizer.Most rare-earth ions with rich energy levels, as the most popular activators, can bring about various emissions over the ultraviolet−visible−near-infrared (UV-vis NIR) spectral region via f-f or d-f transitions.The function of a single-component white phosphor generally relies on their interaction, especially energy transfer, between the rare-earth ions in an appropriate host.Until now, many studies related to rare-earth-doped phosphate phosphors 3−9 have been conducted in search of novel single-component white phosphors, mainly due to high absorption in the UV region and structural diversity of the phosphate host.Nevertheless, few of them are suitable for commercial use, and most ofthese phosphors usually sufer some characteristic deficiencies, such as synthetic processing (requiringinertatmosphereprotection) and emission loss or shift with increasing temperature.Regarding the latter, the so-called “thermal quenching” (TQ) still is a key challenge for groping for novel single-component white phosphors with good thermal stability and high luminescence.TQ is often ascribed to the nonradiative relaxation ofexcited electrons to the ground state of the activator.

en ascribed to the nonradiative relaxation ofexcited electrons to the ground state of the activator.With regard to most phosphors with a single activator, TQ can be well-explained using a configurational coordinate diagram in which the excited luminescent center is thermally activated through phonon interaction and then relaxed through the crossing point between excited and ground states.10−12 In fact, TQ also is dependent on structural rigidity ofthe host, including rigid bonding networks and bond strength, which could substantially minimize the emission loss with increasing temperature.13 Very recently, the zero-thermalq uenchingbeh avi orofblue - emittingphosphor Na3-2xSc2 (PO4) 3: x Eu2+ was reported by Wang’s group and Kim’s group, respectively.14,15 They explained the compensation of emission losses due to the Na+ disordering nature by nonequivalence doping, phase transformation of host and consequent energy transfer from defect level, leading to radiative recombination.On every account, exploring a novel phosphate host with rigid bonding networks, containing disordering cationic, and receptive diverse activators favoring energy transfer could initiate the generation of color-tunable phosphors with excellent TQ behavior.Recently, we have targeted the MgO-In2O3-P2O5 ternary system for exploration of new phosphor host materials, based on the following considerations.First, magnesium and indium prefer to co-occupy the same lattice site and form a highly disordered structure, because of their similar ionic radius and coordination properties in the oxide.Second, both magnesium and indium have similar ionic radius and coordination properties to most rare-earth ions, which facilitate the substitution of diferent rare-earth dopants.Moreover, indium can form flexible coordination geometries in inorganic oxides, namely, InO tetrahedra, InO5 trigonal bipyramids, InO6 octahedra, InO pentagonal bipyramid, or InO8 dodecahedra.

rahedra, InO5 trigonal bipyramids, InO6 octahedra, InO pentagonal bipyramid, or InO8 dodecahedra.The incorporation of indium cations into phosphates can create various topologies and crystal fields, thus ofering great opportunities to design new host compounds, where the rare-earth dopants may exhibit novel luminescence properties.In this contribution, the first magnesium indium phosphate, MgIn2P4O14, was observed and confirmed in the MgO-In2O3-P2O5 system.Based on crystallographic analysis using powder Xray difraction data, the crystal structure of this compound is determined with novel layered structure in which Mg and In atoms co-occupy one special site 4e and one general site 8f.Taking into account our previous research experience, 16, 17 the blue-emitting Tm3+ ions and yellow-emitting Dy3+ ions are chosen and focused on the codoped activators through efective energy transfer to fabricate white-light emitting inorganic phosphors.Recently, Tm3+/ Dy3+-doped single-component white phosphors, such as YAl3 (BO3) 4: Tm3+ and YAl3 (BO3) 4: Dy3+(seeref18) and Ca9Y (PO4) 7: Tm3+ and Ca9Y (PO4) 7: Di y3+(seeref19), exhibit preferable color-tunable properties in white-light-emitting diodes (wLEDs).The composition- and temperature-dependent luminescent properties of Tm3+.- and Dy3+-activated MgIn2P4O14 phosphors have been systematically investigated by means of structural analysis, photoluminescence excitation (PLE), and emission (PL) spectrum, vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) excited luminescence properties, decay lifetime, and high-temperature luminescence.Present results indicate that MgIn2P4O14 is deemed to be a promising host material with good thermal stability for the preparation of white phosphors. 2.EXPERIMENTAL SECTION2.1.Sample Preparations.Pure MgIn2P4O14 polycrystalline sample and a series of Tm3+/ Dy3+ single- or co-doped phosphors Mg (In1-xTmx) 2P4O1 4 (MgInP4O14: Tmx,=0.01, 0.03, 0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.09 and r0.11 ),: Mg (In1-yDyy) 2P4O14 ( MgIn2P4O14: Dyy,: y=0.01.

.05, 0.07, 0.09 and r0.11 ),: Mg (In1-yDyy) 2P4O14 ( MgIn2P4O14: Dyy,: y=0.01.0.03, 0.04, 0.05, 0.07, 0.09 and 0.11 ), and Mg(In-x-yTmxDyy) 2P4O14 ( MgIn2P4O14; TmxDy, x=0.005-0.05, y=0.005-0.05 ) were synthesized using conventional high-temperature solid-state reaction methods.First, diferent stoichiometric amounts of starting materials MgO (99.99%), InO (99.99%), NHHPO (99.95%), Tm?O3 (99.99%), and Dy2O3 ( 99.99 % ) were ground in an agate mortar for 30 min to form homogeneous mixtures.Then, the mixtures were heated in corundum crucibles at 600C for 12 h to get the precursors.Subsquently, the precursors underwent two 24-h calcinations at 1000 °C after being ground for each time.Finally, the products were gradually cooled to room temperature in the furnace and were ground again into homogeneous powders for the following analysis.2.2.Characterization.The phase compositions ofthe samples were characterized via powder X-ray difraction (XRD) technique through an X-ray difractometer ( Rigaku, Model D/MAX-2500).Data for crystal structure determination and refinement was collected on a PANalytical powder X-ray difractometer (X’Pert Pro).The chemical compositions of the samples were measured by inductively coupled plasma−atomic emission spectrometry, using a PerkinElmer ICP/6500 spectrometer.The nominal and the measured compositions of MgIn2P4O14 and the representative Tm3+/ Dy3+ single- and co-doped MgIn2P4O14 samples determined from ICP-AES method are given in Table S1 in the Supporting Information.The measured atomic ratios of the samples are almost-ideal atomic ratios.Infrared (IR) spectrum in the wavenumber range o400-2000 cm - 1 was obtained at room temperature via a Nicolet 6700 infrared spectrophotometer with a KBr pellet as standards.Diferential thermal analysis (TG-DTA) was performed on a Netzsch Model STA449C apparatus with a heating rate of 10K/min.

analysis (TG-DTA) was performed on a Netzsch Model STA449C apparatus with a heating rate of 10K/min.Photoluminescence excitation and emission spectra at room temperature were obtained on a fluorescence spectrophotometer (Hitachi, Model F-7000) equipped with a150W Xe lamp as the excitation source.Temperature-dependence luminescence spectra (25-300C) were measured by adopting the heating apparatus (Tianjin Orient Koji Co., Ltd., TAP≈02 ).The vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) spectra at temperatures ranging from 27K to room temperature were obtained at Beamline 3B1B in Beijing Synchrotron Radiation Facilities (BSRF).Time-resolved emission decay behaviors and the quantum eficiency were evaluated on a Model FLS920n spectrometer (Edinburgh Instruments, Ltd., England) with Model μF900 lamps as the excitation source and a Model R928-PA photo multiplier as the signal detector. 3.RESULTS ANDDISCUSSION3.1.Crystal Structure and Characterization of MgInPO.3.1.1.Crystal Structure of MgIn2P4O14.Based on the powder XRD data acquired in slow-scan mode, the crystal structure ofthe new compound MgIn2P4O14 was solved by using the charge flipping method of the Jana 2006 progra m20 and refined by using the Rietveld method of the FullProfSuite program.21 In the process of refinement, a total of 64 parameters were refined, including 19 profile parameters and 45 structure parameters.The final agreement factors converged to RB=4.47%, Rp=2.08 %, Rwp=2.68 %, and S=1.29;, indicating that the determined structure should be quite credible.The detailed Rietveld refinement parameters and crystal structure data of MgIn2P4O14 are listed in Table 1.The atomic parameters of MgIn2P4O14 are given in Table S2 in the Supporting Information.Mg In2P4O14 crystallizes in the monoclinic system with the space group C2 / c ( No.15 ) and lattice parameters a=9.8733 (3) Å, b=Table 1.

of the MgIn2P4O14 cell along the b-axis, with the closed tetrahedrons representing the PO4 groups.As can be seen from the projective view along the c-axis in Figure 2a, the three-dimensional framework of MgIn2P4O14 has a layered structure that is composed of alternating anionic and cationic layers.Two adjacent [ MnO4n+2 ] layers are bridged by the vertexes of P2O7 groups.Each cationic layer comprises of countless parallel wavy chains [ MnO4n+2 ] interlinked by P2O7 groups through corner-sharing (Figure2b).In the structure, P2O7 groups play dual roles, being interchain parts in one [ MnO4n+2 ] - layer and intrachain parts in the next adjoining [ MnO4n+2 ] layer.The [ MnO4n+2 ] chain is formed by edgesharing MO6 octahedra running along the [101] direction with the repeated basic unit of - [ M2O6-MiO6-M2O6 ] - (seeFigure2c).The projection of MgIn2P4O14 along the c-axis direction is shown in Figure S1 in the Supporting Information, demonstrating long hollow tunnels surrounded by MO6 octahedra and PO4 tetrahedron in this structure.In this structure, the distances between adjacent intrachain metal cations are 3.558 and 3.423 Å for M2−M1 and M2−M2, respectively.M1−O and M2-O distances range from 2.053(9) to 2.281(9) Å and from 2.044(10) to 2.219 (8) A, respectively.Representative bond lengths and angles in MgIn2P4O14 are listed in Table S3 in the Supporting Information.Based on Brown’s bond-valence theory, the bond valence (Vcalc) of each atom MgIn2P4O14 (listedinTableS4intheSupportingInformation) were calculated using the following equation: Figure 1.Final Rietveld refinement pattern for MgIn2P4O14.The observed intensities, calculated intensities, and the diference plot are represented by the red hollow circle, black solid line, and blue solid line, respectively.The positions of all Bragg reflections are marked with the green bars.

A single-phased white-emitting Ca2Ga2GeO7Dy3+ phosphor with different charge compensation ions ZHOUJunhe (周俊鹤)1, YUXue (余 雪)1,2, WANGTing (王 婷)1, ZHOUDacheng (周大成)1,2, QIUJianbei (邱建备)1,2,* (1.College of Materials Science and Engineering, Kunming University of Science and Technology, Kunming 650093, China; 2.Key Lab of Advanced Materials in Rare & Precious and Nonferrous Metals (KunmingUniversityofScienceandTechnology), Ministry of Education, Kunming 650093, China) Received 1June 2016; revised 7November 2016Abstract: A novel white-emitting Ca2Ga2GeO7Dy3+ phosphor was synthesized via a high-temperature solid-state reaction.The crystal phase was analyzed by X-ray diffraction (XRD), and the photoluminescence (PL) properties were studied by luminescence spectra and fluorescence decay curves.Under the excitation of 347 nm, the obtained phosphor exhibited strong emission in the blue region peaked at 478 nm, yellow at 574 nm and a weak red emission band at 665 nm, corresponding to the characteristic transitions o f4F9/2 to 6H15/2, 6H13/2 and 6H11/2 of Dy3+, respectively.By varying the doping concentration of Dy3+, tunable colors from blue-white to yellow-white were obtained in the phosphors.Besides, by codoping charge compensators (Li+, Na+, K+ and Ga3+) in Ca2Ga2GeO7: Dy3- the optimum CIE color coordinate and PL intensity were obtained in Ca2Ga2GeO7: Dy3+, K+.Accordingly, the PL mechanism of Ca2Ga2GeO7: Dy3+ was discussed briefly.

content: n Ca2Ga2GeO7: Dy3+, K+.Accordingly, the PL mechanism of Ca2Ga2GeO7: Dy3+ was discussed briefly.Keywords: phosphor; luminescence; crystal structure; defects; rare earths Phosphor-converted white light-emitting diodes (pc-WLEDs), which are regarded as the next generation of light sources, have attracted significant attention for use in the lighting industry and in display systems because of their unique properties, including but not limited to high luminous efficiency, energy savings, reliability, small volume, and environment-friendliness[1−5].At present, the combination of Y3Al5O12: Ce3+( YAG: Ce ) phosphor with blue InGaN chip is most frequently used[6,7].Unfortunately, this method suffers the problems of poor color rendering index (Ra4500K), restricting their application[8,9].To solve the problems mentioned above, the near-UV white light-emitting diodes (NUVLEDs) coupled with red, green and blue trichromatic phosphors are employed, which at tract much attention during the past few years[10,11].This type of white LEDs has a high color rendering index ( Ra > 90 ) but low luminous efficiency due to the reabsorption among phosphors[12,13].In addition, the different degradation rates of the three-primary phosphors will cause color aberration, which is undesirable in practice[14,15].In these regards, a single-phased white-emitting phosphor pumped by NUVLEDs should be a good choice for phosphor-converted WLEDs, since they exhibit definite advantages, such as improved color stability, better reproducibility, and a simplified fabrication process[16].Dy3+ receives considerable attention in the field of single-phased white-emitting phosphors because of it’s dominant emission bands at blue (4F9/26H15/2) and yellow (4F9/26H13/2) emission regions of visible spectra.The blue emission hardly varies with the crystal field symmetry around the Dy3+ ion[17,18].

he blue emission hardly varies with the crystal field symmetry around the Dy3+ ion[17,18].The yellow emission, however, being a hypersensitive transition, is strongly influenced by the crystal-field environment.Accordingly, white light could be obtained with appropriate ratio of blue/yellow intensity in some special host lattices[19].As an important family of luminescent materials, germanates have attracted much attention for the use of the phosphors emitting layer of LEDs due to their high stability and reasonable conductivity as an oxide host[20–22].Ca2Ga2GeO7 host has been reported in more recent study[23], which could be a suitable host for the application in WLEDs when doped with Dy3+In this paper, a single-phased white light emitting phosphor Ca2Ga2GeO7: Dy3+ was synthesized via a high temperature solid-state method for the first time.The photoluminescence (PL) properties were investigated as potential candidate to be used in WLEDs.Moreover, the charge compensators ( Li+, Na+, K+, Ga3+) ) were added in Ca2Ga2GeO7Dy3+ phosphor and the effects of which on the PL properties were studied. 1Experimental A series of Ca2-xGa2GeO7zxDy3+( x=0.01, 0.02, 0.03,.0.05, 0.07 and 0.09) phosphors were synthesized by a traditional high-temperature solid-state reaction.Ca CO3 (99.99%), Ga2O3 (99.99%), GeO2 (99.99%) and Dy2O3 (99.99%) were employed as starting materials.The mixtures were first mixed and ground in an agate mortar for 30 min, and then sintered in air at 1100C for 5.5 h.The as prepared phosphors were cooled to the room temperature and reground for further researches.The Li+Na+, K+ and Ga3+ ions co-doped samples were prepared in the same way except for adding additional stoichiometry amounts of Li2CO3 (99.99%), Na2CO3 (99.99%), and K2CO33 (99.99%) and Ga2O3 (99.99%).The phases of the obtained samples were identified by X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) with CuKα (λ=0.15418 nm) radiation at a scanning step of 0.

ified by X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) with CuKα (λ=0.15418 nm) radiation at a scanning step of 0.02 in the 2θ range from 10 to 80o operating at 36 kV and 30 mA (Rigaku Model D/max-2200).The photoluminescence excitation (PLE) and PL spectra were recorded using a Hitachi F-7000 fluorescence spectrophotometer with a photomultiplier tube operating at 400V, and a150-WXe lamp was used as the excitation lamp.Photoluminescence quantum efficiency was measured by an FLS-920T fluorescence spectrophotometer equipped with a450W xenon light source ( ex=347 nm, em=574 nm).The PL decay curves were measured by an FLS980 fluorescence spectrophotometer. 2Results and discussion The XRD patterns of Ca1.97Ga2Ge O7.0.03Dy3+, Ca1.91 Ga2GeO7:0.09Dy3+, Ca1.94Ga2GeO7:0.03Dy3+, 0.03R+ (R=Li, Na, K) and Ca1.97Ga2.03Ge0.97O7: 0.03Dy3+ are shown in Fig.1(a).By comparing with JCPDSCard No.38-1328, which is also plotted in Fig.1(a), all the observed diffraction peaks can be indexed to the pure phase of Ca2Ga2GeO7.No phase transformation or impurity is observed in the current range of doping concentration.Fig.1(b) shows the crystal structure of Ca2Ga2GeO7 which belongs to the tetragonal with space group P421m (113).There are one Ca2+ site (surroundedbysixO2-ions), two Ga3+ sites (surroundedbyfourO2-ions) and one Ge4+ site (surroundedbyfourO2-ions) in the compound Ca2Ga2GeO7.Based on the effective ionic radii (r) of cations with different coordination numbers (CN) reported by Shannon [ 24 ], we propose that Dy3+(CN=6, r=0.091 nm), Li+ (CN=6, r=0.076 nm), Na+ (CN=6, r=0.102 nm) and K+ (CN=6, r=0.138 nm) will occupy Ca2+ ( CN=6, r=0.1 nm) sites and Ga3+(CN=4, r=0.047 nm) will occupy Ge4+(CN=4, r=0.039 nm) sites preferably because of their similar ionic radius.Fig.2 exhibits the PLE and PL spectra of Ca1.97Ga2Ge O7.0.03Dy3+.

e of their similar ionic radius.Fig.2 exhibits the PLE and PL spectra of Ca1.97Ga2Ge O7.0.03Dy3+.Monitored at 574 nm, the PLE spectrum clearly demonstrates that there are some intense and sharp lines between 300 and 430 nm, which are assigned to the ff transitions of Dy3+.The excitation peaks are located at 324, 347, 362, 386, and 426 nm, corresponding to the transitions from the ground state 6H15/2 to 6P3/2, 6P7/2, 6P5/2, 4I13/2 and 4G11/2, respectively[25].Besides, Ga3+- O2- transition band peaked at 285 nm can also be observed in the PLE spectrum[26].Under the excitation of 347 nm, the PL spectrum exhibits strong emission in the blue region peaked at 478 nm, yellow at 574 nm and a weak red emission band peaking at 665 nm, corresponding to the characteristic transitions of 4F9/2 to 6H15/2, 6H13/2 and 6H11/2 of Dy3++, respectively.Besides, the peak at about 488 nm maybe result from the splitting of energy level for Dy3+ in the transitions of 4F9/2 t o6H15/2.
