content: - 1 ) are determined by employing Auzel’s model.The chromaticity coordinates ( x=0.288, y=0.338 ), correlated color temperature (7760K) and quantum efficiency value (95%) indicate towards a cool and efficient white light emanating CagBi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 nanophosphor.The crystal and optical properties of the prepared nanophosphor vividly define its potential usage as ultraviolet triggered white light emitting source for lighting applications 1.Introduction Life on earth has been evolving in the presence of natural light for ages.The discovery of fire was a major breakthrough in the field of lighting.The primary artificial light sources used natural gas and oil.Ever since mankind has strived to create advanced and brighter light sources.The continuous efforts led to different new inventions such as producing light artificially by means of incandescent bulbs, metal halide lamps, sodium discharge lamps and compact fluorescent light (CFL) bulbs that not only enhanced working capacity of humans but also enriched the scientific world with excellent innovations [1,2].After mid-20th century the world population took a boom, so the demand of worldwide energy is almost bound to intensify.The scientists faced a challenge to maintain the balance between novelty and energy efficiency of the technologies developed [3].The exploration of rare earth doped nanophosphors as luminescent materials is an example of such a balance.These are known to have wide applications in solid-state laser, solar cells and light emitting diodes etc [4,5].The luminescent rare earth doped nanophosphors are used in combination with UV or NUV chip to fabricate an artificial, durable, cost effective, robust and advanced light source namely white light emitting diode (WLED) [6].The UV/NUV chip is either combined with a single white light emitting nanophosphor or with a group of individual red, green and blue emitting nanophosphors to produce white light [7,8].

with a group of individual red, green and blue emitting nanophosphors to produce white light [7,8].The fabrication through combination of three different color emitting substances is difficult as well as suffer from shortcomings such as degradation of color with time.It is due to difficulties involved in determining afterglow decay process for various components.Therefore, a single type of luminescent component (suchasDy3+) emanating white light through combination of its different color emitting peaks, is preferred.The involvement of a single type of luminescent center/ion leads to equivalent decay process and afterglow color shows no change with time [9,10].This novel approach in fabrication leads to high CRI values and a uniform behavior in spectral distribution [11,12].An appropriate correlated color temperature (CCT) value and an efficient absorption in UV or NUV region also aid to efficiency of white light emitted.Hence, there lies a great opportunity to explore and develop novel phosphor materials with high chemical stability, effective UV absorption and excellent luminescence exhibition to be used for lighting applications.The nanophosphor materials demand to have an appropriate host material with an efficient luminescent center.Rare-earth metals that absorb well in UV or NUV region and emit white light as a single luminescent unit, are introduced in the host lattice as dopants [13–15].The host is selected in a manner to give stability and uniform color emission to the nanophosphor.In order to accomplish that multiple oxide-based nanophosphors such as nitrides, sulphides, borates and vanadates have been studied [16–18].The vanadates as host help achieve the synthesis at lower temperature and provide stable crystal structure and high luminous efficiency.The vanadate group is capable of absorbing and transferring the radiation energy to the luminescent center [19].The Dy3+ ions absorb in UV region and display white emission due to characteristic 4F9/26H11/2 transitions [20, 21].

bsorb in UV region and display white emission due to characteristic 4F9/26H11/2 transitions [20, 21].Thus, doping a vanadate-based host with trivalent dysprosium ions can lead to a stable, efficient and bright white color emitting nanophosphor to be used as phosphor component in WLEDs.In2001, Evans et al.synthesized CaA (VO4) 7 ( A=Bi or RE) type nanophosphors by means of conventional solid-state method at 700C (6h) and 900 ◦C (10h) of temperatures [22].In the author’ knowledge, no work on trivalent dysprosium doped CagBi (VO4) 7 nanophosphor has been conveyed.In the present report, Dy3+ doped CagBi (VO4) 7 nanophosphor is synthesized for the very first time by means of time efficient route of solution combustion synthesis at low calcination temperature of 900C within 3 h.A detailed analysis of the crystal structure and luminescent properties of Dy3+ doped Ca9Bi (VO4) 7 nanophosphor has been carried out.The Rietveld refinement of the synthesized nanophosphor has been exclusively performed.An economic and time saving route of urea-assisted solution combustion synthesis has been followed to prepare the mono-phased Ca9Bi (VO4) 7: Dy3+ nanophosphor series.Urea is employed as a fuel due to presence of amino-acid group that makes it behave as a complexing vehicle for metal ions in the solution involved.The nanophosphors are characterized in numerous ways in order to attain information of the different aspects.The phase purity of the synthesized nanophosphor series is confirmed as the recorded X-ray diffraction patterns are in agreement to the standard JCPDS data of CagBi (VO4) 7 host.It is found by means of Rietveld refinement that both pure host CagBi (VO4) 7 and doped composition CagBi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 crystallize in trigonal system and R3c (161) space group symmetry.The lattice parameters are a=(4) Å, b=(4) Å, c=38.0793 (23) A,=90,=90,=120., V=3904.98A3 and z=6 for Ca9Bi080 (VO4) 7: 0.20Dy3+ nanophosphor.

=90,=90,=120., V=3904.98A3 and z=6 for Ca9Bi080 (VO4) 7: 0.20Dy3+ nanophosphor.The Bi3+ ions are replaced by Dy3+ ions as obvious from similar charge and ionic radii of the ions.Also, the sintering behavior of Ca9Bi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 -the best luminescent composition is studied at different temperature values.The energy band-gap value is attained for host Ca9Bi (VO4) 7 from Diffuse reflectance spectra.The doped composition is analyzed through transmission electron microscopy (TEM) for morphological analysis.The excitation-emission and decay curves of the synthesized nanophosphor series are studied in detail.The radiative, non-radiative lifetimes and quantum efficiency values for 4F9/2 quantum mechanical state are also investigated.The CIE chromaticity coordinates and correlated color temperature (CCT) approve the Ca9Bi080 (VO4) 7: 0.20Dy3+ nanophosphor to be a cool white light emitting component for UV absorbing white light emitting diodes (WLEDs) for lighting applications. 2.Experimenta 2.1.Materials and synthesis The mono-phased white light emitting Ca9Bi (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7 nanophosphor series has been prepared through solution combustion synthesis that is an energy efficient and time saving route.Due to the aforementioned qualities of the route followed, the products obtained are highly crystalline and homogenous [23,24].First of all, chemicals such as Ca (NO3) 24H2O (Central Drug House, CDH, 99.10%), Bi (NO3) 3 ⋅5H O (CDH, 99.8%), Dy(NO).xH O (Sigma Aldrich, 99.9%), NH4VO3 (CDH, 99%) and urea (CDH, 99.5%) have been procured from the chemical suppliers.The metal nitrates (oxidizers) and ammonium vanadate were weighed in a stoichiometric accordance so that the oxidizer to fuel ratio become unity.Deionized water was taken in minimal amount in a pyrex-beaker (250mL) as solvent for the properly weighed reactants.The beaker along with its contents was put on a hot plate set at 150C for 5 min.

rly weighed reactants.The beaker along with its contents was put on a hot plate set at 150C for 5 min.The solution turned homogeneous and the beaker was then put in a muffle furnace set at 500C for half an hour.The solution inside the beaker transformed into voluminous powder that was provided with room temperature in order to cool it down.The powder was finely crushed and moved to an alumina crucible that was put in a muffle furnace providing a temperature of 900C for 3 h.The product obtained was subjected to room temperature and then finely crushed to powder form.The powder was stored in a desiccator so as to undergo characterization procedure.All the compositions were prepared in the above manner and the formation of optimal composition Ca9Bi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 involved the following chemical equation: 9Ca (NO3) 24H2O + (1-x) Bi (NO3) 35H2O + x Dy (NO3) 3 x H2O+ (NO3) 2D + O (1) 37N H4VO3+ 14N H2CONH2Ca9Bi (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7.+ gaseous products (mixture of CO2, H2O and N2). 2.2.Methods of characterization The structural analysis of complete nanophosphor series CaB- i (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7 ( x=0.05-0.3 ) was performed through diffraction patterns displayed by individual compositions.In order to record the X-Ray diffraction patterns a high-resolution X-ray powder diffractometer -Rigaku Ultima-IV with CuKα irradiating X-Rays and a scintillation counter as detector was employed.The diffraction patterns of the complete nanophosphor series Ca9Bi (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7 ( x=0.05-0.3 ) were documented in an angular range from 10◦ to 80◦ at scanning rate of 2 per minute.A software named as General Structure Analysis System (GSAS) was utilized to perform Rietveld refinement of host and optimal composition.In present case, Pseudo-Voigt function was employed for the pattern fitting of XRD peaks.A transmission electron microscope (TEM) labeled as FEITecnaiTF20 with a70 tilted stage was used for TEM and HRTEM imaging.

microscope (TEM) labeled as FEITecnaiTF20 with a70 tilted stage was used for TEM and HRTEM imaging.It was fitted with a high brightness field-emission gun (FEG) and 200 kV been the maximum acceleration voltage.Hitachi F – 7000-a fluorescence spectrophotometer fitted with a Xenon lamp (sourceofexcitation) recorded both excitation and emission spectra.The decay curves and excitation-emission spectra of complete CagBi (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7 ( x=0.05-0.3 ) nanophosphor series were documented at working conditions as photomultiplier tube (PMT) Voltage=400V, excitation-emission slit widths=2.5 nm each and scanning rate=1200 nm/min.The diffuse reflectance spectrum of host- Ca9Bi (VO4) 7 was obtained for wavelength range 200–800 nm through Shimadzu UV–3600Plus (UV–Vis–NIR) ultra-violet–visible–near-infrared spectrophotometer taking Barium Sulphate as reference.The chromaticity coordinates of the Ca9Bi (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7 ( x=0.05-0.3 ) nanophosphor series were obtained using MATLAB software package.The CIE1931 (Commission International DeI’Eclairage) chromaticity diagram was used to display the coordinates of optimal luminescent composition Ca9Bi1.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7.The correlated color temperature (CCT) values were also determined. 3.Results and discussion 3.1.Structural studies A time saving route of solution combustion synthesis has been used to prepare the complete nanophosphor series Ca9Bi (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7 ( x=0.05 – 0.3 ).The pure host and doped compositions have been subjected to X-ray analysis and their diffraction patterns are documented.The X-ray diffraction patterns displayed by Ca9Bi (1-x) Dyx (VO4) 7 ( x=0.0.3 ) nanophosphors are in close agreement to the standard JCPDS card no.46–0404 for pure host Ca9Bi (VO4) 7 prototype (Fig.1).It implies to the trigonal phase and R3c (161) space group of the synthesized nanophosphors.The sintering behavior of Ca9Bi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 nanophosphor has been studied for thermal aspects as given in S.1.

r of Ca9Bi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 nanophosphor has been studied for thermal aspects as given in S.1.Due to similar charges and ionic radii the dopant Dy3+ ions are supposed to replace Bi3+ ions in the host.The aforementioned statement can be validated by calculation of radius percentage difference (r) as follows: r=Rm (CN) - Rd (CN)Rm (CN) 1001In above equation, r signifies the radius percentage difference, Rm (CN) represents the effective ionic radii for host ions, Rd (CN) denotes the effective ionic radii for dopant ions while CN signifies the respective coordination numbers of particular ions.In the present case both Dy3+ and Bi3+ are octa-coordinated ( CN=8 ).The value of radius percentage difference (r) is calculated to be 12.2% whereas the acceptable value for r is less than 30% [ 25, 26 ].Thus, the substitution of Bi3+ by Dy3+ ions has been confirmed.The odds for Ca2+ or V5+ being replaced by Dy3+ are not there because of being dissimilar in their charge, size and large value of radius percentage difference.Rietveld refinement has been performed on the X-ray diffraction patterns of synthesized nanophosphor compositions namely CaBi (VO4) 7 and Ca9Bi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 7 as depicted in Fig.2 and Fig.3, respectively.There are three types of lines present in the refinement– a solid red line displaying experimental XRD pattern, a black diamond shaped line signifying observed XRD pattern and a blue line showing the difference between the prior mentioned two lines.The Ca9Bi (VO4) 7 and Ca9Bi0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 compositions have been refined to 2 value of 2.186 and 2.118, respectively.The Rietveld refinement of CagB – i0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 has led to different lattice parameters such as a=b=(4) A, c=38.0793 (23) Å and V=3904..98 (26) A3 (Table1).There is a similarity between crystallization of CagBi (VO4) 7 and Ca9B- i0.80Dy0.20 (VO4) 7 as both crystallizes in trigonal system and R3c (161) space group symmetry with==90,=120 and Z=6..

Inorganic luminescent materials have historically attracted considerable attention due to their characteristics such as long decay lifetime [1], easy preparation, low toxicity, and high luminous efficiency [2–4].Rare earth luminescent materials have considerable application potential because of their unique 4f orbit, which can be pumped to excited energy levels to emit colorful light under excitation [5,6].Among them, the emission of Dy3+ is mainly from the yellow–orange region ( 570 – 600 nm) with 4F9/26H13/2 transition [7], and 4F9/26H15/2 transition at the blue region (470–500 nm) [8].At a sufficient yellow–blue intensity ratio, Dy3+ can also emit white light [9].The excitation spectrum of Dy3+ consists only of narrow f–f transition lines with low oscillation intensity due to the characteristics of the 300–500 nm parity selection rule (Dy3+chargetransferabsorptionbandsor4f84f75dbandsbelow200nm).Effective energy transfer from the matrix to the Dy3+ ions is one of the most relevant methods to achieve efficient emission of Dy3+ ions in the matrix sensitization of Dy3+ ions [10].The luminescent properties of phosphors are affected by the doped rare earth ions, as well as the structure and composition of the substance host [11,12].Tungstate materials are considered to be effective self-activated fluorescent materials with high-absorption cross-sections [13,14], broadband emissions [15], and high quantum efficiency [16,17].To fix the weak f–f transitions in trivalent rare earth ions, self-activating compounds may also serve as matrix sensitizers.The lattice of matrix material not only affects the dopant’s optical transition, but also reduces its excitation energy [18].Among various matrix materials, phosphate has a wide band gap and high efficiency, with KEYWORDS: Ca19Zn2 (PO4) 14, white-emitting, rare earth, cation substitution, crystal field environment, luminescence enhancement 1.INTRODUCTION White light-emitting diodes (w-LEDs), due to their high eficiency, low pollution, and long operating life, have been widely applied as a new generation of lighting sources.1−4 Currently, two main w-LEDs manufacturing methods have been studied: (i) the most commercial way is combining YAG: Ce3+ yellow phosphor with blue GaInN chips,5−8 but it is dificult to solve the defects of low color rendering index (CRI) and high correlated color temperature (CCT) caused by the absence of the red component;9−11 (ii) the approach exciting the trichromatic phosphors with near-ultraviolet (n-UV) chip have also attracted much attention,12,13 but problems such as low luminescence eficiency due to the reabsorption between phosphors would limit its further development.14−16 Furthermore, w-LEDs can be obtained by exciting singlecomponent white-emitting phosphors with UV/n-UV chips and are considered to possess potential development prospects.17,18 Until now, it has been reported that some white-emitting phosphors can be realized by introducing rare earth ion and transition metal ion activators into the structure, such as Eu2+/ Eu3+, 19Eu2+/ Mn2+, 20, 21 and Ce3+/ Tb3+/ Mn2+ 22-24However, the phenomenon of energy loss in the energy transfer process is inevitable.Therefore, investigating novel single-component white-emitting phosphors with excellent luminescence performance remains important.

stays neutral with regard to jurisdictional claims in published maps and institutional affiliations.Abstract: Optical absorption spectra and luminescence spectra were recorded as a function of temperature between 295K and 800K for single crystal samples of Gd2SiO5Dy3+, Lu2SiO5Dy3+LiNbO3: Dy3+, and Gd3Ga3Al2O12: Dy3+ fabricated by the Czochralski method and of YAl3 (BO3) 4: Dy3+ fabricated by the top-seeded high temperature solution method.A thermally induced change of fluorescence intensity ratio (FIR) between the 4I15/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H15/2 emission bands of Dy3+ was inferred from experimental data.It was found that relative thermal sensitivities SR at 350K are higher for YAl3 (BO3) 4: Dy3+ and Lu2SiO5: Dy3++than those for the remaining systems studied.Based on detailed examination of the structural peculiarities of the crystals it was ascertained that the observed difference between thermosensitive features cannot be attributed directly to the dissimilarity of structural factors consisting of the geometry and symmetry of Dy3+ sites, the number of non-equivalent Dy3+ sites, and the host anisotropy.Instead, it was found that a meaningful correlation between relative thermal sensitivity SR and rates of radiative transitions of Dy3+ inferred from the Judd–Ofelt treatment exists.It was concluded that generalization based on the Judd–Ofelt parameters and luminescence branching ratio analysis may be useful during a preliminary assessment of thermosensitive properties of new phosphor materials.Keywords: luminescence; Dy-doped crystals; optical temperature sensors 1.Introduction The remote temperature readout is a useful and meaningful method, and consequently, great attention has been addressed towards distinct advanced luminescence thermometers.For this purpose, various sophisticated luminescence systems and temperature sensor techniques have been proposed and elaborated on within the last decade.

stems and temperature sensor techniques have been proposed and elaborated on within the last decade.The luminescence sensors, in the form of lanthanide-doped optical systems, quantum dots, organic fluorophores, or biomolecules, may be applied as potential luminescence thermometers and their temperature-dependent spectroscopic peculiarities and sensing capabilities have been reported and compared in the comprehensive review papers, e.g., [1–5].A temperature readout above a thousand degrees is possible for limited luminescence systems, but inorganic amorphous materials or lanthanide-doped crystals showing efficient emission within wide UV-Vis-NIR spectral regions can be satisfactorily utilized there, in contrast to fluorophores or bio-molecules, which are susceptible to destruction [6–15].In the present work we deal with the thermosensitive properties of Dy3+-doped oxide crystals.Their advantage over other rare-earth-doped phosphors stems from a specific energy level scheme of the Dy3+ ions, in which the energy separation between the 4F9/2 luminescent level and the next lower-energy dysprosium excited state is considerable, approaching 7000 cm−1.As a consequence, the contribution of adverse multiphonon relaxation is substantially suppressed and the quantum efficiency of the 4F9/2 luminescence is significant and weakly affected by the temperature for the most optical materials doped with dysprosium when the luminescence admixture concentration is adequately restricted [16].With respect to the structural and optical properties of the host, the visible emission of the dysprosium can be differently distributed within blue, green, and red spectral regions, and, consequently, these individual materials’ spectroscopic characteristics influence the resulting phosphor color.The diverse phosphor materials containing Dy3+ ions, e.g., single-doped with Dy3+[17], double-doped with Dy+Mn [18], Dy+Eu [19], or triple-doped with Dy+Eu+Tb [20], have been described in numerous recent papers point ing out their utility for the design of novel lighting devices.

RESEARCHARTICLELUMINESCENCEWILEYGreen synthesis, structure feature and energy transfer of yellow-emitting ( Y, Gd ) 2O2S O4: Dy phosphors Xiaolong Yang 1,2 | Bin Lu1,3 | Xinyuan Wang 1 | Yoshio Sakka 4 1School of Materials Science and Chemica Engineering, Ningbo University, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China 2College of Science & Technology, Ningbo University, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China 3Key Laboratory of Photoelectric Detection Materials and Devices of Zhejiang Province, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China 4Research Center for Functional Materials, National Institute for Materials Science, Tsukuba, Ibaraki, Japan Correspondence Bin Lu, School of Materials Science and Chemical Engineering, Ningbo University, Ningbo, Zhejiang 315211, China.Email: lvbin@nbu.edu.cn Funding information National Natural Science Foundation of China, Grant/Award Number: 51702171 Abstract A green chemical precipitation route was used to yield a hydrated basic sulfate precursor upon calcination at 1000C into a series of ( Y, Gd ) 2O2S O4: Dy particles.The phosphors exhibited characteristic Dv3+ emissions from 4F9/26H J ( J=15/2, 13/2, 11/2) transitions under ultraviolet light excitation; the quenching concentration of Dv3+ was determined to be 2.5 at.%.Substitution of Gd3+ for Y3+ led to an additional strong sharp band at 277 nm (8S7/26IJtransitionofGd3+) in the photoluminescence excitation spectra, upon which the ( Gd0.975Dy0.025 ) 2O2S O4 phosphor achieved a 2.8-fold higher photoluminescence intensity via an effective energy transfer from Gd3+ to Dy3+ compared with the 354 nm excitation of Dv3+.Both the photoluminescence and photoluminescence excitation intensities of ( Y, Gd ) 2O2S O4; Dy phosphors increased with rising Gd3+ concentration and calcination temperature in the range 750–1000C.

KEYWORDS energy transfer, gadolinium oxysulfate, phosphor, yttrium oxysulfate 1 | INTRODUCTIONThe development of high-definition display systems overwhelmingly requires phosphors with sufficient brightness, high resolution, and long-term stability.Particle properties such as morphology, size, and dispersion significantly affect luminescence behaviour.Spherical particles are readily stacked into dense phosphor layers and are capable of minimizing diffuse reflection from their surfaces.[1] An ultrafine particle size is beneficial for small-sized pixels to improve resolution display.A good dispersion and a narrow size distribution would provide uniform luminescence over the whole phosphor screen.[2,3] Rare-earth oxysulfate-based (Ln2O2SO4) materials with good chemical and thermal stabilities have extensive application in various fields[4] such as fluorescence,[5] scintillation,[6] oxygen storage,[7–9] electrochemical sensing,[10] as catalysts,[11] and for temperature sensitivity,[12] and also as the intermediate phase for the target oxidation product of Ln2O3 or reduction product of Ln2O2S.

as the intermediate phase for the target oxidation product of Ln2O3 or reduction product of Ln2O2S.L [ 8 ] Y2O2SO4 and Gd2O2SO4 are two typical oxysulfates that both belong to monoclinic crystal systems an can be used as excellent matrix materials for highly effective downconversion and upconversion luminescence due to their high absorption cross-section and low phonon energy.[12–17] The latter has a relatively high theoretical density compared with the former, as Gd3+ is much heavier than Y3+Moreover, Gd3+ possesses a large magnetic moment (7BperGd3+) due to its seven unpaired 4f electrons, leading to ideal paramagnetism.[18] The Gd2O2SO4 matrix has been found to be an excellent candidate for use in optical material, as biological labels, in nuclear reactor pipes, or in magnetic refrigeration.Kharieky and colleagues compared three Sm3-+-activated Gd2O3, Gd2O2S, and Gd2O2SO4 samples, and found that the Gd2O2SO4;:Sm nanocrystalline powder exhibited 1.2-fold and 4-fold stronger X-ray excited luminescence intensities compared with the two Gd2O2S: Sm and Gd2O3:Sm in contrast, respectively.[19] This result further demonstrated that the Gd2O2SO4 host is more suitable for scintillation applications in medical and industrial X-ray digital imaging examination systems.Dy3+-activated phosphors generally present three characteristic luminescence colours in the visible region including 483 nm blue (4F9/26H15/2transition), 672 nm red (4F9/26H11/2transition), and 575 nm yellow (4F9/26H13/2transition) emissions, among which the 4F9/26H11/2, 15/2 transitions correspond to magnetic dipole transitions, while the 4F9/2→6H13/2 transition is an electricdipole transition.[20] More importantly, Dy3+ emission was shown to be significantly increased when Gd3+ was used as a sensitizer via effective Gd3+Dy3+ energy transfer in oxide and garnet lattices.[21,22] The role of Gd3+ in Dy3++-activated oxysulfates still needs to be further investigated.

p> The role of Gd3+ in Dy3++-activated oxysulfates still needs to be further investigated.Particle properties are strongly affected by the preparation strategy used and various routes have been adopted for the synthesis of rare-earth oxysulfates including combustion,[23,24] solvothermal synthesis,[25,26] solid-state reactions,[27,28] template synthesis,[29,30] and electrospinning[31].These methods generally need/release polluting gases or are uncontrollable on particle performance.A wet chemical method is superior in terms of simple operation, low cost, controllable size/morphology, and is more environmentally friendly for the preparation of sulfocompounds.In the present work, a series of ( Y, Gd ) 2O2S O4: Dy phosphor powders was synthesized using a green chemical precipitation route plus pyrolysis.The role of Gd3+ in structural features, or particle morphologies and its photoluminescence properties were studied using the combined techniques of Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffractometry (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), thermogravimetry (TG), photoluminescence excitation/ photoluminescence (PLE/PL) spectroscopy, and fluorescence decay text systems. 2 | EXPERIMENTALStarting materials were commercial Gd2 (SO4) 38H2O (99.99% pure; Haoke Technology Co., Ltd, Beijing, China), 2 (504) 38H20 (99.99% pure; Haoke Technology Co., Ltd, Beijing, China) and Dy (NO3) 36H2O (99.99% purity; Diyang Chemical Co., Ltd, Shanghai, China).These raw materials were together dissolved in distilled water ( 18MΩ) to make a mother liquor (0.02M for total cationic concentration) according to the following two stoichiometric cationic ratios: (Gd1-xDyx) 2O2S O4 ( x=0.001-0.075 ) for optimizing activator concentration and ( 1-x GdxDy0.025 ) 2O2S O4 ( x=0-1 ) for studying compositional effect.A white suspension was obtained by dropwise addition of 1.0M ammonia water into the as-prepared mother liquor at a rate of 3 ml/ min up to pH=8.0.

Hydrothermal synthesis and luminescent properties of Ca3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ white-emitting phosphors Xiaofang Yu, Dengwen Yuan, Xiaoyun MiSchool of Materials Science and Engineering, Changchun University of Science and Technology, Changchun, 130022, People’s Republic of China articleinfo Article history: Received 24May 2020Received in revised form 30September 2020Accepted 12October 2020Available online 13October 2020Keywords: Hydrothermal synthesis Ca (PO): Dy3þ phosphors Morphology Luminescence properties abstract The white-emitting Ca3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ phosphors were prepared via hydrothermal synthesis.The phosphors were characterized by XRD, TEM, SEM, EDS, GSAS structural refinement and PL spectroscopy, respectively.Rietveld refinement demonstrated that the Ca3 (PO4) 2 crystal structure consisted of [PO ] tetrahedrons filled with Ca atoms.Dy3+ ions occupied high-symmetry sites due to the emission intensity of 4F9/26H15/2 was strongest.Moreover, the pH value and calcination temperature had important effects on the phosphor morphology and luminescent properties.The morphology of the samples changed from long-rod to short-rod and sphere and the size reduced as the pH value in the initial reaction solution increased.The samples with pH of 7 had the best luminescence properties, and the precursor before calcination corresponded to Ca4P2O9.With the calcination temperature of the precursor with pH of 7 increased, the phosphor morphology changed from nanorods to grains with diameters of about 1 m, and the luminescence properties were improved continuously.The CIE coordinate of Ca (PO): Dy3+ phosphor was (0.283, 0.343).The Ca3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ phosphor has better application prospects for white light-emitting diodes. 1.

content: r application prospects for white light-emitting diodes. 1.Introduction Nowadays, white light-emitting diodes (W-LEDs) with long lifetime, high luminous efficiency, environmental friendliness and energy-saving capability are widely used in solid-state lighting [1e4].At present, there are three combinations of W-LEDs in commercial manufacturing: One is a blue LED chip with 3Al5012Ce3+ phosphors.Due to lack of red component, the LEDs have low color rendering index [5].One is red/ green/ blue (RGB) trichromatic LEDs, which have unstable color correlation temperature (CCT) and high manufacturing costs, because it is difficult for different components to have a consistent afterglow decay process [6].The other is an ultraviolet (UV) LED chip with RGB phosphors.The LEDs have poor luminous efficiency because the combination of three phosphors reabsorbs the emitted light [7,8].To overcome these disadvantages, the study of single-component white-lightemitting phosphors excited by a near-UV chip has become imperative.And the phosphor has the advantages of high efficiency, low manufacturing costs and better color quality, which can also avoid reabsorption.There are two methods for obtaining singlecomponent white-light-emitting phosphors.One is to introduce sensitizers and activators into the matrix to obtain white light through energy transfer between them, such as Eu2+ to Mn2+ ions [9e11] and Ce3+ to Tb3+ ions [12e14].The other is to introduce Dy3+ ions with a4f electron configuration into the matrix.Dy3+ ions with 4f-4f transformation characteristics are shielded by 5s and 5p outer electrons, causing them difficult to be influenced by the host lattice ligands.Dy3+ ions emit white light due to the blue (4F9/26H15/2transition) and yellow (4F9/26H13/2transition) emission bands.The 4F9/2H15/2 transition is magnetic-dipole transition and the emission intensity is almost unaffected by the host.The 4F9/26H13/2 transition is hypersensitive transition, which emission intensity is strongly sensitive to the local symmetry environment [15,16].

this paper, the white-emitting Ca3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ phosphors were prepared via hydrothermal synthesis.We systematically studied the changes of phase structure, morphology, luminescent properties of the phosphor by controlling pH value and calcination temperature.And the formation mechanism of Ca3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ phosphors under different pH condition was investigated.Our study provides a reference for the changes of various morphology and particle sizes of Ca3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ phosphors in hydrothermal synthesis, and the phosphors have better application prospects in white light-emitting diodes. 2.1.Preparation The Ca3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ phosphors were synthesized by hydrothermal synthesis.Stoichiometric Ca (NO3) 24H2O (AR) was dissolved in deionized water.Moreover, stoichiometric DyO (99.99%) was dissolved in extra HNO3 (AR) solution at 80C until completely dissolved.After mixing Ca (NO3) 2 and Dy (NO3) 3 solutions by stirring for 5 min, stoichiometric H3PO4 (AR) solution was added.The ammonia solution was added cautiously for adjusting the pH values, and continuously stirred the solution for 25 min.The precipitates were placed into a100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave and maintained at 180C for 24 h.After cooling, the precipitates were washed three cycles with deionized water, centrifuged and dried in air at 80C for 24 h.Lastly, the resultant powder with a small amount of NH4H2PO4 ( ( 99 % ) was calcined for 3 h to obtain the final product.The Sr3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ and Ba3 (PO4) 2Dy3+ phosphors were obtained analogously by using Sr (NO3) 24H2O (AR), BaNO3 ) 24H20 (AR) and Dy2O3 ( 99.99 % ) as raw materials. 2.2.Characterization The phase structure of the samples was characterized by a Rigaku D/ max-IIB diffractometer (=1.

ccurs due to Ca2+ ions and PO43-, Ca3 (PO4) 2 and CaO react to form CaPO.When the concentration of Hþ is high, ionization reaction is suppressed resulting in the suppression of the formation of PO43-, and the formation of Ca3 (PO4) 2 is inhibited, making the formation of Ca4P2O9 difficult [33].Therefore, when the pH value is 6, the solution has higher Hþ and metal ion concentrations, and lower growth rate of Ca4P2O9..The faster ion motion makes it easier for ions to transfer to large particles, and because the surface energy of the crystal is different, these particles grow in a specific direction to form nanorods [34,35].As the pH value increases, the solution has higher OH and lower H+ concentrations, the ionization reaction is promoted which contributes to the formation of PO3-.Then the solution contains higher concentrations of (PO4) 3-and OH- ions, while formation of insoluble hydroxides by metal ions makes it difficult for the ions transfer.The metal cation concentration decreases and the ion motions slow down which reduce the growth rate of the crystal in a particular direction.When the pH value is 9, the solution has higher OH concentrations, forming insoluble hydroxides with metal ions.The solution has lower metal ion concentrations causing ion motions slow down which makes it harder for ions to transfer to large particles.And the slower ion motion makes it difficult for particles to grow in a specific direction.Thus, a large number ofshort nanorods and a few nano-spherical grains are formed at pH of 9.Therefore, the pH value has a major impact on the morphology of the phosphor. Original Research Paper Luminescent kinetics of Dy3+ doped CaZn2 (PO4) 2 phosphors for white light emitting applications T.Krishnapriya, Adon Jose, Twinkle Anna Jose, Cyriac Joseph, N.V.Unnikrishnan, P.R.Biju ⇑ School of Pure &Applied Physics, Mahatma Gandhi University, Kottayam, Kerala, India articleinfo Article history: Received 15September 2020Received in revised form 21January 2021Accepted 2February 2021Available online 2March 2021Keywords: Phosphor Luminescence Solid state reaction method Judd- Ofelt analysis WLEDsabstractIn the present work, we have synthesized a series of Ca (1-X) Zn2 (PO4) 2X Dy3+( X=0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10) white light emitting phosphors via solid state reaction method.We account the structural and photoluminescence properties of all the prepared samples.The formation of CaZn2 (PO4) 2 was confirmed through X-ray diffraction and Fourier transform infrared spectra analyses.The luminescence properties of the phosphor materials were investigated through optical absorption and photoluminescence studies.The details of radiative properties were obtained through Judd- Ofelt intensity parameters and they were found to follow the trend 2 > 4 > 6..The samples were efficiently excited under near ultraviolet radiations to get excellent white light emission in terms of color rendering and luminous efficacy.Photo luminescent spectra of all the samples exhibit two prominent peaks in blue (474nm) and yellow (572nm) regions corresponding to the transitions 4F9/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 respectively.It is also revealed that the luminescence intensity is maximum for the sample Ca (0.96) Zn2 (PO4) 2: 0.04 Dy3+.

hat the luminescence intensity is maximum for the sample Ca (0.96) Zn2 (PO4) 2: 0.04 Dy3+.The phosphor was characterized by high values of branching ratio and stimulated emission cross section for the 4F9/26H13/2 transition.The emission spectra were also analyzed using Commission Internationale de l’eA-clairage 1931 standard to understand the quality of white light emission.The chromaticity color coordinates of all the samples fall within the white light domain.The photoluminescence life time values of the 4F9/2 excited level was measured by exciting Dy3+ ions at 349 nm and was found to be 0.884 ms for the sample with optimum concentration.The internal quantum efficiency was also calculated and observed to have a very good value of about 74.9%.The present study confirms the Dy3+ doped CaZn2 (PO4) 2 phosphors to be a promising material for white light emitting diodes. 2021The Society of Powder Technology Japan.Published by Elsevier B.V.and The Society of Powder Technology Japan.All rights reserved. 1.Introduction Among the various solid state lighting technologies, phosphor converted white light diodes (pc-WLEDs) having reliability, energy efficiency and easy maintenance are now replacing the conventional light sources such as incandescent and fluorescent lamps.For the past few years, a great deal of progress has been made in the optical properties of pc-WLEDs owing to the active researches in the field of rare earth doped phosphor materials.In the beginning people started making white light by combining the red, blue and green LEDs.But this makes the system bulkier and there arises the requirement of independent driving currents.Another approach was to rely on multiphase phosphors containing more than one phosphor each one giving different emissions.But it also suffer from certain limitations such as reduction in luminescence efficiency arising out of the re-absorption of emission colors, increase in production cost etc [1].

efficiency arising out of the re-absorption of emission colors, increase in production cost etc [1].So white light emission from single phase phosphors are considered as more desirable and this leads to the increasing popularity of blue InGaNLED with yellow phosphor ( YAG; Ce3+) [2].Further research in this field is demanded owing to the instability of blue emission caused by LED’s sensitivity to drive current and temperature.Above all, it also faces problems such as halo effect and low color rendering in long run.As an activator in single phase white light emitting phosphors, Dy3+ ions have gained much research interest owing to the presence of large number of 4f- 4f transitions and intense emission in the visible region.In general, Dy3+ ions when incorporated into a ligand environment can give white light due to major emissions in the blue and yellow regions corresponding to the 4F9/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 transitions respectively.A very weak emission in the red region corresponding to the 4F9/26H11/2 transition of Dy3+ is also observed [3–5].It is possible to achieve white light by making appropriate modifications on the Y/B intensity ratio either by changing the composition of host material or by varying the concentration of Dy3+ ions.The studies have confirmed the necessacity in availing suitable host matrices for dispersing the rare earth ions to improve their performance [6].Among the different host matrices, the phosphate materials are of great importance as they possess many advantages such as high thermal and chemical stability, requirement of lower sintering temperatures etc [7].Based on the above information, the present work reports the synthesis of Dy3+ doped CaZn2 (PO4) 2 phosphors by conventional solid- state reaction method and their structure, morphology, photoluminescence excitation, emission and chromatic properties were investigated in detail to check the suitability of this composition for white light applications such as outdoor lighting, vehicle headlight, indicators, back lights etc. 2.

has started to replace the incandescent lamps and the fluorescent lights because of its high efficiency and long lifetime.A combination of yellow phosphors and InGaN blue LED chips is the most popular approach to realize white luminescence.The blue light could be partially absorbed by the yellow phosphor to emit yellow luminescence, and then the complementary blue and yellow light are mixed in appropriate proportions to produce white light in the packaged LED.Dy3+ doped yellow light phosphors via 4F9/2 to 6H13/2 transition (565–585 nm) have been reported in different host materials, such as titanate [1], borate [2], fluoride [3], phosphate [4], aluminate [5], silicate [6] and tungstate [7].Owing to the extraordinary chemical stability and the excellent thermal and mechanical properties of aluminates, they could provide appropriate coordination circumstances for Dy3+ to emit yellow lumines cence.In addition, aluminates own relatively high phonon energy, so the populations in 6H13/2 level could relax to the ground state 6H15/2 quickly, which benefits the population inversion for yellow light emissions.Since the blue LED has made great progress in the last decade, the two kinds of popular yellow-emitting phosphors including Ce3+YAG and Dy3+: YAG phosphors, which are based on 4f-5d transition of Ce3+ and 4f-4f transition of Dy3+, respectively, have been widely studied owing to the convenient and environment-friendly production of them [8–11].However, the high sintering temperature and the possible phase transformation during the fabrication of YAG phosphors are prone to make it contain the phases of YAlO3 and Y4Al2O9.

Research paper New Ba2YAlO5: Dy3+ nanomaterials for WLEDs: Propellant combustion synthesis and photometric features for enhanced emission of cool-white light under NUV excitation Priyanka Sehrawat a, R.K.Malik a,*, R.Punia b, Monika Sheoran a, Sonika Singh c, Mukesh Kumar a Department of Chemistry, Maharshi Dayanand University, Rohtak 124001, India b Department of Physics, Maharshi Dayanand University, Rohtak 124001, India c Department of Chemistry, Chaudhary Bansi Lal University, Bhiwani 127021, India ARTICLEINFOKeywords: Opto-electronic Nanomaterials Photoluminescence Combustion synthesis Time-resolved fluorescence ABSTRACTA new-variety of cool-white-emitting Ba2YAlO5: Dy3+ nanomaterials has been prepared via a cost-effective, en ergy-saving and ecofriendly propellant-combustion-synthesis, to boost the performance of single–phase wLEDs (white-light-emitting diodes).X-ray-diffraction-profiles substantiate distortion-free Dy3-+-diffusion into monoclinic BaYAlO-prototype.Photoluminescence-spectra exhibits two-emission-bands in visible-domain centered at 486 (bluish) and 579 nm (golden), to impart white-color to powders.Additionally, decay-time, non-radiative rates, radiative-lifetime and quantum-efficiency are examined by Auzel’s model.White-light parameters (colorcoordinates (0.2702, 0.3308), color-purity (24.8910-2) & color-temperature (9132K)) emulate the standard-NTSC and LED-white-coordinates.Henceforth, aforementioned outcomes suggest their successful employment for advanced lasers, white-LEDs, security-labels, bio-imaging, latent-fingerprinting and photovoltaicapplications. 1.

, white-LEDs, security-labels, bio-imaging, latent-fingerprinting and photovoltaicapplications. 1.Introduction SSI (solid-state-illumination) technology has been transmuted the world-wide energy-supplies and so, globalized economy.Infact, their illuminating appliances, particularly white-LEDs (light-emanating-diodes) are presumed to emanate green energy as they are marked with non-toxic (free-of-mercury), longer service, easy-handling, digitally controllable and lesser power-consumption [1,2].Commercially, ongoing methodology to generate white-light is to surface yellowphosphors over blue chips of LEDs.But, that too, brings some cons in appearance like pathetic red-chromaticity.For the sake of circumventing these impediments, single-composition white-phosphors can be sheathed over near UV (ultra-violet)-triggered LEDs, to emanate highquality white-light.Henceforth, it becomes imperative to probe such new white-emanating phosphor materials with improved luminanceefficacy [3,4].With this prime object of white-light generation, RE ions (rare-earth), explicitly dysprosium ion (Dy3+) serves to be a promising activator for the inorganic type luminous materials.It manifests visible white-light in its emission-spectrum via two noticeable emission peaks of Dy3+ in blue (B) & yellow (Y) regime due to typical intra 4f subshell electronic-transitions.Consequently, by altering the Y to B color light emission intensity ratio, white-color-light can be emitted [5–7].Presently, ternary aluminates structured matrices are pretty convenient luminous materials, owing to their inherent stabilized crystalstructure, improved optical and luminescence aspects, non-hazardous and ecologically-suitable characteristics.Therefore, Ba2YAlO5 has been rightly generated for our current empirical prospective study, which has been stabilized into ABC3 kind analogous perovskite structure with pseudo bcc type lattice.

effectual generation of proposed Ba2YAlO5 materials activated via Dy3+ content as rx=0.01 – 0.10, in a crystalline and homogeneous powder form; a time and energy-efficacious propellant solution combustion-synthesis route, was duly preferred by the authors [14].Consummation of this methodology involved procurement of different chemicals, particularly Y (NO3) 36H2O3Ba (NO3) 2Dy (NO3) 36H2O ) Al (NO3) 2 as well as urea.The oxidizer to fuel ratio demands to be unity and the various chemicals are weighed accordingly, which later on, have been dissolved in a small quantity of deionized water filled in a pyrex-beaker of 250 mL capacity; Novel NASICON-type Na3.6Y1.8-x (PO4) 3; x Dy3+ phosphor: Structure and luminescence Nataliya Krutyak a,b,*, Dmitry Spassky b,c, Vitali Nagirnyi b, Andrey V.Antropov d, Dina V.Deyneko da Physical Department, M.V.Lomonosov Moscow State University, Leninskie Gory, 1(2), 119991, Moscow, Russia b Institute of Physics, University of Tartu, W.Ostwald Str.1, 50411, Tartu, Estonia c Skobeltsyn Institute of Nuclear Physics, M.V.Lomonosov Moscow State University, Leninskie Gory, 1(2), 119991, Moscow, Russia d Department of Chemistry, Lomonosov Moscow State University, Leninskie Gory, 1, 119991, Moscow, Russia ARTICLEINFOKeywords: Phosphate NASICON structure Luminescence Dysprosium emission Intrinsic emission Energy transfer ABSTRACTSingle-phase Na3.6Y1.8-x (PO4) 3; x Dy3+ phosphors were synthesized by high-temperature solid-state reaction.Powder X-ray diffraction study reveals that a homogeneous solid solution with a NASICON-type structure is formed at 0 x0.4.Luminescence properties of the phosphors were studied using the methods of UV and VUV spectroscopy.Narrow emission bands originating from intraconfigurational transitions in Dy3-+ were detected in the region 450–800 nm and optimal concentration of the dopant determined.The concentration quenching of Dy3++ emission is shown to be due to dipole-interaction.In addition, two broad bands were detected in the UV and blue spectral regions, which were tentatively ascribed to the intrinsic emission of self-trapped excitons and defect-related centers, respectively.Optical bandgap energy of Na3.6Y1.8 (PO4) 3 was estimated to Eg7.1 e V.

materials with intense luminescence are widely applied in lighting, security systems, medicine, high energy physics, etc.The requirements for their properties depend on the potential application and can differ significantly.However, for the overwhelming majority of phosphors a high light output and temperature stability of luminescence intensity are important.At present, thermal quenching is still the main problem for phosphors application in pcLEDs [1–3].Recently, the emission of phosphate-based Na superionic conductors (NASICON) has been shown to demonstrate high thermal stability in the region of pcLED operation (300–500K).In particular, Na3-2xSc2 (PO4) 3: x Eu2+ phosphate demonstrates a unique thermal stability exceeding that of traditional LED phosphors [4].The effect is due to the Na+ cation disorder at elevated temperatures, which allows to create additional channels of energy transfer from electron–hole pairs to activators via thermally populated defect levels, thus reducing non-radiative energy losses.Novel phosphate-based Na3.6Y1.8 (PO4) 3 phosphors doped with Bi3+ and (or) Eu3+, which are isostructural to Na3Sc2 (PO4) 3, are also considered for application in pcLEDs [5,6].In particular, Eu3+ doped Na3.6Y1.8 (PO4) 3 phosphors demonstrate excellent thermal stability and three times higher intensity in comparison to the commercially available Y2O2S: Eu3+ and Y2O3: Eu3+ phosphors [5].Highly transparent glass ceramics containing Na3.6Y1.8 (PO4) 3 crystals co-doped with Er3++ and b3+ ions have shown intense up-conversion luminescence with quantum yield as high as 80.5% that is suitable for the development of LEDs [7].Dy3+-doped phosphors are attractive for application in lighting because the Dy3+ emission spectrum consists of several groups of narrow lines covering the entire visible spectral region.

Novel thermally robust warm white light emitting phosphor Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14: Dy3+: Synthesis, crystal structure and luminescence property investigation Miao Gaoa,b, Kun Lib, Yuehui Yana,b, Shuangyu Xina, Heng Daia,b, GeZhua,∗, Chuang Wangb,∗ a Key Laboratory of New Energy and Rare Earth Resource Utilization of State Ethnic Affairs Commission, College of Physics and Materials Engineering, Dalian Minzu University, 18Liaohe West Road, Dalian, 116600, PRChina b College of New Energy, Bohai University, Jinzhou, 121000, PRChina articleinfo Article history: Received 3September 2020Revised 14October 2020Accepted 14October 2020Available online 15October 2020Keywords: Luminescence Optical materials Phosphors abstract To explore novel single phase warm white light emitting phosphor, a series of phosphate phosphors Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14: Dy3+ were prepared.The phase purity, crystal structure, morphology and element component were confirmed by XRDRietveld structure refinement, SEM and EDS analysis.The luminescence process of Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14Dy3+ were systematically studied by photoluminescence spectroscopy and decay curves.The results indicated Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14Dy3+ phosphors had strong excitation from 300 nm to 420 nm.Under the excitation of 350 nm, warm white light emission was achieved with the CIE color coordinates of (0.399, 0.448) and low CCT of 3992K.The concentration quenching mechanism and quantum eficiency of Dy3+ in Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14: Dy3+ were calculated and discussed in detail.The thermal quenching behavior revealed that Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14: Dy3+ had excellent thermal stability with stable color rendition.The thermal activation energy was finally calculated.

content: thermal stability with stable color rendition.The thermal activation energy was finally calculated.All the results indicated the potential application of Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14.Dy3+ white light emission phosphor to be used in solid state lighting. 1.Introduction To improve the energy utilization eficiency, it is necessary to create and develop sustainable energy sources.As a new generation lighting source, white LEDs have achieved rapid development owing to their unique characteristics, such as environment friendly, long life and quick response [1–3].Currently, the most widely used white LED is “phosphor-conversion” type LED (pc-LED), that is, coating the yellow Y3Al5O12: Ce3+( YAG: Ce3+) uniformly on a blue LED chip to generate white light.However, this combination lacks red light composition, resulting in high CCT (correlatedcolortemperature) and low CRI (colorrendingindex) [4,5].Meanwhile, the color of this LED device will shift along with current and temperature, which limits its application in some special lighting fields, such as medical, art or other high color rendering fields.The other way to obtain white light is to use three different phosphors combined with one n-UV (nearultraviolet) LED chip [6,7].However, the combination process brings many problems within phosphors, such as different service life, reabsorption and complex packaging process.Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop a new type of single phase white light emitting phosphor for applications in warm white light LEDs.For phosphors, it is particularly important to select appropriate luminescent center and host materials.As a typical luminescent center, trivalent Dy3+ is usually employed to acquire warm white light or yellow light emission, due to their characteristic emissions of 4F9/2-6H J / 2 ( J=11, 13 and 15) transitions [8].

sion, due to their characteristic emissions of 4F9/2-6H J / 2 ( J=11, 13 and 15) transitions [8].Based on the above emissions, Dy3+ can generate high eficient and warm white light emission in many different matrix materials, such as SrGa12019: Dy3+Ba7 (BO3) 3 (SiO4) Cl: Dy3+, Gd3Al5O12: Dy3+ and so on [9–11].Phosphate is considered as an important matrix for luminescent materials for its merits of low price, low phonon energy and suitable crystal field environment.Moreover, rareearth ion-doped phosphate compounds exhibit excellent luminescent characteristics, typically, c e3+, Tb3+ co-doped LaPO4 and Eu3+ doped (Y,Gd)(P,V)O [12,13], which have been commercially used in mercury lamp and plasma display panel.In this work, Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14: Dy3+( CLYP: Dy3+) was successfully prepared and the phase purity, crystal structure, morphology and photoluminescence properties as well as the related mechanism were systematically studied. , 6M21/2, 4G11/2, 4I15/2 transitions of Dy3+ ions appear at 325, 350, 365, 385, 425, and 450 nm [16].The strong absorption in (near) ultraviolet range shows that CLYP: Dy3+ phosphor has potential to be applied in n-UVLEDs.Fig.2(b) displays the emission spectra of CLYP: x Dy3+( 0.01 x0.1 ) phosphors pumped by 350 nm radiation.The emission spectra clearly show characteristic blue emission (484nm), yellow emission (572nm) and red emission (660nm), due to the 4F9/2-6H1/2 ( J=1513 and 11) transitions of Dy3+, respectively.Based on the above three emissions, warm white light can be achieved with CIE coordinates of (0.399, 0.448) and a low CCT of 3992K in CLYP:0.04Dy3+.As is known, the transition of Dy3+ ion at 482 nm (4F9/2-H15/2) is a magnetic dipole transition, which greatly depends on the symmetry of the lattice environment around Dy3+ ion.That is, when Dy3+ ion occupies a low symmetry site with non-inversion center symmetry, the yellow emission of 572 nm ( 4F9/2: -: 6H13/2 ) ascribed to the electric dipole transition will dominate the emission spectrum.On the contrary, the blue emission from the magnetic dipole transition is predominant if Dy3+ ion occupies a high symmetry site [17].In this work, the dominated peak of Dy3+ emission at 572 nm indicates that Dy3+ occupies non-centrosymmetric sites in CLYP, which accords with the previous hypothesis.With increasing content x of Dy3+ ions, the emission intensity is observed to be increased gradually.When x is equal to 0.04, the luminescence intensity of Dy3+ ion acquires the maximum and then sharply decreases resulting from the resonance energy transfer between the adjacent Dy3+ ions.Generally, the critical distance Rc could be calculated according to Blass’s theory [18], Rc = 2(3V/(4πxcN))^(1/3) where xc represented the optimal doping content of Dy3+, V was the volume of unit cell, and Z indicated the number of formula units per unit cell.In this work, V3417.71A 3, xc=0.04, N=3.

ion levels and the probability of non-radiative transfer along with the increase of temperature.Fig.3(b) shows the temperature quenching mapping spectrum, which clearly shows that both transitions ( 4F9/26H15/2, 6H13/2 ) at 482 and 572 nm have excellent thermal stability and results in a stable color rendition.The CIE coordinates ( x, y ) along with increasing the temperature are plotted in Fig.3(c).It can be seen that both the values of x and y change little along with temperature, indicates that CLYP: 0.04Dy3+ has robust color stability.To further investigate the thermal quenching behavior of CLYP: 0.04Dy3+, the thermal activation energy (E) can be calculated by Arrhenius formula, [22,23] I (T)=I0 (1+Aexp (-E/kT)) - 16 where I0 was the room temperature initial emission intensity.I(T) meant the emission intensity at temperature T and K was the Boltzmann constant.The experimental value is well fitted by a linear equation as shown in Fig.3(d), which demonstrates the temperature quenching process follows the Arrhenius-type model and the calculated activation energy is 0.137 eV.The results indicate that CLYP:Dy3+ exhibits good thermal stability and has potential to apply in single phased WLEDs. 4.Conclusion A bran-new phosphate compound Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14 was synthesized and the structure feature was investigated.Warm white light can be realized from a single phased Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14Dy3+ under ultraviolet light excitation with suitable CIE coordinates of (0.399, 0.448) and low color temperature (3992K).The luminescent property, internal quantum eficiency as well as the interaction mechanism were discussed.Significantly, Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14Dy3+ exhibits a stable temperature quenching behavior.The current results indicate that Ca18Li3Y (PO4) 14; Dy3+ has potential to serve as a single phased white emission phosphor to be applied in n-UVLEDs. content: Photoluminescence enhancement in a Na5Y (MoO4) 4: Dy3+ white-emitting phosphor by partial replacement of MoO42- with WO42- or VO43-Jiangguo Xiao a, Wentao Zhang a,*, Teshen Wang a, Jiyong Zhang a, Haiying DuaCollege of Materials and Chemistry & Chemical Engineering, Chengdu University of Technology, Chengdu, 610059, China b College of Ecology and Environment, Chengdu University of Technology, Chengdu, 610059, China ARTICLEINFOKeywords: Molybdate Rare earth White-emitting phosphor Anion substitution Luminescence enhancement ABSTRACTA series of Na5Y (MoO4) 4-y Ay: Dy3+( A=WO42-, VO43-; y=0-0.05 ) phosphors were synthesized by the combustion method.Some of the MoO2− sites were occupied by WO2− and VO43- anions, which enhanced the luminescence property of Dy3-+-doped Na5Y (MoO4) 4.XRD results show that the crystal structures of the samples were consistent with the standard Na5Y (MoO4) 4 phase.Under excitation at 352 nm, the Na5Y (MoO4) 4-y AyDy3+ phosphors exhibited a characteristic blue emission at 485 nm and a yellow emission at 577 nm, which originated from the 4F9/2→6H15/2 an d4F9/2→6H13/2 transitions of Dy3+ ions, respectively.White light can be achieved by combining these blue and yellow emissions.After replacing MoO42- with WO42- and v O43- anions in NaY (MoO4) 4: Dy3+, the luminescence intensity of Dy3+ was significantly improved due to the crystal field effect.The results indicate that Na5Y (MoO4) 3.97 (WO4) 0.03; Dy3+ and Na5Y (MoO4) 3.97 (VO4) 0.03: Dy3+ phosphors have good prospects for application in n-UV-excited w-LEDs. 1.

content: .97 (VO4) 0.03: Dy3+ phosphors have good prospects for application in n-UV-excited w-LEDs. 1.Introduction White light-emitting diodes (w-LEDs) have high efficiency and low environmental impact, thereby presenting a new generation of lighting.They have broad applications in many fields, such as illumination, displays, and backlighting [1–4].Currently, commercial w-LEDs are fabricated by coating a yellow YAG:Ce phosphor onto a blue InGaN chip [5–7].However, this can produce a low color rendering index (CRI) and high correlated color temperature (CCT) because of the lack of a red emission component, which greatly hinders the application of w-LEDs [ 8, 9 ].Another way to fabricate w-LEDs involves exciting red, green, and blue phosphors with a near-ultraviolet (n-UV) chip; however, this has low efficiency due to reabsorption between the phosphors [10,11].Meanwhile, the emitted white light is unstable due to the different degradation rates of the tricolor phosphors [12].Therefore, a single-component white-emitting phosphor with an n-UV chip may be the most effective method of w-LED production.Some potential phosphors have been studied, such as SrZn2 (PO4) 2: EuZ+ / Mn2+/ 13 ], La10 (SiO4) 6O3; Eu2+/ Eu3+[ 14 ], and Ca9Bi (PO4) 7: Ce3+/ Tb3+/ Mn2+[15].Additionally, some Dy3+-doped phosphors also reveal white-emissions because of their blue emission peaks at approximately 480 nm and their yellow emission peaks at about 580 nm [16–19].Recently, Dy3+- doped molybdate phosphors with a scheelite structure have attracted much attention, such as CaMoO4: Dy3+/ K+ [20], Y2 (MoO4) 3: Dy3+[19], LiLa (MoO4) 2Dy3+/ Eu3+[21], and CaGd2(-MoO4) 4: Dy3++ [22].In these molybdate compounds, Na5Y (MoO4) 4, with its quadrangle structure, has potential as an outstanding phosphor host because of its low synthesis temperature and chemical stability [23].The Na5Y (MoO4) 4 structure can be realized as CaMoO4 according to the substitution equation 4Ca2+=5Na + + Y3+.

) 4 structure can be realized as CaMoO4 according to the substitution equation 4Ca2+=5Na + + Y3+.However, there are few reports on rare earth ions doped Na5Y (MoO4) 4, especially for NaY (MoO4) 4: Dy3+ phosphors.Furthermore, structural substitution can also improve the luminescence property of phosphors.For example, Zhang et al.[24] reported partially replacing MoO42- with SO42- or BO33- in NaLa (MoO4) 2: Eu3+, which increased the luminescence intensity by 2 and 1.6 times, respectively.In Chiu’s research [25], after introducing MoO2− in M5Eu (WO4) 4 ( M=Li, Na, K) phosphors, the luminescence intensity was significantly increased.Hence, anion substitution in Na5Y (MoO4) 4: Dy3+ may be a feasible way to enhance luminescence properties.Hence, it is very important to investigate the synthesis and photoluminescence of Na5Y (MoO4) 4-y Ay: Dy3+ CA=WO42-−, VO43− ) phosphors.In this study, a new type of Na5Y (MoO4) 4: Dy3+ phosphor was prepared by a simple combustion method.Partial substitution of WO42- and VO43- for MoO42- was carried out to enhance the luminescence property of Na5Y (MoO4) 4: Dy3+.The effects of heat-treatment temperature, Dy3+ ion concentration, and anion substitution on the luminescence intensity of a Na5Y (MoO4) 4: Dy3+ phosphor were studied, and a potential white-emitting phosphor was achieved using Na5Y (MoO4) 4 y Ay: Dy3+( A=WO42-, VO43- ) for w-LED application. 2.Experimenta All Na5Y (MoO4) 4-y Ay: Dy3+ ( A=WO42-,: VO43- ) samples were synthesized by the combustion method.Dy2O3 ( 99.99 % ), Na2CO3 (AR).2O3 (AR), citric acid (AR), (NH4) 6Mo7O244H2O (AR), (NH4) 10 (H2W12O42) H2O (99.0%) and NH4VO3 (99.0%) were used as starting materials.The amounts of WO42- and 043 - (y) were controlled at 0-0.

.0%) were used as starting materials.The amounts of WO42- and 043 - (y) were controlled at 0-0.05 in the structure.Y2O3 and Dy2O3 were dissolved in dilute HNO3 according to stoichiometric ratios to form the corresponding metal nitrates, and Na2CO3, (NH4) 6Mo7O244H2O3, and citric acid were added to the above solution in turn.The citric acid served as a chelating agent and combustion agent for metal ions, with the molar ratio of total chelating metal ions to citric acid set as 1:2.This transparent solution was stirred on a magnetic agitator at 70C for 30 min until a yellow sol was obtained.Then, the sol was placed in a crucible and calcined in a muffle furnace at temperatures of 500-700 C for 1 h.Finally, the sample was furnace-cooled and removed for further experimentation. ults show that the synthesis temperature had two effects on the luminescence property of the sample.On the one hand, increased temperature made the diffusion of the reaction material more complete, better promoted Dy3+ ions to enter the lattice, and improved the crystallinity of Na5Y (MoO4) 4On the other hand, the luminescence intensity was reduced due to the excessive increase of grain size and agglomeration at high temperature [28,29].At temperatures below 650C, the former plays a major role in luminescence and the luminescence intensity is enhanced.When the temperature exceeds 650C, the latter has a major effect on luminescence and significantly affects the luminescence intensity.Therefore, the optimum synthesis temperature of Na5Y (MoO4) 4; 2 / o Dy3++ phosphor was 650 ◦C.Fig.4 shows the XRD patterns of Na5Y1-x (MoO4) 4: x Dy3+ with different Dy3+ concentrations ( x=0.01 – 0.07 ) and the Rietveld refine ment result.In Fig.4(a), the diffraction peaks of all samples are the same as those of the standard structure and no other impurity peaks are visible.The persistent co-doping of Dy3+ ions does not cause obvious changes in crystal structure, indicating that Dy3+ ions enter the lattice successfully.To more accurately determine the structure of the Na5Y1-x (MoO4) 4: x Dy3+ samples, Fig.4(b) shows the Rietveld refinement result of Na5Y (MoO4) 4; 0.05Dy3+The refinement factor of NaY (MoO4) 4: 0.05Dy3+ converges to Rwp=10.62 % Rp=6.74 %, and 2=4.6.The results show that the structure after adulteration is almost the same as that of the pure Na5Y (MoO4) 4 phase.Fig.5(a) shows the emission spectra of Na5Y1-x (MoO4) 4: x Dy3+ with different Dy3+ doping concentrations.In Fig.5(a), the luminescence intensity gradually increases with Dy3+ concentration x increases to 0.04.With further increases in the Dy3+ concentration, the luminescence intensity gradually decreases due to concentration quenching.

Correspondence: eayoung 21@naver.com; Tel.: +82-51-999-5465Abstract: The precursor prepared by co-precipitation method was sintered at various temperatures to synthesize crystalline manganese tungstate (MnWO4).Sintered MnWO4 showed the best crystallinity at a sintering temperature of 800C..Rare earth ion (Dysprosium; Dy3+) was added when preparing the precursor to enhance the magnetic and luminescent properties of crystalline MnWO4 based on these sintering temperature conditions.As the amount of rare earth ions was changed, the magnetic and luminescent characteristics were enhanced; however, after 0.1 mol.%, the luminescent characteristics decreased due to the concentration quenching phenomenon.In addition, a composite was prepared by mixing MnWO4 powder, with enhanced magnetism and luminescence properties due to the addition of dysprosium, with epoxy.To one of the two prepared composites a magnetic field was applied to induce alignment of the MnWO4 particles.Aligned particles showed stronger luminescence than the composite sample prepared with unsorted particles.As a result of this, it was suggested that it can be used as phosphor and a photosensitizer by utilizing the magnetic and luminescent properties of the synthesized MnWO4 powder with the addition of rare earth ions. r three classic bands at 482, 573 and 666 nm to phosphors owing to their 4 f9 electronic configuration.The sharp peaks at 482 nm (4F9/26H15/2) and 573 nm (4F9/26H13/2) are located in the blue and yellow regions, respectively.13,14 Therefore, efforts to explore Dy3+-activated luminescent materials are important because these materials may have white light emissions.The structural compounds of double perovskites are typically used as excellent host materials because of their good optical characteristics and stable physical and chemical properties 15-18 Dy3+ iondoped double-perovskite compounds, such as Sr2CaWO6: Dy3+SrLaMgTaO6: Dy3+, and Ba2ScMO6Dy3+( M=Nb, Ta ) with the formula r A2 (BB) O6, have recently been reported in the literature.19e21 In1978, Neurgaonkar etal.22 reported the Eu3+-, Tb3+-, Dy3+-, and Er3+-activated tellurate double perovskite M22+R2+TeO6 ( M=Ba, SrCa, Cd; RBa, Sr, Ca, Cd, Mg, Zn) and found that only CaMgTeO compounds are effective hosts for rare-earth-activated luminescence.In2008, Dias et al.23 pointed out that Ca2MgTeO6 ceramics exhibit a monoclinic P21 / n structure belonging to the A2 (BB) 06 double perovskite family.However, Dy3+-doped CaMgTeO phosphors have not been investigated in recent years.In this study, the tellurate Ca2MgTeO6 phosphors of Dy3+-doped double perovskite were successfully synthesized.Then, the phase purity, surface morphology, elemental mapping, photoluminescence properties, content quenching mechanism, CIE chromaticity coordinates, color purity, CCT, decay curves, thermal stability, and internal quantum efficiency (IQE) of the resulting products were investigated in detail.The fabricated w-LEDs based on a UV-InGaN chip (=366 nm ) display good potential in applications such as commercial w-LEDs. 2.Experimental The phosphors of Ca2MgTeO6: x Dy3+, x Na+ ( x=1.mol%, 5 mol%, 10 mol%, 15 mol%, 20 mol%, 25 mol%, and 30 mol%) were prepared by solid-state synthesis method.

rdinates of the prepared w-LED were measured using a spectrometer (USB4000, Ocean Optics, USA). 3.Results and discussion The Ca2MgTeO6 crystal structure is monoclinic, with space group P21 / n.As shown in Fig.1, Ca2+(bluesphere) occupies the same site A with 12 oxygen atoms, and Mg2+(graysphere) and Te6+(darkyellowsphere) occupy the same site B with 6 oxygen atoms.When the charge difference between B0 and B ions is 4, the order between the B0 and B00 ions is quite common for cubic perovskites of the type A2 (BB) O6.24The XRD peaks of the Ca2MgTeO6: x Dy3+, x Na+ (1 mol% x30 mol%) phosphors are shown in Fig.2.Although no standard card for the Ca2MgTeO6 compound exists in the database of the Joint Committee on Powder Diffraction Standards, the standard card (PDF48-0108) of Ca2MgWO6 is taken as reference on account of the isostructural forms of these compounds.The diffraction peaks of Ca2MgTeO6: x Dy3+, x Na+ ( 1 mol% x30 mol%) samples matched well with the standard card of Ca2MgWO6 with a=0.56102 nm, b=0.55944 nm, c=0.79045 nm, and V=0.24809 n m3.It suggests that the single-phase phosphors of Ca2MgTeO6: Dy3+, Na+ were successfully synthesized.Moreover, increasing contents of Dy3+ ions have no influence on the crystal structure of the prepared phosphors, thereby indicating their high purity.Fig.2(b) displays the enlarged diffraction peaks of Ca2MgTeO6xDy3+, x Na+ (1 mol% x30 mol%) from 32.0- to 33.5 (2)..The reflection peaks of the samples shift toward higher angles with increasing content of Dy3+ ions compared with the standard data of Ca2MgWO6.In our work, the radii of Dy3+, Mg2+, and Ca2+ ions when the coordination number (CN) is 6 are 0.0912, 0.072 and 0.1 nm, respectively.Dy3+þ ions can replace Ca2+þ ions due to their similar radii.According to the Bragg diffraction formula of 2 dsin=n, 25 the diffraction peaks shift toward the higher-angle side because of the smaller radii of doped ions compared with the substituted Ca2+ ions in the Ca2MgTeO6 host lattice.

RESEARCHARTICLELUMINESCENCEWILEYThermoluminescence dosimetry properties and kinetic analysis of K3Ca2 (SO4) 3F Dy3+ phosphor C.M.Mehare 1,3 | M.D.Mehare 2 | C.Ghanty 3 | N.S.Dhoble 4 | S.J.Dhoble 1 1Department of Physics, R.T.M.Nagpur University, Nagpur, India 2Department of Physics, Priyadarshini College of Engineering, Nagpur, India 3Department of Chemistry, O.P.Jindal University, Punjipathra, Raigarh, India 4Department of Chemistry, Sevadal Mahila Mahavidhyalaya, Nagpur, India Correspondence C.M.Mehare, Department of Physics, R.T.M.Nagpur University, Nagpur-440033, India.Email: cmmehare 18@gmail.com Abstract A trivalent Dy3+-activated K3Ca2 (SO4) 3F fluoride-based phosphor was synthesized using a solid-state reaction method and characterized for its thermoluminescence (TL) application.The crystal structure and surface morphology of the as-synthesized material was analyzed using X-ray diffraction and scanning electron microscopy.A series of the K3Ca2 (SO4) 3F Dy3+ phosphor was irradiated using γ-rays from a60Co source and TL glow curves were recorded using a Nucleonix 1009I TL reader.The glow curve of the prepared phosphor showed a prominent single peak at 278C.TL characteristics were maximum intensity at 1 mol% of Dy3+ ion with a single TL glow peak.The TL glow curve revealed linearity with increase in exposure dose range from 0.1 kGy to 3.0 kGy.Theoretical analysis of the TL glow curve of the γ-ray-irradiated sample was carried out using a computerized glow curve deconvolution method and trapping parameters such as activation energy and frequency factor were calculated using the initial rise method and Ilich’s method.The synthesized Dy3+-doped K3Ca2 (SO4) 3 phosphor revealed excellent TL properties and was found to be a potential candidate for dosimetric applications.
