1.Introduction At present, due to the progressively serious circumstances of global energy and environment, people come to comprehend that they should live in a more energy saving way.The need for the generation of light emitting material has increased rapidly due to the quickly growing market of lighting industry [1].Because of its exceptional qualities such as bright thermal endurance, high intensity and ecologically sound behaviour, inorganic phosphor synthesis has received a great deal of attention [2,3].Numerous photonic devices including field emission displays [4], vacuum fluorescent displays [5], plasma display panels [6], fluorescent lights [7], scintillators [8], lasers [9], electroluminescent lighting [10] and white light emitting diodes [11], utilized inorganic phosphors based on rare earth metal ions.White light-emitting diodes (LEDs) have recently become popular owing to their excellent performance in a variety of applications including device indications, car headlights, and general lighting [12–14].Because it is more affordable and technically advanced so, the commercial fabrication of white LEDs is often accomplished by coating a yellow-emitting n of white LEDs is often accomplished by coating a yellow-emitting phosphor on a blue LED chip [15].Due to the absence of the red component, these white LEDs have a low colour rendering index (CRI<80) and a high correlated colour temperature (CCT) [16].In the modern era, several researchers have tried to develop white LEDs by fusing a near-UVLED chip with RGB phosphors.However, because the red and green generating phosphors reabsorb the blue light, these RGB systems are expensive to develop and may not produce blue light as efficiently as they should.Due to these drawbacks, research on effective, stable and single phase white light emitting phosphors is becoming more and more popular [17,18].For the determination of crystal structure and luminescent characteristics, the selection of host material is a vital issue.The perovskite GdAlO3 (GAP) nanomaterial is a significant host material because it includes trivalent gadolinium (Gd3+) ions which are effective sensitizers for various perceptible emissions of Ln3+ ions, permitting the energy transfer route from Gd3+ to dopant ions, which further increase the luminous features of the doped ions [19].Due to their relative ionic radii to the host lattices, trivalent rare-earth ions (RE3+) are the only dopant ions that are employed as emission sources.Due to the complexed electronic energy levels, multiple electronic transitions between f-levels are predicted for the Dy3+ ion, which has an outermost 4 f9 electronic structure [20].However, the transitions between these energy levels are very selective, only sharp lines are formed.Dy3+ doped GdAlO3 were mainly involving two intense bands which are attributed to dopant centered intraconfigurational transitions viz.4F9/26H15/2 (calledblueband) and 4F9/26H13/2 (calledyellowband) [21].Hence, Dysprosium ion is deliberated as most proficient applicant for the production of white light because of its significant ratio of yellowish and bluish emission bands.

e production of white light because of its significant ratio of yellowish and bluish emission bands.For the development of nanophosphors, a variety of chemical synthetic methods have been used which include solid state reactions [22], hydrothermal routes of synthesis [23], aerosol furnace methods [24], co-precipitation methods [25], gel-combustion techniques [26], sol-gel processes [27] and spray-pyrolysis processes [28].In this work, synthesis, structural characterization and luminescence analysis of GdAlO3: Dy3+ phosphors are reported.No significant report on the current phosphors produced by the gel-combustion process is found in the literature review.The gel-combustion procedure was chosen in this instance to produce GdAlO3: Dy3+ nanophosphors due to some of its key advantages over alternative synthetic techniques, including low cost, low synthesis temperature, greater uniformity and high emission intensity of synthesized materials [29].The obtained outcomes of cool white light emissive GdAlO3: Dy3+ nanophosphors make it better applicant for the white light emitting diodes and other lighting foundations. 2.Experimental 2.1.Materials used The high quality chemicals such as metal nitrates i.e.Gadolinium Nitrate Hexahydrate [ Gd (NO3) 3.6H2O4, purity; 99.9%], Dysprosium Nitrate Hexahydrate [ Dy (NO3) 3.6H2O, purity; 99.9%], Aluminium Nitrate Nonahydrate [ Al (NO3) 3.9H2O, purity; 99.9%] and urea [NH2CONH2] of Sigma Aldrich have been employed as raw materials because they dissolve easily in water and have a low decomposition temperature.Deionized (DI) water has been used for post action processes. 2.2.Synthesis Perovskite undoped GdAlO3 and Gd1-xAlO3: x Dy3+( x=1, 3, 5, 7, 9 mol %) powdered samples have been fabricated via ecofriendly, economically viable and low temperature based self-propagating gelcombustion process.Precursors have been weighed out and liquefied in a small amount of deionized water according to their stoichiometric composition.

ut and liquefied in a small amount of deionized water according to their stoichiometric composition.The solution was then heated to around 80C on a magnetic hot plate for 15–20 min while being vigorously stirred.After heating, a viscous framework mixture was produced and the specified amount of urea was then added to the solution together with a small amount of water.A transparent gel-like fluid was developed after heating.A self-sustaining exothermic redox reaction between metal nitrates as oxidant and urea as reducer occurs in this process [30].This viscous mixture was then heated to 600C and placed in the furnace for 12 min to ensure proper combustion.Gases such as N2, CO, CO2, and NH3 are released after combustion, creating a fluffy, porous white substance as a product.The crystallinity and low temperature treatment, which were responsible for the reduced particle size of the powdered materials, were due to the tremendous energy release during the redox combustion process [31].The final product was ground and sintered for 3 h at temperatures of 800, 950 and 1100 C..The crystalline product was prepared for various investigations after calcination. 2.3.Instrumentations By employing a variety of techniques at room temperature, the structural and spectroscopic properties of selected nanomaterials were investigated.To determine the XRD profiles of synthesized powdered samples within 2θ angle range of 10◦-80◦ and scan rate of 2◦ per min and step interval of 0.02, the Rigaku Ultima-IVX-ray diffractometer with CuKα rays (=1.5416 ) was used.By employing Match-3 software, Rietveld analysis of doped and undoped (host) crystals was done to explain their phase purity, refinement parameters and crystal structure engineering in general terms.By employing a procedure called pellet production, the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectrum of focused sample was captured by a PerkinElmer 5700 spectrophotometer (within400-4000cm-1region).

PAPERView Article Online View Journal | View Issue Check for updates Cite this: RSCAdv., 2022, 12, 31757 Photoluminescence and afterglow of Dy3+ doped CaAl2O4 derived via sol–gel combustion† Bao-gai Zhai, Meng Meng Chen and Yuan Ming Huang * With doping concentration varying from 0.1 to 5.0 mol%, a series of Dy3+ doped calcium aluminate ( CaAl2O4; Dy3+) phosphors were synthesized via a sol–gel combustion technique.The phase, morphology, photoluminescence (PL), afterglow, and thermoluminescence (TL) glow curves of CaAl2O4; Dy3+ were investigated by means of X-ray difractometry, scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, PL spectroscopy, afterglow spectroscopy, and TL dosimetry, respectively.It is found that: (i) oxygen vacancies and Dy3+ work as two independent sets of luminescence centers of PL for CaAl2O4; Dy3+; (ii) Dy3+ works as the luminescence center of afterglow for CaAl2O4; Dy3+; (iii) the afterglow of CaAl2O4; Dy3+ lasts for about 115 min at the optimal doping concentration of around 0.8 mol%; and (iv) multiple traps, which are sensitive to doping concentration, are present in CaAl2O4; Dy3+.The PL and afterglow mechanisms of CaAl2O4; Dy3+ are discussed to reveal the processes of charged carrier excitation, migration, trapping, detrapping, and radiative recombination in CaAl2O4: Dy3+Received 10th August 2022Accepted 1st November 2022DOI: rsc.li/rsc-advances 1.Introduction Rare-earth doped calcium aluminate phosphors have been intensively studied due to their excellent aerglow properties,1–4 among which Dy3 doped calcium aluminate ( CaAl2O4: Dy3+) is a well-known inorganic phosphor which emits white photoluminescence (PL) under ultraviolet excitation.5 Apart from its white PL, CaAl2O4: Dy3+ exhibits a white afterglow even after the removal of ultraviolet excitation.6 As reported by Liu et al.

te afterglow even after the removal of ultraviolet excitation.6 As reported by Liu et al.in 2005, Dy3+ works as the luminescence center of aerglow for CaAl2O4: Dy3+ and the white aerglow of solid state reaction derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ lasts 32 min at the optimal doping concentration of 2 at%.6 For aerglow materials, the processes of charged carrier excitation, migration, trapping, detrapping, and radiative recombination are critically important to understand their aerglow properties.7–9 For example, long aerglow can be achieved at room temperature only when traps have an appropriate activation energy somewhere around 0.65 eV whereas shallow traps ( E0.4 e V ) and deep traps (E > 2 eV) are not favorable because they can be emptied either easily or with dificulty at room temperature.7 Up to date, only a single report exists on the aerglow of CaAl2O4: Dy3+, leaving the processes of charged carrier excitation, migration, trapping and detrapping not fully revealed.The lack of such knowledge hampers the comprehensive understanding of the aerglow mechanism of CaAl2O4: Dy3+With respect to solid state reaction derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ sol–gel combustion derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ is abundant in oxygen and calcium vacancies.In CaAl2O4: Dy3+, oxygen vacancies are potential electron traps because they are positively charged whereas calcium vacancies are potential hole traps because they are negatively charged.8,10 Therefore, sol–gel combustion derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ phosphors are suitable for exploring the aerglow mechanisms of CaAl2O4: Dy3+.In this paper, we report the PL and aerglow properties of sol–gel combustion derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ with the doping concentrations varying from 0.1 to 5.0 mol%.A picture on the PL and aerglow mechanisms of CaAl2O4: Dy3+ is given to reveal the processes of charged carriers' excitation, migration, trapping, detrapping, and recombination in CaAl2O4: Dy3+ 2.

ged carriers' excitation, migration, trapping, detrapping, and recombination in CaAl2O4: Dy3+ 2.Experimental section 2.1Sol–gel combustion synthesis of CaAl2O4: Dy3+CaAl2O4: Dy3+ phosphors with the doping concentrations varying from 0.1 to 5.0 mol% were synthesized via the sol–gel combustion with urea as fuel.11–13 All reagents were in analytical grade and provided by Sinopharm Chemical Reagents Co., Ltd (Shanghai, China).The purity of dysprosium oxide (Dy2O3) was 99.99%.Under stirring with a magnetic bar, Ca (NO3) 24H2O (0.2mol), Al (NO3) 39H2O (0.4mol), urea (6.0mol), H3BO3 (0.02mol) and stoichiometric amount of Dy2O3 were dissolved in deionized water (600mL) to form a transparent solution.A homogeneous solution was obtained aer the mixture was stirred vigorously for 60 min in a glass beaker.Aer having been aged at room temperature for two weeks, the solution was ready for the sol–gel combustion.Urea and boric acid functioned a the fuel and ux, respectively.Alumina crucibles, each with the volume capacity of 50 mL, were employed as the reaction containers.Half lled with the aged solution, the solutioncontaining alumina crucible was transferred into an air-lled box furnace for self-propagating combustion.The temperature in the furnace was preset at 780 C.After the solution containing crucible was transferred into the furnace, the temperature in the furnace was gradually dropped to about 706 °C.Heated at such high temperatures, water in the solution got boiling and the starting materials (fuelsandmetalnitrates) in the crucible were partially decomposed until the organic fuels were automatically ignited to initiate the exothermic reactions.The sol–gel combustion yielded voluminous gases and bright ames.In this work, the synthesis was initiated by pointheating of a small part of the mixture in the crucible, and the ignition was started at around 750C..Once started, a wave of exothermic reactions swept through the remaining material in the crucible.

..Once started, a wave of exothermic reactions swept through the remaining material in the crucible.This combustion synthesis lasted for about 40 s, which was exceptionally fast when compared to hightemperature solid state reactions.During the sol–gel combustion, a large amount of energy was released from the exothermic reactions, which in turn raised the temperature in the furnace up to 830C.Measured with an infrared thermometer, the temperature in the ame was up to 1300C..After the fire was extinguished, the crucible was taken out of the furnace immediately.The total holding time of the crucible in the furnace was about 4 min.White powders were resulted aer the sol–gel combustion.According to molar ratio of Dy3+ to Ca2+ in the starting materials, a series of CaAl2O4: Dy3+ phosphors were obtained with the nominal doping concentration of Dy3+ varying in the range of 0.1–5.0 mol%.No further calcination was applied to the sol–gel combustion derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ 2.2Solid state synthesis of CaAl2O4: Dy3+ phosphors For comparison, solid state reaction derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ phosphors were synthesized with CaCO3 (0.02mol), Al2O3 (0.02mol), H3BO3 (0.002mol), Dy2O3 as raw materials.Stoichiometric mixtures of the raw materials were homogeneously mixed and ground.Subsequently the mixture was transferred into alumina crucibles and sintered at 900 °C for 4 h in an air-lled electric tube furnace.The sintered products were ground again in an agate mortar, then the powder products were calcined at 1350 ° C for 10 h in air.According to the molar ratio of Dy3+ to Ca2+ in the starting materials, the doping concentration of Dy3+ in the solid state reaction derived CaAl2O4: Dy3+ varied in the range 0.1–10.0 mol%. 2.3Phase, morphology and elemental composition of CaAl2O4: Dy3+ phosphors X-Ray difraction (XRD) proles of CaAl2O4: Dy3+ phosphors were recorded on X-ray difractometer (D/max 2500PC, Rigaku Corporation, Akishima, Japan) using CuKa radiation (=0.15405 nm).

content: ce properties of LaVO4: Dy3+ and reveal the mechanism. 1.Introduction Luminescent materials, usually composed of a luminescent center and a host matrix with additional dopant ions, have long been the subject of great interest to many researchers.Among many rare earth compounds, vanadate (LnVO4) is an important luminescent matrix material with good crystal structure and physical properties, this provides the proper crystal field for the lanthanide ions, which, when their energy levels are disturbed, can lead to the phenomenon of photoluminescence [1,2].The absorption cross section of lanthanide ions is small, and direct excitation leads to low luminous eficiency.When dopant ions are doped into orthovanadates ( YV04, GdV04, LaV04 ) as activators, the dopants can be easily sensitized by energy transfer or charge transfer mechanisms.The vanadate (VO3-4) group can be eficiently excited by nearultraviolet light, allowing energy to be transferred to rare earth ions [3–5].The LaVO4 compound has good heat stability, suitable wide band gap width, moisture resistance and environmental friendliness [6,7].These characteristics make LaVO4 apply to actual applications.As a common phosphor activator, Dy3+ has received widespread attention because it can be matched with near ultraviolet light or blue LED chips and emit white light in specific substrates.When excited by near UV light at about 350 nm, Dy3+ produces linear blue (470–500 nm) and yellow (570–660 nm) emission peaks, which are derived from electron transitions from excited state 4F9/2 energy level to ground state 6H15/2 and 6H13/2 energy level [8], respectively.As a white phosphor, LaVO4: Dy3+ can obtain white light with different color temperature by adjusting the transition intensity ratio of blue light and yellow light.It is expected to be used as a single-color matching phosphor for white LED [9–11].To improve the luminescence properties of LaVO4: Dy3+, a lot of research has been done in recent years.Fan et al.

uminescence properties of LaVO4: Dy3+, a lot of research has been done in recent years.Fan et al.[12] synthesized LaVO4 nanorod-like crystals with different crystal phase configurations by controlling the pH of the reaction system in the aqueous solvent system.Studies showed that LaVO4Ln3+(LnEuSmDy) with tetragonal (t-) zircon type had better luminous performance than that with monoclinic (m-) monazite type.Liu et al.[13] prepared new polyhedral LaVO4: Dy3+ crystals by liquid phase synthesis technique and analyzed the fluorescence characteristics of LaVO4Dy3+ crystals obtained at different morphologies and different calcination temperatures in detail.Yu et al.[14] prepared spindle-shaped vanadate LnVO4 ( Ln=LaCePrNdSmEuGdTbDyHoErTmYbLu), analyzed the luminescence characteristics of LnVO4Dy3+( Ln=GdLaLu ), and found that LaVO4: Dy3+ had the highest luminescence intensity.However, it has been found in other doped phosphors that the luminous intensity is limited due to the luminescence quenching of the phosphor.The luminous quenching here refers to the attenuation of luminous following the augment of doping concentration.Because the suitability of light emitting devices mainly rely on the luminescence intensity, solving the quenching matter of luminescent devices is the main obstacle in the research of luminescence.Thence, a great deal of research work is needed to conquer this matter.Luckily, it was know in the report that co-doping can increase the intensity of quenched photoluminescence.In this context, Okram et al.[15] have studied the effects of Bi3+ sensitizers and Li+ and Sr2+ surface modifiers in Eu3+-doped LaVO4 phosphors, and the photoluminescence intensity of the phosphors was significantly improved under the excitation of 282 nm light.Ekta Rai et al.[16] different concentrations of Eu3+ and Bi3+ ions were doped and co-doped in LaVO4 phosphor.The energy level information of excited ions and the ef - fect of sensitizer on band emission intensity are revealed.Reena Okram et al.

ted ions and the ef - fect of sensitizer on band emission intensity are revealed.Reena Okram et al.[17] prepared LaVO4: Ln ( Ln=Dy3+, Sm3+) phosphors in different solvents at a low temperature of 140 ◦C by a simple precipitation method, and studied the photoluminescence of Dy3+ and Sm3+ ions using Ba2+ as activator.However, the study of the photoluminescence properties of co-doped large divalent ions enhanced LaVO4Dy3+ was few and the physical source of the enhancement was not clear.Nevertheless, to the best of the authors’ knowledge, there are few reports on the luminescence properties of LaVO4: Dy3+ codoping with Ca2+.In this paper, firstly, the LaVO4 phosphor doped with Dy3+ was prepared by high temperature solid-state method, and the effects of doping concentration and pre-sintering on the luminescence properties of the phosphor were studied.Secondly, Ca2+ co-doped LaVO4Dy3+ was prepared by high temperature solid-state method, and the effect of Ca2+ doping concentration on luminescence performance of phosphors was studied.Finally, by means of first-principles calculations, the relationship between the electronic structure and photoluminescence properties of co-doped LaVO4: Dy3+, Ca2+ phosphors, as well as the underlying physical mechanism, were investigated. 2.Experimental procedure and first-principles calculations 2.1.Experimental procedure 2.1.1.Synthesis of Dy3+ doped LaVO4Lanthanum ox ide ( La203, 99.9 % ), vanadium pentoxide ( V205, 99.5 % ) and dysprosium oxide ( Dy203, 99.99 % ) were used as the raw materials.For LaVO4: Dy3+ phosphor, according to one of which calcined at high temperature of 1200C for 3 h with the same heating rate.

content: etermine the parameters (Ω=2, 4, 6), radiative lifetime and branching ratios of BBiLDy15 glass.The visible luminescence spectra at 482, 576, 663 and 772-nm correspond to transitions 4F9/26H J ( J=15/2, 13/2, 11/2, 9/2 ) under ex=350 nm were observed.The lasing parameters like stimulated emission cross section (5.4510-22cm2) and experimental branching ratio (61%) of the BBiLDy1.5 glass were determined from the visible transitions in the PL-emission spectra.The decrease in life time value of glass samples was observed that was attribute to the energy trans fer via resonance energy transfer (RET) from host matrix to luminescence centers.The CIE chromaticity color coordinates, CCT results and the emission cross section for the visible transitions emphasizing the capacity of BBiLDy glass samples as potential material for white light emitting diodes and visible laser application. 1.Introduction Borate glasses have been investigated due to their transparency, chemical durability, excessive heat stability, excellent rare earth (RE) ion solubility and low melting temperature [1].It has different applications in solid state electronic devices including white-light-emitting diodes (WLEDs), liquid-crystal displays (LCDs), vehicles indicators and phone screens [2].The important aspects of glasses are their high-power energy and lower carbon emission, longer lifespan, high capability, good reliability and environment friendliness [3,4].LEDs have wide applications in data communications, display backlighting, security cameras, medical devices, barcode scanners and signals [5,6].The B2O3-Bi2O3-Li2O contained host glassy materials have broad spectrum of transparency in the UV-region and have high thermal and photo mechanical stability [7,8].The insertion of Li2O as a modifier to glass matrix reduces melting point as well as changes conductivity of the host material.It breaks the network bond and forms non-bridging oxygen ions in glass structure [9].

host material.It breaks the network bond and forms non-bridging oxygen ions in glass structure [9].The heavy metal oxide like BiO is combined into glass matrix because of their higher density, high infrared transparency, higher refractive index, optical non-linearity and long infrared (IR) cut off.On combining with B2O3 it reduces the phonon energy, improves the chemical durability, possess high efficiency for detection of X-ray and γ-ray owing to its large effective atomic number ( Zeff=83 ) [10].Among the RE-ions, dysprosium ion is a promising material for luminescence studies as it exhibits strong visible emission in the yellow and blue range under UV excitation.The corresponding transitions are 4F9/2→6H15/2 an d4F9/2→6H13/2 for blue and yellow color that could be potentially utilized in white LEDs.The yellow emission is more sensitized to the host environment in comparison to blue emission.The luminescence intensity or Y/B ratio for dysprosium ions confirms the strength of covalence in Dy, O and localized symmetry in Dy3+ ions environment [11,12].For Dy3+ ions, the Y/B proportion may be tuned along with changing Dy3+ content, heat treatment, as well as chemical arrangement of the host glass.The Dy3+-doped crystal and glasses are considered as the best laser-active material for fiber optical communications [13].I.Ullah et al.[14] explored the physical, optical, luminescence and lasing properties of LiBGdMg-Dy glasses and found that developed glass can be used for white light production and as a yellow lasing material.I.Khan et al.[15] measured the luminescence properties and lasing parameters of LiNaKB-Dy glasses and acquired its importance for WLEDs and an optimistic material for deficient threshold laser action and high optical gain.P.Chimalawong et al.[16] explored physical and optical properties of silicate-soda-lime glasses doped with Dy2O3 but did not found its suitableness for laser and LEDs applications.F.Zamam et al.

Structural, morphological and optoelectronic aspects of YAlO3: Dy3+ doped nanocrystalline materials for NUV energized WLEDsIsha Gupta a, Sitender Singh a, Pawan Kumar a, Shri Bhagwan a, Vinod Kumar b, Devender Singh a,* a Department of Chemistry, Maharshi Dayanand University, Rohtak, 124001, India b Department of Physics, Netaji Subash University of Technology, Sector 3, Dwarka, Delhi, 110078, India ARTICLEINFOKeywords: Solution combustion Orthorhombic CCT (K) WLEDsABSTRACTCost-effective urea assisted solution combustion (SC) synthetic method was employed to prepare a series of doped YAlO3:xDy3+ (0.01–0.08 mol) phosphors.The resulting powdered samples were comprehensively examined through various structural as well as optical measurements.Rietveld refinement studies concluded that prepared nanomaterials structured into the orthorhombic system having Pbnm (62) space group.Energy dispersive spectral (EDS) analysis was executed to observe the relative proportions of constituent elements in all doped nanophosphors.Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) micrograph indicated the presence of agglomerated particles with the average size in the nano range.Photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectra showed that the designated phosphors could be excited by near ultraviolet (NUV) energized lighting sources.The strongest emission centred at 576 nm, corresponding to electric dipole (4F9/26H13/2) transition of Dy(III) ion.Furthermore, characteristics photometric parameters viz.correlated color temperature (CCT), chromaticity coordinates (xandy), and color purity (%) were figure out with the aid of PL data, which strongly endorsed their usage in NUV energized WLEDs applications. 1.

A R T I C L E I N F O Keywords: Solution combustion Orthorhombic CCT (K) WLEDs ## A B S T R A C T Cost-effective urea assisted solution combustion (SC) synthetic method was employed to prepare a series of doped YAlO<sub>3</sub>:xDy<sup>3+</sup> (0.01–0.08 mol) phosphors.The resulting powdered samples were comprehensively examined through various structural as well as optical measurements.Rietveld refinement studies concluded that prepared nanomaterials structured into the orthorhombic system having Pbnm (62) space group.Energy dispersive spectral (EDS) analysis was executed to observe the relative proportions of constituent elements in all doped nanophosphors.Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) micrograph indicated the presence of agglomerated particles with the average size in the nano range.Photoluminescence excitation (PLE) spectra showed that the designated phosphors could be excited by near ultraviolet (NUV) energized lighting sources.The strongest emission centred at576 nm, corresponding to electric dipole ( 4F9/26H13/2 ) transition of Dy(III) ion.Furthermore, characteristics photometric parameters viz.correlated color temperature (CCT), chromaticity coordinates (x and y), and color purity (%) were figure out with the aid of PL data, which strongly endorsed their usage in NUV energized WLEDs applications.## 1.

features of RE3+ ions, peculiar lumi nescence characteristics of RE3+ such as narrow emission line, high emission efficiency, and broad spectral range from ultraviolet to the infra-red region have been exploited [11].Therefore, RE3+ doped materials could be applied as displays [12], amplifiers and lasers [13], luminescent lamps [14], scintillators [15,16], or light-emitting nanophosphors [17,18].Predominately, light emissive nanophosphors have proved itself as promising candidates in harmonizing the increasing demand of energy consumption of the lighting sector throughout the world.RE3+ doped nanophosphors have been broadly used in numerous, widespread photonic applications viz.white light emitting diodes (WLEDs) [19,20], fluorescent lamps [21], optical lasers [22], plasma display panels (PDPs) [23,24], luminescent solar concentrators (LSC) [25] and other storage photonic appliances [26].Nowadays, rare-earth based white LEDs have become the first priority of SSL sources owed to their superior characteristics, including long service durability, persistency, high color purity, virtuous color tunability, good environmental sustainability, low energy consumption, good thermal and chemical stability, enhanced luminous performance and so on [27–29].

Fig.1.Schematic representation of synthetic route for the preparation of YAlO3: Dy3+ doped nanomaterials.Recently, yttrium aluminum perovskites (YAP) have attracted much attention owing to their promising characteristics such as propitious color tunability, high chemical and thermal durability, long persistency, compositional flexibility, high lumen equivalent, low lattice-phonon energy, environmental friendliness, and distinct electronic structure that develops itself as active host material and enormously anticipated for the doping of a suitable dopant ion [31–33].As far as dopant ion is concerned, trivalent rare-earth ions (RE3+) ) have been exclusively used as emission centre because of their close proximity of ionic radii with the host lattices.Dysprosium (III) doped phosphors have been acknowledged itself as efficient light-emitting materials for material scientist because of their characteristics color perception [34].Dy3+ ion has an outermost 4 f9 electronic configuration and numerous electronic transitions between f levels are anticipated owing to complexed electronic energy levels.

electronic transitions between f levels are anticipated owing to complexed electronic energy levels.Although, only sharp lines have obtained as the transitions between these energy levels are highly selective in nature [35].Dy3+ doped nanophosphors principally comprise two intense bands, which are attributable to dopant centred intraconfigurational f-f transitions viz.4F9/2→6H15/2 (blueline) and 4F9/26H13/2 (yellowline).The emission intensity of 4F9/2→6H13/2 ( L=2, J=2 ) transition is highly sensitive to the crystal field and alters with the alteration of host lattice used.On the other hand, the transition 4F9/26H15/2 is not sensitive to the crystalline field and their intensity remains almost unaltered even on varying the host lattice.Doped samples are popularly known for their white emission which can be maintained only by regulating the intensities ratios of yellow to blue emission [36,37].Color perception of Dy3+ doped phosphors is very nearer to white light emission and thus can be widely applied as dopant ion in the architect and design of WLEDs.In the present paper, we have discussed the synthetic, structural and the optical characteristics of doped YAlO3: Dy3+ nanophosphors.The early investigations reveals that there are some reports on the synthetic aspects of Dy3+ doped YAlO3 nanocrystalline materials via conventional solid-state reaction method [34,38], Czochralski (CZ) method [39–41], citric acid combustion method [42], and oxalyl dihydrazide combustion method [43].To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first study to fabricate YAlO3: Dy3+ nanophosphors via a facile, economical and self-propagating method namely urea-assisted solution combustion, which facilitates the commercial production of such spectral materials.The SC method have numerous advantages over other synthetic method in perspective to controlled composition and high purity of prepared materials in short duration of time [44,45].

e to controlled composition and high purity of prepared materials in short duration of time [44,45].Our paper reports the methodical research for extensive inspection of intricate crystal framework, elemental probe, morphological studies, photometric features including luminescence-quenching pathway, decay-profile, quantum-efficiency, color-purity (CP), color-temperature (CCT) and systematic effect of Dy3+ doping on the crystallographic and photophysical properties of perovskite YAlO3: Dy3+ nanophosphors, which signifies the novelty of research work realized by the authors. 2.Experimental details It is well revealed that synthetic route plays a vital role in defining the morphology of prepared materials [46].Owed to cost effectiveness, ecological sustainability, and effortless synthetic approach, urea-assisted solution combustion (SC) synthetic method was used for the first time to prepare doped Y1-xAlO3: x Dy3+(abbreviated as YAP: x Dy3+; x=0.01-0.08 mol) nanophosphors.All ultrapure precursors materials were purchased from the Sigma-Aldrich.Metal nitrates viz.yttrium nitrate hexahydrate [ Y (NO3) 3.6H2O ], aluminium nitrate nonahydrate [Al(NO).9H O] were used as oxidising agents while urea (fuel) was cast-off as reducing agent.Moreover, dysprosium nitrate pentahydrate [Dy(NO).5H O] was used as dopant precursor material.The schematic diagram of synthetic process is illustrated in Fig.1.Initially, stoichiometric weighed raw materials were poured in minimum quantity of distilled water and then mixed thoroughly in order to get a homogeneous solution.Later on, mixture solution was heated in silica crucible to approximately 80C on hot plate until a paste-like material was formed.Now, the crucible was placed in a preheated muffle furnace (600C) and instantaneously combustion of the mixture would take place.

Structural, thermal, optical and luminescence properties of Dy3+ ions doped Zinc Potassium Alumino Borate glasses for optoelectronics applications Manjeet a, A.Kumar b, Anu d, Ravina b, Nisha Deopa b,*, Anand Kumar b, R.P.Chahal a, S.Dahiya c, R.Punia c, A.S.Rao 0 a Department of Physics, Chaudhary Bansi Lal University, Bhiwani, Haryana 127021, India b Department of Physics, Chaudhary Ranbir Singh University, Rohtak Bypass Road, Jind, Haryana 126102, India c Department of Physics, Maharshi Dayanand University, Rohtak, Haryana 124001, India d Department of Applied Physics, Delhi Technological University, Bawana Road, New Delhi 110042, India ARTICLEINFOKeywords: Glasses Luminescence Optical Optoelectronics Potassium ABSTRACTZinc Potassium Alumino Borate (ZnKAlB) glasses doped with dysprosium (Dy3+) ions of different concentrations were synthesized through the process of melt quenching which is commonly used in solid-state lighting (SSL) and laser systems, to comprehend their viability.This article evaluates and analyzes the physical, structural, thermal and optical properties of Dy3+ ions doped glasses by X-ray diffraction (XRD), Infrared Fourier Transform (FT-IR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), UV absorption and photoluminescence (PL) spectra to explain their utilization in optoelectronic devices such as lasers and white light-emitting diodes (w-LEDs).The physical parameters viz.density, refractive index, inter-ionic distance, molar volume, polaron radius, field strength, optical electronegativity, dielectric constant, reflection loss and metallization were computed by following the expressions reported in the literature.

content: ection loss and metallization were computed by following the expressions reported in the literature.Glasses are non-crystalline materials and the non-crystallinity of an un-doped Zinc Potassium Alumino Borate glass was proven by the absence of high-pitched peaks in the XRD spectra.FT-IR spectroscopy was used to identify the presence of different functional groups and their bond nature in Dy3+ ions doped ZnKAlB glasses.The transition temperature (Tg):, melting temperature (Tm) and thermal stability was calculated by monitoring DSC thermograms of all glasses.Further, the bonding parameters (δ) and nephelauxetic ratio (β) were estimated to explore the bonding nature of Dy3+ ions in its neighborhoods by using UV-absorption data.The optical direct-indirect band gap energy (Eopt) and Urbach’s energy (ΔE) were enumerated from the absorption spectrum to elaborate electrical properties of as-prepared glasses.Judd-Ofelt theory was employed to find oscillator strengths from absorption spectra and for further calculation of radiative parameters such as the radiative lifetimes (τR), radiative transition probability (AR), total radiative transition probability (AT) and branching ratio (R) to understand the quantum efficiency (η).Furthermore, the colorimetric parameters such as correlated color temperature (CCT), CIE coordinates and yellow to blue (Y/B) ratio were estimated from the PL emission data.The multipole-multipole interaction was confirmed by Dexter approximation to explain concentration quenching.This work primarily explains the essential features of borate glasses with Dy3+ ions doping to explain their potential use in tricolor w-LEDs and lasers 1.Introduction In the field of SSL, there have been various scientific innovations with an enormous implementation mainly in magneto-optical devices, liquid crystal displays (LCD), traffic signals, w-LEDs, lasers and many more [1–5].

optical devices, liquid crystal displays (LCD), traffic signals, w-LEDs, lasers and many more [1–5].In the last few years, the research area of oxide glasses has attracted significant interest from scientists and researchers because of their remarkable properties.Due to incredible developments in controllable solid-state lasers, many scholars and physicists have drawn their attention towards crystalline and amorphous materials with Rare Earth (RE) ions doping.SSL-based products have created an opportunity for the significant growth of w-LEDs, because of their long-life duration, smaller design, excellent economy and low power consumption.The w-LEDs are considerably superior to traditional light sources such as incandescent lamps, tubes and bulbs.The crystals are much complicated to grow, costly and almost very impractical to shape into waveguides compared to glasses, which are easy to prepare, low-priced and can easily shape for optical device applications because of the absence of the fundamental structure of crystals.Researchers have preciseness interest in elaborate glasses as they are optically transparent, mechanically strong, electrically resistive, thermally non-conductive and chemically inactive.Researchers are now undertaking different chemical compo sitions as glass hosts for RE doping to analyze their electric properties.It is well-known that the borate glasses are more important than other previous glasses due to their high thermal stability, high chemica stability, low melting point, high clarity and good solubility of RE ion [ 6, 7 ].The stunning features inhabited in RE ion-doped boric acid (B2O3) make it an excellent hosting framework for preparing luminescen products with better quantum efficiency.Borate glasses possess large phonon energy of the range 1300 cm - 1 due to stretching vibration of network bonding oxides, which strongly decreases the quantum effi ciency and increases non-radiative decay, so they cannot employ as good optoelectronic tools [8].

fi ciency and increases non-radiative decay, so they cannot employ as good optoelectronic tools [8].Consequently, by adding heavy metal oxide such high phonons energy possessed by borate glass can be diminished.These low phonon-energy glasses can minimize non-radiative relaxation and thus can increase quantum efficiency by increasing radiative emis sions.These glass materials with fewer phonon energies are more acceptable for various photonics applications.Further, Al2O3 is an electrical insulator but it has a surprisingly good thermal conductivity about of 30Wm - 1K - 1..Aluminum oxide is most commonly used in formulations of glass and is essential for the weathering resistance of metallic aluminum.The inclusion of aluminum trioxide (Al2O3) into the borate glass mold is most suitable for enhancing emission property, chemical and thermo-mechanical stability of RE doped borate glass and acting as a network modifier [9].The addition of Al2O3 in borate glasse enhances the stability of glass, minimizes crystallization effectively and modifies glass structure [10].Zinc oxide has many material science applications such as high thermal conductivity, high refractive index and UV protection.Thus, zinc oxide (ZnO) is added to products o glasses, ceramics, cement and lubricants.The addition of ZnO in glas makes them perceptibly covalent, sublime and thermally stable, which can minimize the time of solidification of glasses [11–13].The existence of ZnO in host glass has specific features due to its binate behavior as a network modifier as well as glass former [14,15].When the borate glasses are coupled with alkali/alkaline earth oxides, the formed glasse have certain physical traits and exhibit a wide variety of applications in optoelectronic devices.Thus, the addition of K2O has been expected to minimize the crystalline tendency of the glasses to enhance the me chanical stability and decrease the hygroscopic property of the borate glass network [16–18].

the me chanical stability and decrease the hygroscopic property of the borate glass network [16–18].In borate glasses, K2O is working as a network modifier implies that they are unable to create any structural units on their own but they affect the borate network by creating eithe non-bridging oxygen ions (NBOs) or tetrahedral BO4 units.The aforesaid scientific knowledge inspired us to prepare a noble glass host namely Zinc Potassium Alumino Borate glasses (ZnKAlB) glass.RE elements possess remarkable properties that differ from other optically active transition element ions.Generally, the RE ions can emit and absorb under selective wavelength ranges.The emission and absorption transitions of the RE elements are relatively insensitive to host material since they occur within the shell that is shielded with external shells.RE doped glasses are essentially identified by electronic transi tions like 4f-5d & 4f-4f and the luminescence efficiency can be examined from these transitions [19–24].To make optoelectronic devices from RE doped glasses a detailed study of their chemical, optical, structural and physical properties is required.Generally, the borate glasses doped with Dy3+ ions exhibited yellow and blue emissions for (4F9/26H13/2) and (4F9/26H15/2) transitions, corresponding to wavelength 575 and 481 nm, respectively [25].The Dy3+ ions emit white light when the ratio of these two emissions (yellowandblue) is proper.They show luminescence in yellow to orange bands and are commonly used in telecommunications and lasers.The w-LEDs are fabricated by merging blue or near-ultraviolet LED chips coated by single or multiple phosphors [26, 27].It has been found that in w-LEDs, the radiations were influenced by phosphors coupled with epoxy resin and also by concentration in phosphors-based w-LEDs.In addition, the luminescent performance directly linked to the sealant can be depreciated at high energy and high-temperature sources of excitation for pc-based w-LEDs [28–30].

rate glasses with Dy3+ ions doping as an optical probe to elaborate the luminescence nature of w-LED.They reported two emission transitions 4F9/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 under 387 nm excitation wavelength with their contribution for the white light emission with the help of the 1931CIE coordinates and mentioned their Y/B ratio.I.Khan and group [36] reported luminescence behavior of LiF – Na2O – K2O – B2O3 glasses with Dy3+ ions doping for white light production.They suggested that the NKLB-Dy glasses can be used for SSL applications.In this research work, Zinc Potassium Alumino Borate glasses (ZnKAlB) doped with Dy3+ ions of different concentrations have been synthesized through the melt quench method and then characterized to elaborate their usage in op toelectronic applications through a variety of spectroscopic techniques such as XRD, DSC, FT-IR, PL and UV absorption.The Eopt, bonding parameters (δ), J-O intensity parameters ( 2, 4, 6 ) were calculated from the UV absorption data to study the radiative properties of Dy3+ doped ZnKAlB glasses to explain their potential use in optoelectronic applications, w-LEDs and lasers.The physical, structural and optical traits of the glasses significantly affect the composition of dopant and synthesi conditions.The advancement in optical glasses with doping of RE ions has caused an evolution in electronic industries and opto-communication. 2.Experimental 2.1.Synthesis of glasses In the present research work, glass samples are prepared using the chemical composition: 65B2O3 - (10-x) Al2O3-10Zn O-15K2O - x Dy2O3, where the values of x are varying as 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 (in mol%), through the melt quench technique.

td>350.26980.2490>10,000 4.Conclusions SrLa1-xDyxAlO4 ( x=0, 1, 3 and 5 mol%) phosphors have been successfully synthesized via conventional solid-state technique and their structural, morphological, metallic bonds and luminescent characteristics were investigated.XRD studies disclosed the singlephase tetragonal crystal structure of synthesized all the phosphor samples.The SEM and EDS analysis confirmed that the particles possessing some agglomerated spherical like morphology and precursor elements exist in all the samples.From the FTIR and Raman spectra it is identified that the powders having metallic bonds and tetragonal crystal nature.The characteristic keen excitation peaks in excitation-spectra were ascribed to intra-4f transitions of the Dy3+-ions in 325-425 nm range were detected in these phosphors, a peak at 353 nm assigned to 6H15/24F7/2 transition being the most prominent.The emission-spectra of SrL a1-x DyxAl04 phosphors exhibit both blue and yellow emission corresponding to 4F9/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 transitions of Dy3+- i0 ns, respectively.The relative emission intensity of hypersensitive electric forced transition (4F9/26H13/2) is found to be stronger than the magnetic dipole transition (4F9/26H15/2) in each of the prepared phosphors.The decay lifetime times are calculated and were detected to be decreased with the increasing of Dy3+ ion concentration.The CIE-coordinate values were shifted towards white lightemission with the increase of Dy3+ ion concentration.Hence, all these results strongly suggest that the Dy3+ doped SrLaAlO4 phosphors are potentially suitable candidate for white light emission. Abstract: Whitlockite has the advantages of a low sintering temperature, high stability, and a low fabrication cost, and it is widely used as the host for luminescent material.In this study, Ca1.8Li0.6La0.6-x (PO4) 2: x Dy3+ phosphor was prepared by the high-temperature solid-state method, and its structure, composition, and luminescence properties were systematically studied.The results showed that a new whitlockite type matrix was prepared by replacing Ca2+ in whitlockite with monovalent and trivalent cations.The prepared phosphors belonged to a hexagonal crystal system with a particle size in the range of 5–20 μm.Under the excitation of 350 nm UV light, the samples emitted white light, and there were mainly two stronger emission peaks at 481 nm in the blue band and 573 nm in the yellow band, which correspond to the electron transitions at 4F9/26H15/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 of Dy3+, respectively.The optimal doping concentration of Dy3+ in Ca1.8Li0.6La0.

/2 and 4F9/26H13/2 of Dy3+, respectively.The optimal doping concentration of Dy3+ in Ca1.8Li0.6La0.6 (PO4) 2 matrix was 0.03 (mol%).The main mechanism of concentration quenching in the sample was dipole–dipole energy transfer.When the temperature was 130C, the luminescence intensity of the samples was 78.7% of that at 30C, and their thermal quenching activation energy was 0.25 eV.The CIE coordinates of the sample at 30 ◦C were (0.2750, 0.3006), and their luminescent colors do not change with temperature.All the results indicate that Ca1.8Li0.6La0.6-x (PO4) 2: x Dy3+ phosphor is a luminescent material with good luminescence performance and thermal stability, which shows a promising application in the field of LED display. y highly sophisticated industries to day, and they have their own unique advantages in many aspects.There has been extensive research on rare earths in permanent magnetic materials [1], luminescent materials [2,3], catalytic materials [4–6], and hydrogen storage materials [7].With the development of science and technology, rare-earth luminescent materials often appear in the research of luminescent materials for third-generation lamps.Rare-earth luminescent materials have a high luminescence efficiency, a strong emission ability in the visible region, resistance to ultraviolet radiation, good thermal stability, and can adapt to the requirements of high-load fluorescent lamps.Therefore, rare-earth luminescent materials are widely used in fluorescent lamps, white diode fluorescents, display imaging, X-ray enhancement screens, and other fields.Host and activator make up the majority of rare-earth luminous materials.As a host, the most basic needs are stability and ease of preparation.Whitlockite ( - Ca3 (PO4) 2 ) has the advantages of a low sintering temperature, a low manufacturing cost, and strong physical and chemical stability [8,9].On the other hand, there are five non-equivalent cation lattice sites that exist for rare-earth ions in the whitlockite structure.Therefore, whitlockite is an outstanding host.Isomorphism can open up new possibilities for luminous materials and is crucial for the discovery of new luminescent materials.Lithium is an alkaline earth metal with a solubilization function that can boost the luminescence of rare-earth ions significantly.La3+ is commonly employed in the fabrication of luminous matrix materials doped with rare-earth ions because it has a stable structure with nearly negligible light absorption and emission.As a result, Li+ and La3+ have frequently been utilized to micro-modify the structure of the luminous matrix, such as Li7La3Zr2O12: x Tb [10], Li7La3-xZr2O12: x Eu3+[ 11 ] Li5La3Nb2O12 [12], and La2LiMO6; Eu3+[ 13 ].

r2O12: x Tb [10], Li7La3-xZr2O12: x Eu3+[ 11 ] Li5La3Nb2O12 [12], and La2LiMO6; Eu3+[ 13 ].Scholars at home and abroad have been paying close attention to the design and development of luminous materials using whitlockite materials as matrices in recent years [2,14,15].The introduction of Li+ and La3+ in whitlockite structure may bring some new opportunities to generate novel excellent whitlockite host for luminescent materials.In conclusion, luminous materials with the matrix Ca1.8Li0.6La0.6 (PO4) 2 were created in this article.Activators in luminous materials activate the host by forming luminescent centers.To generate prepared luminous materials with good luminescent characteristics, rare-earth ions are frequently doped in the host as activators.Dy3+ is a rare-earth ion that is commonly employed to make luminous materials [ 16-19 ]. 4F9/26H13/2 transitions are found in the yellow zone of Dy3+ ions, while 4F9/26H15/2 transitions are found in the blue region.When the Dy3+ ion is at the center of symmetry, multilevel interactions are the main cause of luminescence, and the luminescent material emits standard white light when the transitions intensity is comparable in both places [20,21].Currently, most commercial white LEDs are manufactured by using blue diode chips to excite the yellow phosphor 3Al5O12: Ce3+ [ 22 ].Due to the absence of the red spectral component, white light from this combination exhibits poor color rendering index and high color temperature, and the white light emitted is unstable.Single-component white phosphor has better color stability, it produces less energy loss during energy transfer, and the pure white color is also more favorable for phosphor color improvement.There fore, the development of new single-component white phosphor has obvious practical application value.In this study, single-component phosphors, Ca1.8Li0.6La0.6-x (PO4) 2...Dy3+, were prepared by the high-temperature solid state method.

Full length article Synthesis and characterization of a new double perovskite phosphor: NaCaTiTa ( O6: Dy3+ with high thermal stability for w-LEDs application Jiang Guo a,1, Sichun Lia,1, Jiayun Kong a, Yuxin Lia, LiZhou a, Liyang Lou a, Qiuyi Lva, Rong Tang a, Lingling Zheng d, Bin Deng b,c,*, Ruijin Yua,* a College of Chemistry & Pharmacy, Northwest A&FUniversity, Yangling, Shaanxi 712100, PRChina b School of Chemistry and Environmental Science, Xiangnan University, Chenzhou, Hunan 423043, PRChina c Hunan Provincial Key Laboratory of Xiangnan Rare-Precious Metals Compounds Research and Application, Xiangnan University, Chenzhou, Hunan 423043, PRChina d Guangzhou Vocational College of Technology & Business, Guangzhou, Guangdong 511442, PRChina ARTICLEINFOKeywords: NaCaTiTaO6:Dy3+ Double perovskite Thermal stability LEDsABSTRACTA new yellow-emitting phosphor, NaCaTiTaO6: Dy3+, was synthesized via solid-phase synthesis at 1300 °C.X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis and Rietveld refinement showed that the prepared phosphors exhibited a stable double perovskite structure.The particle size of the phosphor was around 3.8 μm.The maximum emission peak at 574 nm is attributed to the 4F9/26H13/2 energy level transition under irradiation at 389 nm.The optimum Dy3+ doping concentration is 0.10M equivalent, and concentration quenching is due to the nearest neighbor ion interaction.The luminescence intensity of the phosphor was reduced by only 15% at 420K, exhibiting high thermal stability.Quantum yield (QY) was measured to be 26.31%.

ed by only 15% at 420K, exhibiting high thermal stability.Quantum yield (QY) was measured to be 26.31%.Finally, the Commission International de I’Eclairage (CIE) color coordinate of the phosphor for white light emitting diode (w-LED) was (0.314, 0.323), with a color rendering index (Ra) of 92 and a correlated color temperature (CCT) of 5578K.Above all, the Dy3+.doped double perovskite NaCaTiTaO:Dy3+ phosphor is expected to be used in w-LEDs. 1.Introduction The use of green and environmental-friendly light energy has always been a top priority.As the fourth-generation lighting source, LED lights are highly attuned to human needs and have been widely used commercially.Because of their superior characteristics, involving high energy conversion efficiency, long lifespan, ease of mass production, and consistent with sustainable development principles, w-LEDs have aroused great interest [1–5].Today, commercial w-LEDs are primarily coated with Y3Al5O12: Ce3+( YAG: Ce3+) phosphors [6–8].However, the absence of the red-light component in the spectrum of the prepared products leads to obvious drawbacks, involving high CCT and low Ra, which limits the application of w-LEDs.Another improved strategy is to add a small amount of red phosphor into the yellow phosphor, while realizing the warm white light [9–11].Rare earth Dy3+ ion is an effective activator that can produce three classic emission peaks at 482 (blue), 577 (yellow), and 666 (red) nm corresponding to the 4F9/26H J / 2 transition (J=15, 13, and 11) when exposed to n-UV [12–14].It has been reported that the coordination environment has a large effect on the yellow emission of Dy3+ and a small effect on the blue luminescence [15–18].Therefore, different matrix materials doped with Dy3+ can be coated onto the n-UV chip to obtain white light.Some Dy3+-doped phosphors have been used in w-LEDs applications successfully, such as SrLaAlO4:Dy3+, LiY9(SiO4)6O2: Dy3+, and (Ca1-xMOx) TiO3: Dy3+( M=Mg2+/ Zn2+) [19–21].

(d).Eu3+, and Mg2InSbO6: Sm3+ phosphors exhibit excellent luminescence thermal stability [27–29].Recently, many Dy3+ doped double perovskite phosphors, involving Ca2LuTaO6: Dy3+/ Eu3+ [ 14 ], Li2MgZrO4: Dy3+[30], and Ba2 (1-x) ( Na, RE ) x ZnWO6 ( RE=Ce3+, Eu3+, and Dy3+) [ 31 ], have been used for w-LED packaging.In2008, Rajendran et al.demonstrated that NaXTiYO6 ( X=CaorSr; Y=Nb or Ta) has an orthorhombic perovskite-type structure (Space group, Pnma ) by XRD analysis [32,33].For the past few years, NaCaTiTaO6 has been an excellent matrix material for solid-state lighting applications, particularly when s m3+ and Eu3+ are used as doping ions [34–36].However, Dy3+-doped NaCaTiTaO6 have not been reported.In this research, a series of yellow phosphors NaCaTiTaO6: x Dy3+( x=0.005 – 0.20 mol) was obtained by the conventional high temperature solid-phase method.Its structural characteristics, luminescent proper ties, decay time, thermal stability, and CIE coordinates were systematically characterized.The w-LEDs were also prepared by combining the prepared phosphor with n-UV (390nm) chips. 2.Experimental procedures 2.1.Reagents and operating procedures A serry of phosphors, NaCaTiTaO6: x Dy3+( x=0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 mol), were prepared by traditional high temperature solid-phase synthesis.The raw materials, a2C O3 ( A.R.), CaCO3 ( A.R.), TiO2 ( A.R., nanoscale), Ta2O5 ( A.R.), and Dy2O3 ( A.R.) were purchased from Shanghai Aladdin Bio-Chem Technology Co., LTD.In addition, the commercial phosphors used in this work were purchased from Jiangmen Kanhoo Industry Co.,Ltd.After weighing by analytical balance, the mixed raw materials with stoichiometric ratio were transferred to agate mortar and ground for 15 min.Then, the ground mixture was transferred into an alumina crucible and placed in an electric furnace to calcinate in air atmosphere for 5 h at 1300C..

section: Synthesis and characterization of wide band excited yellow phosphor La Nb2V O9 : Dy3+and application in potential fingerprint and lip print detection ![image](https://cdn-mineru.openxlab.org.cn/result/2026-08-11/22607e5f-5145-4547-87d5-d6ada558c0b0/1f6100e6a970e105648856013ead1656dc23efd2e7bc87be781efba88f11d409.jpg) Sichun Li <sup>a,1</sup>, Jiang Guo <sup>a,1</sup>, Wen Shi <sup>a</sup>, Xiaopeng Hu <sup>c</sup>, Shanshan Chen <sup>a</sup>, Junmeng Luo Yuxin Li <sup>a</sup>, Jiayun Kong <sup>a</sup>, Junzhi Che <sup>a</sup>, Haiqiang Wang <sup>a</sup>, Bin Deng <sup>b,e,**</sup>, Ruijin Yu <sup>a</sup> <sup>a</sup> College of Chemistry & Pharmacy, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, Shaanxi, 712100, PR China <sup>b</sup> School of Chemistry and Environmental Science, Xiangnan University, Chenzhou, Hunan, 423043, PR China <sup>c</sup> College of Science, Central South University of Forestry and Technology, Changsha, 410004, PR China <sup>d</sup> College of Materials and Chemical Engineering, Key Laboratory of Inorganic Nonmetallic Crystalline and Energy Conversion Materials, China Three Gorges University, Yichang, Hubei, 443002, PR China <sup>e</sup> Hunan Provincial Key Laboratory of Xiangnan Rare-Precious Metals Compounds Research and Application, Chenzhou, Hunan, 423043, PR China ## A R T I C L E I N F O Keywords: Phosphors LaNb VO :Dy<sup>3+</sup> Latent fingerprints Lip print detection ## A B S T R A C T LaNb<sub>2</sub>VO<sub>9</sub>:Dy<sup>3+</sup> yellow phosphors were synthesized by high-temperature solid-state method.The luminescent properties, structure, and color purity of the products were studied systematically.LaNb VO :Dy<sup>3+</sup> phosphors can be effectively excited by two broad charge transfer bands (CTB) under307 nm excitation.The strong yellow light at570 nm was caused by the4F9/26H13/2 energy level transition of Dy3+.

content: ation.The strong yellow light at 570 nm was caused by the 4F9/26H13/2 energy level transition of Dy3+.The optimum doping concentration of LaNb2VO9:xDy3+ phosphor was x=0.10 mol, and the dominant factor of concentration quenching effect is the nearest-neighbor ions interaction.The chromaticity coordinates of International Committee LaNb2VO9:Dy3+ were located in the yellow color area.In addition, LaNb2VO9:0.1Dy3+ phosphor can well visualize the latent fingerprint (LFP) image and lip print image.The levels 1–3 features of fingerprint and groove pattern of lip print can be easily recognized, with high resolution and contrast.The experimental results showed LaNbVO:Dy3+ can be well applied to LFP and lip print detection. 1.Introduction Fingerprint and lip print play an essential role in criminal science because of their uniqueness and lifetime of persons [1,2].There are three levels of fingerprint characteristics.The level 1 is the typical features of fingerprints (suchasringsandeddies), level 2 is the macro details of the fingerprint (eye, lake, island, ridge fragments, and endpoint), and level 3 is the microscopic details of the fingerprint (suchaspores) [3,4].The fingerprint features can be used to identify the raised lines on the finger, which are covered with grease and sweat [5].The latent fingerprint (LFP) can assist police with identifying personal information and crime scenes.In addition, lip print recognition is a relatively attractive emerging field for personal identification.Lip marks are the normal wrinkles and grooves between the mucous membrane of the lip and the outer skin in the transitional area of the human lip [6–8].The groove pattern of lip prints is rarely changed and can resist various physical factors, including pressure, physical injury, and exposure to hot and cold stimuli.The stability of lip prints makes it a reliable and efficient tool for forensic field investigation [9–11].

bility of lip prints makes it a reliable and efficient tool for forensic field investigation [9–11].For fingerprints, the traditional powder dust method has low sensitivity, low resolution, and considerable background interference [12].For lip lines, smoking, vacuum coating, and other methods have the very low visibility and the complex operation [13].Recently, rare-earth-doped luminescent materials are widely used in luminescence and have a surprising effect in finding potential fingerprints and lip lines at crime scenes, for examples, LaOF:Sm3+ [14], CaAlO:Eu2+, Dy3+[15], MoO3: Dy3+[16], and CaAl2O4; Tb3+, Ce3+, M+ ( M+=K,.Na, Li) [17].The luminescent materials based on vanadate have the advantages of low synthesis temperature and stable chemical properties [18–21].Moreover, vanadate group can effectively transfer the absorbed energy to the activated ions, and present high luminous efficiency [22–24].Up conversion nanoparticles (UCNPs), especially lanthanide doped rare earth nano ions, are hardly disturbed by background fluorescence for potential fingerprint and lip image, and have good optical contrast and high detection sensitivity [ 25, 26 ].However, the optical properties of Dy3+-doped LaNb2VO9 phosphors under UV light have not been reported [ 27-29 ] In this work, X-ray diffraction (XRD) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) were used for studying the phase purity and surface morphology.In addition, the optical properties of LaNb2VO9xDy3+(x=0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, and 0.35) were investigated by photoluminescence (PL), and PL excitation (PLE) spectra, the optical correlated color temperature (CCT), and Commission International de I ‘Eclairage (CIE).Finally, Dy3+-doped LaNb2VO9 phosphors were used for LFP and lip development for the first time. 2.Experimental details 2.1.Samples preparation Dy3+-activated La1-xDyxNb2VO9 ( x=0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10.2, 0.3, and 0.35) phosphors were synthesized by high temperature solid-phase method.

05, 0.10.2, 0.3, and 0.35) phosphors were synthesized by high temperature solid-phase method.The corresponding reagents, when x=0.02, 0.0015 g Dy2O3 ( 99.99 % ), 0.255 g La2O3 (analytical reagent, abbrevi ated as A.R.), 0.418 g NbO (A.R.), and 0.184 g NH4VO3 ( A.R.) were weighted on the basis of the specific stoichiometric, fully mixed, transferred into agate mortar, and ground thoroughly.The mixture is heated in 1000C for 5 h and cooled to room temperature to obtain the final phosphors.The relevant reaction equation is as follows: l0.5 (1-x) La2O3+Nb2O5+NH4VO3+ 0.5 x Dy2O3 & 1000C, 5 h La1-xDyxNb2VO9 & + volatile produces 2.2.Measurements The phase formation of LaNb2VO9: x Dy3+( x=0-0.35 ) was analyzed by X-ray diffractometer (XRD) (BrukerD2PHASER) with CuKα radiation (=1.5405, 20 < 2 < 60 )..A scanning electron microscopy (SEM, Nova Nano SEM-450) was adopted to collect the morphology and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) of samples with the elemental mappings.The size distribution of phosphors was measured by laser particle size analyzer Malvern MS2000 and analyzed by the machine’s own software Mastersizer 2000.PLE and PL were measured on a fluo rescence spectrometer (EdinburghFLS980). 2.3.Visualization of LFPFig.1 shows a schematic diagram of the steps for LFP and lip print detection.A21-year-old female volunteer provided the fingerprint and lip print sample.She gently rubbed a clean finger against the forehead (thegreaseisattached) and pressed it against the foil substrate to form LFP.Then gently touched the lips with the foil substrate to form the lip print.La Nb2VO9: 0.10Dy3+ phosphor was lightly swept on the LFP and lip print with a brush.Fingerprint and lip print pictures were preserved with a digital camera (CanonEOS700D) under ultraviolet light at 275 nm. 3.Results and discussion The XRD is used to examine the structure and crystal phase purity of the La1-xDyxNb2VO9 phosphors ( x=0.001 – 0.35 ), which are presented in Fig.2.

purity of the La1-xDyxNb2VO9 phosphors ( x=0.001 – 0.35 ), which are presented in Fig.2.All the diffraction peaks were indexed to the standard card (PDF42–0107) of the LaNb2VO9 [30], meaning that the Dy3+ doping does not significantly cause any impurity or induce major changes in the crystal structure.The XRD peak at 23 was attributed to an unknown impurity.The SEM image of LaNb2VO9:0.10Dy3+ phosphor is shown in Fig.3 (a).The particle size distribution is relatively uniform, but agglomeration particles also appear in a few samples due to high tem perature treatment.Fig.3 (b) shows the particle size distribution, which is about 4.65 μm.The particle size and configuration of the surface of phosphor are related to the luminescence property of phosphor and the adhesion degree of phosphor to fingerprint and lip grain residue.The smaller the particle size of phosphor is, the higher the degree of adhesion to fingerprints and lip lines is.Thus, the particle size of phosphor is significant for the image definition of fingerprint and lip lines.After grinding these phosphors, they will be easily combined with the substrate and applied to the LFP [14].So La1-xDyxNb2VO9 phosphors conform to the application requirements of fingerprint and lip lines (see Fig, 4 ) Fig.2.XRD patterns of La1-xDyxNb2VO9 phosphors ( x=0.001 – 0.35 ) Apply the phosphor with a brush Fig.1.Schematic of LFP and lip print detection step.

part of a forced electric dipole transition, which is susceptible to the crystal field environment.When Dy3+ was in a highly symmetrical position, the blue emission was dominant; by comparison, the yellow emission was dominant [34].The intensity of blue radiation is lower than that of yellow, indicating that Dy3+ occupied high asymmetry in LaNb2VO9.Fig.7(b) shows the corresponding energy level transitions obtained from the emission spectrum.In addition, the energy absorption and transfer process of LaNbVO: Dy3+ can be further described.A series of energy level transitions occur in the ultraviolet excitation at 265 nm, 300 nm, and 307 nm.As shown in Fig.7(b), electrons were excited from the valence band (VB) to the conduction band (CB) of the matrix under 307 nm excitation.This en ergy could be transferred non-radiatively (NR) from VO43- to the 4f excited level of Dy3+ and was enough to excite the electrons of Dy3+These electrons decayed non-radiatively to 4F9/2 and relaxed in the form of luminescence to 6H13/2 and 6H15/2 states.Fig.8 (a) shows the concentration influences to the PL intensities of La1-xDyxNb2VO9 phosphors ( x=0.005 – 0.35 ) under 307 nm excitation.The emission spectra of different concentrations of Dy3+ consist of several emission bands with similar profiles, which indicates that Dy3+ doping into La1-xDyxNb2VO9 matrix has little effect on the peak position.The strongest emission band at 570 nm corresponds to the 4F9/26H13 / transition of Dy3+.It can be seen from the inset in Fig.8 (a) that the luminous intensity of the prepared samples increases with the increase of the doping concentration.When the doping concentration exceeds 0.10 mol, the luminous intensity begins to weaken, which indicates the existence of concentration quenching phenomenon. Synthesis and luminescence characteristics of Na6Ca (1-X) P2O9: XDy3+ phosphor for outdoor lighting applications T.Krishnapriya, Remya Mohan P, Adon Jose, Jeena Rose Jose, Cyriac Joseph, P.R.Biju School of Pure &Applied Physics, Mahatma Gandhi University, Kottayam, Kerala, 86560, India HIGHLIGHTS • Highlights (forreview).• A new and efficient Dy3+ doped Na6CaP2O9 phosphor was synthesized by solid state reaction method.• The luminescent spectra reveal that the samples can be well excited under near UV light to get an efficient white emission.• The energy transfer interaction between Dy3+ ions was dipole-dipole in nature, as evident from the Dexter theory.• The chromaticity color coordinates of all the samples fall in the vicinity of white region.st. ARTICLEINFOKeywords: Phosphor Luminescence Solid state reaction method LEDsWhite light emission ABSTRACTLight emitting devices, especially outdoor lighting light emitting diodes (LEDs) that do not disrupt the natural plant habitat is an interesting field.In this regard, a series of r Na6Ca (1-X) P2O9XDy3+( X=0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08, 0.10) phosphors were synthesized by solid state reaction method.Structural details of the phosphors were analyzed by the X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis.Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) analysis proves that the samples are having a one-dimensional needle like morphology which is advantageous for its use in miniaturized devices like LEDs and solar cells.The luminescent properties of Na6CaP2O9: Dy3+ phosphors were investigated via UV–Visible–NIR absorption, photoluminescence excitation and emission spectra and life time analyses.
section: Synthesis and luminescence characteristics of Na6Ca ( 1 - X ) P2O9 : X Dy3+phosphor for outdoor lighting applications ![image](https://cdn-mineru.openxlab.org.cn/result/2026-08-11/312cf3e8-3200-4526-8d5c-c0251028cb90/b6474ee716772ee2c42139db468bdb6f1d58628420efcf79144befa3b878e001.jpg) T.Krishnapriya , Remya Mohan P , Adon Jose , Jeena Rose Jose , Cyriac Joseph , P.R.Biju School of Pure &Applied Physics, Mahatma Gandhi University, Kottayam, Kerala, 86560, India ## H I G H L I G H T S • Highlights (for review).• A new and efficient Dy3+doped Na6Ca P2O9 phosphor was synthesized by solid state reaction method.• The luminescent spectra reveal that the samples can be well excited under near UV light to get an efficient white emission.• The energy transfer interaction between Dy3+ions was dipole-dipole in nature, as evident from the Dexter theory.• The chromaticity color coordinates of all the samples fall in the vicinity of white region.st.## A R T I C L E I N F O Keywords: Phosphor Luminescence Solid state reaction method LEDs White light emission ## A B S T R A C T Light emitting devices, especially outdoor lighting light emitting diodes (LEDs) that do not disrupt the natural plant habitat is an interesting field.In this regard, a series of r Na6Ca ( 1 - X ) P2O9X Dy3+( X = 0 .02 , 0 .04 , 0 .06 , 0 .08 , 0.10) phosphors were synthesized by solid state reaction method.Structural details of the phosphors were analyzed by the X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis.Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) analysis proves that the samples are having a one-dimensional needle like morphology which is advantageous for its use in miniaturized devices like LEDs and solar cells.The luminescent properties of Na6Ca P2O9 : Dy3+phosphors were investigated via UV–Visible–NIR absorption, photoluminescence excitation and emission spectra and life time analyses.

content: UV–Visible–NIR absorption, photoluminescence excitation and emission spectra and life time analyses.The samples can be well excited by near ultraviolet LED (NUV-LED) chips and exhibit bright, narrow yellow (574nm) and blue (480nm) emission respectively corresponding to the 4F9/26H13/2 and 4F9/2→6H15 / transitions of Dy3+ ions under 350 nm excitation.Since the value of Y/B ratio for the samples being close to unity, they can be a promising candidate for phosphor converted- WLEDs.The temperature dependent PL spectra reveal the thermal stability of the prepared material to be very promising.The average life time values for the optimum concentration sample is 0.0262 ms and is in the submillisecond range indicating their high speed switching response when used in LEDs.The lack of any red-near –IR emission along with the cool appearance of this phosphor proves it as an excellent candidate for outdoor lighting applications. 1.Introduction Asa part of reducing the global carbon footprint, it becomes essential to lower the electricity consumption since its cost may not only be counted in terms of money value but also on grounds of environment cost of carbon emission associated with electricity generation.The developments in the field of artificial illumination were dramatic starting from oil lanterns, incandescent and fluorescent lamps to the present age solid state lighting devices.Solid state lighting has given new colors and dimensions to lighting and helps to explore various regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.White light sources are probably the most widely used means for household and street lighting.So, attempts have been made to improve the quality of white-light emission and also the energy and cost efficiency.Recently phosphor converted white light emitting diodes (pc-WLEDs) have undertaken the lead role as white light sources replacing the conventional filament lamps and fluorescent lamps [1,2].

d role as white light sources replacing the conventional filament lamps and fluorescent lamps [1,2].A combination of blue InGaN light emitting diode (LED) along with yellow-emitting phosphor ( Y3Al5O12: Ce3+), and red-emitting nitride phosphor was one of the common strategies to realize white light emitting diodes (WLEDs).However, this approach of merging blue LED with two types of phosphors can lead to waste of materials and lowering of quantum efficiencies due to intense reabsorption of blue light by red phosphors.But these limitations may easily be resolved with the use of single phased phosphors having tunable emission color, excellent luminous output, better thermal and chemical stability etc [3].By using this strategy, some novel phosphors such as ( Sr, Ba ) 2Al3O6F: Eu2+[4], Ca8-2x-yCexNaxEuyMg3Al2Si7O28 [ 5 ], Ca5 (BO3) 3F; 0.15Bi3+, y Eu3+[ 6, 6, 7 ], 6] etc have been designed.In most of these phosphors, white light emission is achieved via an energy transfer mechanism from sensitizer to activator or with the addition of suitable red emitting phosphor.However, the thing is that, in these co-doped systems, this energy transfer consumes energy from sensitizer and may lead to lowering of luminescence intensity and use of red phosphor may leads to strong energy reabsorption.s0, single phase white light emitting phosphors based on the mechanism of single doping are widely investigated today [3,7].Also, even if these ordinary WLEDs when used in indoor and outdoor lighting satisfy the human color perception, it has been reported that the extensive use of the above-mentioned sources can collapse the natural habitats of indigenous plants [8].Usually, plants adjust their flowering time depending on the photoperiod at a particular time of the year at a geographical area with the help of certain genes that control the circadian clocks.

are subjected to ordinary white light from WLEDs, it hampers the flowering and fruiting of short-day plants while boosting the same of long day plants [9].The results are the obvious imbalance in the natural vegetations of an area.With this apprehension in mind, active investigations are on in the science fraternity in developing plant habitat conscious white LEDs (PHC-WLEDs) having their emission spectrum designed so as to contain the night time photosynthesis, thus preserving the endemic species of a geographical area.It is in this regard, pc-WLEDs made of Dy3+ doped phosphors have gained attention and were proved to be an excellent choice to reduce the night time photosynthesis owing to their very feeble red-near –infra red emissions [9].Dy3+ doped luminescent materials are generally a type of full-color emission phosphors that may be excited by ultraviolet (UV) or nearultraviolet (NUVLEDs) [10].Dy3+ plays a crucial role in designing near white light emitting luminescent materials and is very popular owing to its copious energy levels, color purity, high conversion efficiency etc.In general, Dy3+ shows three major visible emission bands including blue emission at 470 nm–500 nm (4F9/26H15/2), yellow at 570 nm–600 nm (4F9/26H13/2) and a feeble red emission at 650 nm–680 nm (4F9/26H11/2) which are necessary for the development of white light emission [11,12].It is known that the relative intensity of blue (4F9/26H15/2) and yellow (4F9/26H13/2) transition can be significantly influenced by the microscopic environment, for the blue emission being highly influenced by the chemical environment around Dy3+ ions [13,14].Thus, in many cases it may be possible to tailor the color properties of the emitted light through selection of suitable host lattice or changing the doping concentrations.
